== Origins and the Varangian Arrival ==

Kievan Rus' (or the Principality of Kiev) was the first organized state to form in the region, and the Varangians founded Kievan Rus and united the areas where Eastern Slavs lived into a single state.
Kiev Rus was founded by an elite Varangian army.
The history of Russia began with the leadership of Rurik, whose ancestors were legendary Varangian princes.
Rurik initiated the migration of the Varangian people, and the Varangians moved from Scandinavia to Novgorod by crossing the Baltic Sea during this migration.
The Varangians settled in Novgorod in 862 AD.
The history of Russia began with the migration of Scandinavian peoples, and Rurik crossed the Baltic Sea.
The Varangians were led by a semi-legendary figure named Rurik, and in 862 AD, Rurik entered the city of Novgorod.
A group originating from Scandinavia emerged in the mid-9th century, and the Varangians assumed the role of the dominant elite in Novgorod.
The Varangians migrated to Northeast Rus in the 9th century, and the Varangians are suspected to be Normans.
The Varangians engaged in trade and engaged in raiding.

The Varangians eventually settled in the region.
Vikings made the greatest contribution to the formation of this country.
Vikings were invited to rule the Slavic tribes.
Three brothers led the Vikings.
The three brothers were Rurik, Sineus, and Truvor.

== Founding of Novgorod and Early Expansion ==

Kievan Rus' formed a poorly structured state whose subjects were Eastern Slavic tribes living in the region that were gradually conquered.
Varangian princes developed a trade route using the Dnieper River known as the Route of the Varangians.
These princes imposed themselves on the Byzantine Empire using military force to achieve this dominance and became commercial partners of the Byzantine Empire.
Novgorod is located in northern modern-day Russia and was a Slavic capital.
Rurik was the first recorded Varangian ruler who strengthened his power in Novgorod and expanded his territory to the south.
Rurik attempted to conquer Kiev, which was inhabited by East Slavs and was a developed city.
The term Rhos or Rus began to refer to Varangians and also came to refer to Slavs who inhabited the region.
Novgorod developed as a trade hub with the Byzantine Empire.

The Primary Chronicle was written in later generations.
The Varangians moved their base to the Dnieper region in the late 9th century, during which period northeastern Rus became a border region.
Rurik established the Rurikid dynasty, and after his death, power passed to Oleg.

== Consolidation of Kiev and Military Campaigns ==

The Principality of Kiev had to fight nomadic peoples that came from the steppes and from the east, some of whom were the Pechenegs.
In 882, Oleg defeated local feudal lords in Kiev, and between 883 and 885, he subdued the Radimich tribes.
In 907, Oleg campaigned in Byzantium.
After Oleg's death, Igor became the ruler of the state in 912, and the feudal state of Kyivan Rus was strengthening.
Igor also conducted active foreign policy.
The rulers of Kievan Rus waged wars against the Pechenegs, and Sviatoslav, the Great Prince of Kievan Rus, died in one of these battles.
A struggle for succession erupted among Sviatoslav's sons after his death.

== Adoption of Orthodox Christianity ==

Orthodox Christianity became the state religion and was a factor in Russian national unity.
The adoption of Orthodoxy as the state religion was decisive for the later history of the Eastern Slavs.
The adoption resulted in a strong connection between church and state.
The adoption resulted in isolation from the Catholic remainder of Europe and from the Protestant remainder of Europe.
This adoption marked the beginning of Byzantine and Slavic culture.
Vladimir I expanded his territory in 989 to the Caucasus region and the Black Sea.
Vladimir I adopted the teachings of the Greek Orthodox Church.
In the 9th century, the Eastern Orthodox Church emerged from the Great Schism between the Eastern and Western Churches.

== Political Structure and Social Hierarchy ==

The medieval state of Kievan Rus was ruled by an elite of Varangian warriors and their descendants.
The integration of Eastern Roman and Slavic cultures began in the following millennium.
The Kievan Rus' state was Slavicized, including its Varangian ruling class.
Feudalism was already firmly established in Russia.
Princes directed these principalities, had eminent ownership of the land, employed armies, and ruled over a large population of peasants.
These armies were led by boyars.
Boyars gradually became landowners.
These peasants were generally free at that time.

== External Threats and Population Movements ==

Turkish populations, including the Kipchaks and the Pechenegs, frequently raided during the 11th and 12th centuries.
These raids caused southern Slavic populations to migrate northward to the regions known as Zales.

== Fragmentation and Legacy ==

Internal instability was caused by succession divisions among Vladimir's descendants, leading Kievan Rus' to give way to approximately fifteen principalities located on the territories of modern-day Ukraine, Belarus, and western Russia.
The death of Vladimir II Monomach's son in 1132 aggravated the decline and fragmentation, after which the states of Novgorod and Vladimir-Suzdal emerged as heirs of Kievan Rus in the northern territories.
The region of Rus was characterized by the proliferation of small states, and different ethnic consciousness developed early on between people of Ukraine and Belarus and people of Russia.
According to old Russian chronicles, the first rulers of Kievan Rus were legendary Kyi, Shchek, and Khoryv around 852, and the territory expanded during the reign of Vladimir.
Kiev Rus was led by the descendants of the Varangians, including Oleg who was the son of Rurik, and the empire established in Kiev is considered the ancestor of modern Russians.
Kievan Rus' developed a unique culture and was known as Kievan Russia in our region, while Kiev is now the capital of Ukraine.

== Origins and Formation ==

These Slavic tribes came from the forested mountain region of the Pinsk Marshes and migrated across the Baltic Sea to the current territory of Russia.[2414,2415][669,671] Since the 7th century, northern Russian lands have been controlled by Eastern Slavs.[2414,2415] The Turkification of East Slavs occurred between the 5th and 10th centuries due to the domination of Central Asian Turkic peoples over the East Slavs.
As a result of this influence, East Slavic culture was treated as somewhat alien to Western European culture.
Rus people of the North Germanic lineage began to operate from the Scandinavian Peninsula in the northwest and possessed advanced navigation skills.
The Rus engaged in piracy and acts of aggression and were involved in trade along the Baltic Sea and the North Sea.
The Rus traded with the economically prosperous Byzantine Empire to the south, and trade with the Islamic Empire was also active.
These two trade routes influenced the East Slavs through the Rus and Turkic peoples.
The East Slavs formed the Kaganate of the Rus under this influence, which was the initial state of the Rus people and was founded after the conquest by the Khazar Khanate.
The Rus people of the Rus Khaganate became the ancestors of Russians, Belarusians, and Ukrainians.
Kievan Rus was the predecessor of Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine.

The Varangians created Kievan Rus in the 9th century, a state also known as Gardariki that was located along the Dnieper River [cite: 121].
Scandinavian Vikings were known as Varjags in Northern Europe [cite: 2693,2694], and the ancestral homeland of these tribes is considered to be the Pripet Marshes by some scientists [cite: 2692].
A trade route from Varangians to Greeks connected Northern Europe with Byzantium and, through it, with Eastern countries, and this route was important for the political unification of East Slavic tribes.
In 862, the Slavs invited Viking brothers Rurik, Sineus, and Truvor to rule their lands, establishing a capital at Novgorod.
Rurik was the founder of the Rurikid dynasty, and the state was named Rus after the tribe of Rurik.
In 882, Oleg, a relative of Rurik, captured Kiev and moved the capital to Kiev, after which Kievan Rus formed around Kiev.
By the end of the 10th century, the Nordic minority merged with the Slavic population [cite: 2695,2696].
Russia expanded to cover all Eastern Slavic lands and a large part of Baltic lands, including the region known as Galinda that stretched from Smolensk to Moscow.
The legacy of Kievan Rus formed the basis for the national identities of Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine.

During the Viking age, the Varangians came by sea for trade and other purposes, and those who arrived were started to be called Rus or Ross.
The name was gradually adopted by the Slavic settlers who migrated there.
The first Russian state, Rus, was founded in 862 in Novgorod.
Rurik expanded his territory along the Volkhov River and Dnieper River trade route.
The rulers were initially all Varangians but eventually became Slavs through assimilation.
In 882, the capital of Rus moved to Kiev.
The solid foundation of Russian history began in the western regions.

== Early Expansion and Military Campaigns ==

Vladimir the Great (980–1015) won the struggle for succession.
Prince Oleg, together with Rurik's son Igor, implemented measures to place alliances in those regions under their control and also raided the Buzdin and Persians.
Kiev was attacked by nomadic tribes in the 11th and 12th centuries, including the Kipchaks and the Pechenegs, which caused the East Slavic population to migrate.[121,2417] The East Slavs include Russians, Belarusians, and Ukrainians.
The Khazar Khanate had a massive influence on the East Slavs.
The Principality of Kiev adopted concepts of Slavic paganism and autocracy from the Eastern Roman Empire, while Kievan Rus adopted Byzantine culture from the Byzantine Empire in the 9th century.
Internal division caused by the partition inheritance of the Rurik dynasty contributed to the fall of Kievan Rus.
Exchanges with the Byzantine Empire became active.
The prince maintained good relations with the rulers of Sweden, the rulers of Byzantium, and the rulers of the Holy Roman Empire.
The Khazars were a major ally of the Byzantine Empire.[2751,2752] These Slavic descendants later split into Russians and Ukrainians.[2751,2752] They engaged in various trade activities with Asia and Europe.
During the Crusades, new trade routes emerged which diminished the importance of Kievan Rus.

Trade declined as a result of the emergence of new trade routes during the Crusades.
In the 11th and 12th centuries, Turkic tribes including the Kipchaks and Pechenegs began large-scale migration.
This influx forced Slavic populations to migrate in large groups north to the relatively forested regions known as Salezia.
The area settled by the Slavs later became the Novgorod Republic.
The Muslim Turks took over the middle parts of the Volga left empty by the Slavs, a region known as Volga Bulgaria.

== Christianization and Cultural Development ==

This occurred during the time of Vladimir and his son Yaroslav the Wise.
The establishment took place between 988 and 989.
A struggle for the throne began among Yaroslav the Wise's sons after his death.
Vsevolod became the Grand Prince of Kiev between 1078 and 1093.
Vsevolod failed to stop the process of the disintegration of Kievan Rus.
Princes of the lands were asserting increasing independence.
Assemblies of princes held between 1097 and 1113 failed to resolve the situation.
Vladimir Monomakh became the Grand Prince of Kiev in 1113.
Vladimir Monomakh succeeded in stabilizing the situation.
Vladimir Monomakh defeated the Polovtsians.
Vladimir Monomakh subjugated individual princes.
The disintegration of Kievan Rus took an irreversible form.
Mstislav, Vladimir's son, reigned from 1125 to 1132.
After Mstislav's death, Kievan Rus finally disintegrated into separate principalities.
Ancient Rus culture was not limited to the culture of the Kyivan state.
The Kyivan state's culture extended from the Taman Peninsula in the south to the upper reaches of the Northern Dvina in the north and to the upper reaches of the Vistula in the west.
The majority of the population in the state of 'Rus' were East Slavs [669,671].
Historians named this first Russian state 'Kievan Rus' to avoid confusion with other states [669,671].

Eastern Slavs built successive generations of states that continue to exist today.
By the end of the 10th century, the majority of the population was Slavic.
At this time, trade was adopted from Byzantium (Greece).
Vladimir I baptized the country between 988 and 989.
The official introduction of Christianity coincided with the baptism of Prince Vladimir.
Prince Vladimir Sviatoslavich married Anna.
Christianity became the state religion.
During the reign of Yaroslav the Wise in the 11th century, the economy flourished in Russia.
During the reign of Yaroslav the Wise in the 11th century, literature flourished in Russia.
During the reign of Yaroslav the Wise in the 11th century, architecture and craftsmanship flourished in Russia.
Monasteries were built during the reign of Yaroslav the Wise.
Churches were built in Kiev, Novgorod, Polotsk, and other cities during the reign of Yaroslav the Wise.
The first school in the country was established during the reign of Yaroslav the Wise.
Kievan Rus began to split into separate principalities in the 11th century.
Prince Mstislav the Great died in 1132.
The state fragmented into 13 principalities after his death.
The number of principalities constantly increased.
This initial division into lands has persisted.
So-called 'partial principalities' maintained a common identity.
These principalities often fought together against a common enemy from another land.

Anna was the sister of Byzantine Emperor Basil II.

== Ethnic Composition and Assimilation ==

The region began with Eastern Slavic ethnic groups, and Kievan Rus was primarily populated by East Slavs [669,671].
Multiple influxes of Slavic settlers occurred from the 7th to the 10th centuries, originating from the Moravian Danubian region and moving into various regions of the Russian Plain already occupied by Slavs.
This migration played a significant role in consolidating the Slavic population of Eastern Europe and concluded with the formation of the Old Rus ethnic group.
Slavs began to settle in the territories of modern Ukraine and modern Belarus, where Kievan Rus was formed on the territory of modern-day Ukraine.
The early migration wave originated from the lands of the Krivichs and Slovenes, while the later migration wave originated from Southern Rus.
The East Slavic tribes included the Slavs, Krivichs, and Polochans, and one of the groups gathered included Ugric tribes.
The Ugric tribes included the Chud, Ves, Meria, Muroma, and Meshchera.
Eastern Slavs assimilated indigenous Finno-Ugric communities such as the Merya, Mordvins, and Meshchera, and the assimilated groups included the Meshchera.
Eastern Slavs constituted the majority of the population in Western Russia.
Later, Eastern Slavs also assimilated Varangian tribes of Germanic origin.

== Trade Routes and Economic Networks ==

Trade routes passed through Rus territories and connected Baltic Sea countries with Byzantium and the Near East.
One of these routes was known as the 'route from Varangians to Greeks', while another was known as the 'Sarmatian route'.
Trade expeditions took place along the Dnieper River, the Volga River, and the Don River.
These expeditions brought traveling merchants and Varangians into contact with Slavic tribes.
These waterways provide connections to the Caspian Sea.
The power of the Eastern Roman Empire spread as far as the region of Kiev.

== Rulers and Dynastic Succession ==

Oleg ruled until 912 or 922, after which Igor Rurikovich ruled from 912/922 to 945.
Princess Olga ruled from 945 to 957, centralized the state, and established the foundations of a lasting administrative order.
Sviatoslav I, the son of Olga, was the ruler following her and reached Crimea, the Caucasus, and the Balkans during his expeditions.
Sviatoslav I fought numerous wars against the Khazars, and these conflicts led to the final collapse of the Khazar Khaganate around 969.
Jarosław Mądry strengthened the position of the Orthodox Church in Rus, and Anna was the sister of the Byzantine emperor.

== Foreign Relations and Military Campaigns ==

Oleg and Igor Rurikovich signed trade agreements with Byzantium that ensured profitable trade for the country.

== Religion and Cultural Synthesis ==

The adoption of Orthodox Christianity initiated a synthesis of Byzantine and Slavic cultures, an event that began this synthesis and defined the following millennium.

== Political Fragmentation and Principalities ==

These inheritance rules were based on the rule of seniority, but the country's political unity was not preserved by these rules.
Kievan Rus divided into competing principalities in the 11th century.
The Principality of Polotsk was formed in the northwest, the Volhynian Principality in the southwest, the Principality of Kiev, Principality of Turov, and Principality of Smolensk in the central region, the Rostov Principality and Murom Principality in the northeastern region, and the Chernihiv Principality, Pereyaslav Principality, and Tmutarakan Principality in the southeastern region.
Princes who managed to seize Kiev were higher in the feudal hierarchy than other princes and used the title of Grand Prince.
Between 1054 and 1224, 64 principalities were established in Rus, during which 293 princes attempted to sit on the throne and whose political actions led to the outbreak of 83 civil wars.
The rulers of the Chernihiv principality and the rulers of the Halych-Volhynia principality attempted to unite the Russian lands.

== External Threats and Population Migration ==

Constant raids by nomadic Turkic tribes, including the Pechenegs and the Quipchaks, occurred during the 11th and 12th centuries.
These raids caused a massive migration of Slavic populations to safer, heavily forested northern regions such as Zalesye.

== Geography and Regional Terminology ==

Ruthenia was applied mainly to the western and southern regions of Rus, which were adjacent to Catholic Europe.

== Unification and Expansion ==

The Slavic groups included the Slovenes and Krivichs, while the Finno-Ugric tribes included the Ves, Merya, and Chud.
Oleg was a prince of Novgorod who annexed the southern center of the Eastern Slavs to his territories in 882.
Kyiv was the main city of the Polans, and Oleg made Kyiv his capital before subsequently launching an expedition against Byzantium.
Historians consider the unification of northern and southern centers under the Rurikids as the conclusion of the process of forming the Kievan Rus state.
The center of Khazaria was located on the lower Volga, and the expansion of the state to the south led to a confrontation with powerful Khazaria that resulted in a battle in 965.
The leaders of Kiev conducted military campaigns and diplomatic efforts through which the new state expanded.
The lands of some Finno-Ugric, Baltic, Turkic-speaking, and Iranian-speaking tribes were incorporated into the new state.
The process of Slavic colonization was taking place simultaneously in the Volga-Oka interfluve.

Ancient Rus fought for a dominant position in Eastern Europe and the Black Sea region against the Byzantine Empire.
Oleg attacked Constantinople in the early 900s, established Kievan Rus, and founded the Principality of Kiev.
Igor was Oleg's son.
Rurik united the northern and southern territories and founded the Rurik dynasty.
Medieval Rus was founded and ruled by Varangian warrior aristocrats and their descendants [121,2179,2183,2184,4032,4033].
The name 'Kievan Rus' is used to distinguish it from successor states [669,671].
Raids were conducted continuously by nomadic Turkic tribes, including the Kipchaks and the Pechenegs, during the 11th and 12th centuries [2417,4121].
These raids caused a large-scale migration of the Slavic population to safer, densely forested northern regions known as Zalesye [2417,4121].

== Society and Culture ==

A ruling class of princes and boyars formed, and an armed escort of men was part of this ruling class [cite: 3849].
These tribes lacked a stable organization.
These events caused a severe disruption to Nordic trade with the Caliphate, and the Vikings had to seek western trade routes.
The merger of Nordic and Slavic elements began in the late 900s during the time of Grand Princes Vladimir and Yaroslav.
The territory of this kingdom is now part of Ukraine.
Novgorod was a capital city during the first centuries.
This adoption initiated a blend of Byzantine and Slavic cultures that defined Russian culture for the next millennium [cite: 121,2179,2183,2184,4032,4033].
Prince Vladimir Monomakh ascended to the throne in 978.
Kyiv was the center of royal power and the center of the Orthodox Church during the 11th century.
This event marked the beginning of a synthesis between Eastern Roman and Slavic cultures [cite: 121,155,4395].
This cultural synthesis established Russian culture [cite: 121,155,4395].
The Varangians gradually assimilated with the Slavs, and Slavs slowly assimilated Scandinavians.
Slavs formed the main population group from the 8th century onwards.
The Merya were an indigenous Finno-Ugric tribe.

The Muromia were an indigenous Finno-Ugric tribe.
The Meshchera were an indigenous Finno-Ugric tribe.

== Decline and Fragmentation ==

Prince Vladimir Svyatoslavich was the ruler at the time of the adoption.
The disintegration of the unified state began in 1132 after the death of Prince Mstislav Vladimirovich of Kiev.
One of these independent entities was the Chernigov Principality, one was the Ryazan Principality, and one was the Polotsk Principality.
Kyiv remained an object of struggle between the most powerful princely branches, and the land of Kyiv was considered a collective possession of the Rurikids.
One of these principalities was Chernigov and one was Smolensk.
Kievan Rus was the predecessor of modern Ukraine, Belarus, and Russia, and the historical terms refer to a common ancestor of modern Ukraine, Belarus, and Russia.
The Republic of Novgorod was located to the northwest of Kiev.
The military aristocracy consisted of Varangians.

== Origins and Foundation ==

The Rus people originally lived in Europe.
Rurik arrived in Novgorod at the invitation of Slavs and established the first Rus principality, from which the Rurik dynasty originated.

== Cultural Legacy and Modern Successors ==

A fusion of Byzantine and Slavic cultures began after the conversion and lasted for a millennium.
According to historical views, Kievan Rus is considered the predecessor of three modern East Slavic nations: Belarus, Russia, and Ukraine.

The destruction of Kievan Rus' saw the eventual rise of the Grand Duchy of Moscow, initially a part of Vladimir-Suzdal.
While still under the domain of the Mongol-Tatars and with their connivance, Moscow began to assert its influence in the region in the early 14th century, gradually becoming the leading force in the "gathering of the Russian lands".
When the seat of the Metropolitan of the Russian Orthodox Church moved to Moscow in 1325, its influence increased.
Moscow's last rival, the Novgorod Republic, prospered as the chief fur trade centre and the easternmost port of the Hanseatic League.

Led by Prince Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow, the united army of Russian principalities inflicted a milestone defeat on the Mongol-Tatars in the Battle of Kulikovo in 1380.
Moscow gradually absorbed its parent duchy and surrounding principalities, including formerly strong rivals such as Tver and Novgorod.

Ivan III ("the Great") threw off the control of the Golden Horde and consolidated the whole of northern Rus' under Moscow's dominion, and was the first Russian ruler to take the title "Grand Duke of all Rus'".
After the fall of Constantinople in 1453, Moscow claimed succession to the legacy of the Eastern Roman Empire.
Ivan III married Sophia Palaiologina, the niece of the last Byzantine emperor Constantine XI, and made the Byzantine double-headed eagle his own, and eventually Russia's, coat-of-arms.
Vasili III united all of Russia by annexing the last few independent Russian states in the early 16th century.

== Origins and Early Formation ==

The Grand Duchy of Moscow was the most important state, took the place of Kiev-Rus, and was the most powerful successor state of Kievan Rus.
It eventually became the basis of the modern Russian state.
The Principality of Rostov-Suzdal emerged after the fall of Kiev.
Prince Yuri Dolgoruky extended his influence over Novgorod and Kiev, gave his son the title of Grand Prince, and made Vladimir his capital.
Daniel Alexandrovich was the youngest son of Alexander Nevsky and founded the Principality of Moscow, which is also known as Muscovy or Moscovia.
Moscow was located in a favorable position between the central rivers of Russia, and the area included forests and swamps that formed a shield for Moscow.
The reunited principalities established the Moscow Principality, which was a successor to the cultural and political heritage of Kievan Rus.
The Principality of Galicia-Volhynia laid the foundation for the modern Russian nation.
The Grand Principality of Moscow was founded in 1263, and these records date back to 1147.

The area settled by the Slavs later became Vladimir-Suzdal.
The Kyivan Rus had already declined, which facilitated the work of the Mongols.
The arrival of Chinggis Khan's Mongol Empire followed.
The Mongols completely destroyed the existing Russian rule up to that point.
Eventually, the large Kievan Rus state fragmented into many small states with serfdom systems.
The invading group later established a state in the central and southern territories.[158,2418,2419,2420,2421,2422,2423] The new state was named the Principality of Moscow.
The Principality of Moscow was established in the 13th century.
Daniel Moskovsky founded the Principality of Moscow.
Daniel Moskovsky was the youngest son of Alexander Nevsky.
The Grand Duchy of Moscow was founded by Daniil Alexandrovich.
Daniil Alexandrovich was from the Rurik dynasty.
The Grand Duchy of Moscow existed from 1283 to 1547.
The Grand Duchy of Moscow was a principality of Rus.
The Grand Duchy of Moscow was a partial successor to the Kievan Rus' principalities.

== Mongol Invasion and Rule ==

The fragmentation made it easy for the Mongols to overthrow the principalities.
The Mongols, or Golden Horde, had invaded the region since 1223.
Mongol tribes led by Batu Khan, a grandson of Genghis Khan, began invading Russia in 1237.[155,156] Batu Khan invaded with an army consisting of approximately 150,000 to 200,000 fighters.[155,156] Most of the lands were invaded by the Mongols and became branches of the Golden Horde State.
The Golden Horde was a Turkic-Mongol state.
They settled in the steppes north of the Caspian Sea and adopted Sarai Batu as their capital.[157,158,159,160,161] Batu Khan forced living Russian princes to pledge their allegiance to him and to pay heavy taxes.
The Mongols forced many Russians to serve in their armies and appointed a Great Prince.
The Mongol campaigns caused the population of Kievan Rus to lose half its people.
Mongol rule hindered the region's economic development and social development.
The Mongols maintained control over Russian lands until approximately the year 1480.
The Mongol rule in Russia ended in the late 15th century.
Russia was isolated from important Western European influences.

The Golden Horde ruled over southern and central Russia for two centuries.

== Rise of Moscow under Mongol Patronage ==

Mossoon quickly became independent from Vladimir.
Prince Yuri of Moscow married a daughter of the Golden Horde Khan in the early 13th century.
Yuri was appointed Grand Prince of Russia around 1318.
Mongol forces assisted Yuri and helped suppress threats to his rule after some principalities had ignited a rebellion against him.
The Tatars granted the title of Grand Prince of Moscow to the Princes of Moscow and appointed the Princes of Moscow as tax collectors from Russian principalities.
Tax collection began during the principality of Ivan I, who ruled around 1330 and was nicknamed 'Moneybag'.
Ivan kept some of the tax money for himself, purchased many lands, and significantly expanded his territories.
Other princes and major landowners were taken to serve in the Mongol army and government.
Ivan convinced the Patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church to agree to remain in Moscow.
Since the 15th century, the Princes of Moscow wanted to expand Russian territory.

The goal of this struggle was to obtain the title of 'Grand Prince' from the Golden Horde khans.
Prince Ivan Kalita of Moscow eliminated his rival through deceit and received a 'yarlyq' (charter) from the Khan of the Golden Horde.
Ivan Kalita acquired the title of Grand Prince.
After Ivan Kalita obtained the title, the Golden Horde khans did not launch raids into Russian lands for a considerable period.

== Territorial Expansion and Unification ==

The goal of expanding territory was to increase population and wealth under their rule.
Ivan III was the most successful of these princes and laid the foundations for the creation of a Russian national state.
Ivan entered into strong competition with the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, which was located in the northwest of the country, with the goal of controlling some semi-independent kingdoms of the Dnieper River located in the upper reaches of the Dnieper and the basins of the Oka River.[166,167,168] Prince Ivan III split some of the princes, engaged in border skirmishes, fought a long war with the Republic of Novgorod, and defeated Novgorod.[169,170,171] The Duchy of Moscow increased three times in size under Prince Ivan III's rule, and the unification of Russian lands around Moscow continued very rapidly during his reign.[169,170,171] The entity ended the existence of the Principality of Rostov and the Principality of Yaroslavl.
The boyars of Novgorod tried to preserve their independence and requested help from the Grand Prince of Lithuania, which caused Ivan III to launch a campaign against Novgorod.
The Battle of Shelon took place in 1471.
The Moscow Principality expanded north, east, south, and west.

Grand Prince Ivan I used wars to expand the borders of the Grand Principality, fighting a war against Novgorod in 1332 and a war in the Smolensk region in 1340.
Ivan used the purchase of lands and cities to expand the borders by buying territories from impoverished co-rulers and neighboring princes, including Beloozjorsk, Galich, and Uglich.
A war broke out in the second quarter of the 15th century between supporters of state division, led by the princes of Galicia, and others, ending with a victory for Vasily II.
The Republic of Novgorod was annexed in 1478, the Principality of Tver was annexed in 1485, the Principality of Smolensk was annexed in 1514, and the Principality of Ryazan was annexed in approximately 1521.
In principalities united only with the Grand Duchy of Moscow, centralized central authority reigned and the autocracy of the Grand Prince reigned.

== End of Mongol Domination ==

The Principality of Moscow eventually expelled the Tatars from Russia.
Russian principalities declared independence from the Golden Horde, stopped dealing with it, failed to pay tribute on time, and sometimes completely refused to pay tribute.
After the Battle of Kulikovo, where Russian forces achieved their first victory over Mongol-Tatar forces, the Prince of Moscow completely stopped paying tribute to the Golden Horde.
Grand Prince Ivan the Great of Moscow lived from 1440 to 1505 and ended Mongol rule almost 100 years later by standing at the Ugra River.
Ivan declared his absolute sovereignty over all Russian princes and nobles, began a series of attacks that paved the way for the complete defeat of the Golden Horde, and took the final step in separating from Mongol control in 1480 by refusing to pay any taxes to the Mongols.
At that time, the Golden Horde was weakening due to internal power struggles.
Mongol soldiers advanced towards Moscow but then turned their backs.
Russia was freed from Mongol-Tatar domination in 1480, a victory supported by the revival of spiritual life initiated by the Russian Orthodox Church.

== The Time of Troubles ==

The Russian ruler emerged as a powerful and autocratic leader.
A large number of Russians who were dissatisfied with Boris's rule joined the invaders.
This invasion was a landmark event that marked the beginning of an era of turmoil in Russia.
Russia was torn apart by invasion and political chaos.
This period of destruction lasted until 1613.
False Dmitry ascended the tsarist throne in 1605.
A group of landowners killed False Dmitry in the following year.
Prince Vasily Shuisky became the Tsar of Russia after False Dmitry's death.
Polish invaders occupied Moscow in 1610.
The Polish invaders ruled through a parliamentary council of landowners.
The ruling council was powerless.
Another claimant named Dmitry appeared at the same time.
These claimants found many supporters.
Peasant uprisings swept through Russia.
Landowners fought Cossacks on the borders.
Polish control of Moscow led to the unification of the Russians.
The united Russians worked to expel the Polish invaders.

== Other Principalities and External Conflicts ==

The capital was moved during the 11th century.
The Pskov region was freed from Mongol domination.
The Novgorodians successfully thwarted the Teutonic Knights' attempt to establish a colony in Northern Russia in 1242.
Moscow achieved success in trade with Western European and Eastern countries.

== Origins and Early Rise ==

Moscow was founded in 1147 and was small and insignificant at that time.
The most powerful of the states that emerged after the destruction of Kievan Rus was the Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal, which existed from 1157 to 1389 [cite: 1480] and formed the basis of modern Russia [cite: 121].
Both the Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal and the Republic of Novgorod were independent, and this independence allowed them to develop.
The Moscow Principality was formed in the 13th century and later replaced the former Kiev/Vladimir-Suzdal principality.
Daniil Alexandrovič, the youngest son of Alexander Nevsky, moved the seat of his principality from Vladimir to Moscow.
The Grand Principality of Moscow was founded in 1276, and the Grand Duchy of Moscow existed from 1263 to 1547 [cite: 1480].
The expansion of the Moscow Principality led to the formation of the Grand Duchy of Moscow, which began to gain significance in the late 13th century.
The Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal later transformed into the Principality of Moscow, which was the most powerful state to emerge after the destruction of Kievan Rus [cite: 162] and proved to be the most assertive principality in the long run.

== Mongol Invasion and the Tatar Yoke ==

The Mongol invasion of Rus began in 1223 with the Battle of the Kalka [cite: 943].
This principle facilitated the subjugation of the divided principalities during the Mongol invasion [cite: 943].
One such transition period was between 1240 and 1480, and the transition phase lasted until the mid-14th century [cite: 943].
This period is referred to as the 'Dark Age' [cite: 943], while Russian national historiography refers to this period as the 'Tatar Yoke' [cite: 944].
The Golden Horde was part of the Mongol Empire [cite: 699], and the principalities of Rus were within the power sphere of the Golden Horde.
The extent of this inclusion varied in intensity among different principalities, yet the principalities of Rus were able to preserve a certain degree of internal autonomy.
Mongol foreign rule led to a break in relations with the West and promoted the isolation of Orthodox Russia [cite: 944].
This break in relations lasted for two centuries [cite: 944].
There were frequent Mongol-Tatar raids, a decline in agriculture, and various epidemics spread.
The Black Death did not affect Russia as severely as Western Europe, and the Russian population was able to recover quickly.

== Rise of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania ==

The Grand Duchy of Lithuania initially established itself in unoccupied or weakly controlled territories and took over or subjugated territories of the old Rus, including Kiev, which it took in 1362.
The Lithuanian princes remained pagan for a long time, while the majority of the Lithuanian subjects were East Slavic and Orthodox.
The Lithuanians partially adopted the culture of their subjects, used Church Slavonic as the written language in their chanceries, and converted to Orthodoxy when marrying into East Slavic principalities.
The pagan Lithuanians attempted to establish their own metropolitan see.
They achieved victories over the Teutonic Order, the Mongol Golden Horde, and a certain Principality of Moscow, with one of these victories being the Battle on the Blue Waters in 1362.
The principalities in the area of the Golden Horde were fragmented and hostile towards each other.

== Consolidation of Power and Independence ==

Prince Ivan III of Moscow won the Battle of Shelon, and the territory of Novgorod was completely occupied by Moscow in 1478.
The Principality of Moscow adopted a policy of expanding its territory through conquests, with the next target being the Turkic peoples who lived in the north and along the Volga River.
These peoples lost their independence and sovereignty and faced Russification and Christianization policies.
The Russian principalities completely lost their independence, and a centralized state was formed that was governed by a Grand Prince and the Boyar Duma.
The Duma was composed of former princes and the heirs of those former princes.
Tsar Ivan III lived from 1462 to 1505 and laid the foundation for the empire that would emerge later.

He tripled the territory of the state and ordered the restoration of the Moscow Kremlin.
The battle took place at the Kulikovo Field [cite: 699].
Moscow continued to pay tribute to the Golden Horde.
The Muscovite state became fully independent from the Tatars in 1480.
The Tatars lost political power.
The Metropolitan of Kiev moved in the 14th century, first to Vladimir and then to Moscow in 1328.

== Legal and Social Reforms ==

In 1497, the Grand Prince issued a decree to apply the right of judicial serfdom and grant peasants specific rights regarding their land.
The decree permitted peasants to leave their lord's land only once a year during a window of one week before or after Yuri's Day.
This decree laid the foundation for a nationwide serfdom system.
From the 10th century to the 17th century, land was managed by nobles (boyars).

== Demographics and Cultural Assimilation ==

In the 17th century, Russians were a mixture of peoples speaking different languages who belonged to the Slavic family.
The Great Russians and the Muscovites lived around Moscow, penetrated the northern forests, and assimilated numerous Fin tribes.

== Religious Autonomy ==

The Russian Orthodox Church finally separated from the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate in Constantinople in the 15th century after the Patriarchate agreed to concessions to the Pope due to the political decline of Byzantium.

== Territorial Expansion and Wars ==

Kyiv was included among these territories, which extended from Kyiv to Mozhaysk, near Moscow, and were formerly part of Kievan Rus [cite: 700].
Moscow residents sought to gain control over these territories during the protracted Russo-Lithuanian War.
The battle took place at Orsha in 1514, where the Polish-Lithuanian Union defeated the Muscovites.
A peace treaty was signed in 1522, based on which Lithuania ceded certain territories located in the lands of former Kievan Rus to Moscow, including Smolensk.
The Grand Duchy of Lithuania attempted to attack Moscow again in the same year.
Major military conflicts were resolved for approximately 40 years.

== Southern and Siberian Colonization ==

The colonization occurred in the mid-16th century and followed the conquest of Kazan and Astrakhan.
Many cities were initially founded as border fortresses that served as support points for the Verhaulinie, a defensive line against the Crimean Tatars.
The current city of Voronezh was founded in 1586, Samara was founded in 1586, Zarizyn was founded in 1589, and Saratow was founded in 1590.
Numerous Cossack forts known as Ostrogs were established in Siberia, including Tobolsk, Irkutsk, Bratsk, Tomsk, and Yakutsk.
The ancient Golden Horde State was fragmented and three Tatar khanates were established in place of the Golden Horde.
Pskov maintained a certain degree of autonomy.

== Mongol Invasions and Rule ==

Turkic nomadic tribes launched continuous attacks during the 1000s and 1100s, which caused a massive migration of Slavs to safer northern forest areas.
In 1226, a nomadic warrior people that came from Mongolia attacked the principalities, and the Russians called this group Tataro-Mongols.
Batou was a khan.
The Golden Horde ruled southern and central Russia and plundered Russian principalities.
Many other regions of Eurasia were conquered by the Mongols, and the Golden Horde raided the principalities of the Russian region and ruled the southern and central parts of the region.
Mongol rule slowed the region's economic development and social development.
Vladimir-Suzdal remained under Mongol rule.

== Northern Republics and External Threats ==

Mongol invasions did not reach the Principality of Pskov, while Northern Crusades directed by the Roman Catholic Church took place in the region.
Before the subjugation of feudal states in Russia to the Grand Duchy of Moscow, certain principalities existed in Western Russia and were located in the Galicia-Volhynia region.
This period occurred during the time when the territories belonged to the Grand Duchies of Lithuania, Rus', and Samogitia.
These principalities had limited central power, and the nobility (szlachta) and magnates within them enjoyed significant freedoms.
Novgorod and Pskov were republics with significant commercial and economic power, and Pskov retained part of its autonomy during the Mongol period.
Novgorod and Pskov were partially spared from other disturbances affecting the region.
The German crusaders sought to turn the region into a colony.
The Republic of Novgorod formed the basis of modern Russia.
Novgorod was a city-state with an original system of government that prospered due to trade exchanges with Baltic countries.

== Diplomacy with the Golden Horde ==

Prince Yuri Danilovich of Moscow achieved support from the Golden Horde using diplomatic means in 1318, married the daughter of the Khan of the Golden Horde in 1318, was recognized by the Golden Horde as the senior prince of Russian princes in 1318, and was recognized by the Golden Horde as Grand Prince of Vladimir in 1319.
The Golden Horde encouraged the creation of a strong vassalage in Russia.
Iwan I. gained precedence over other principalities starting in 1325 through good contacts with the Golden Horde.
Iwan I. helped the Mongols with the difficult task of tax collection and collected payments on behalf of the Mongols [cite: 945].
The Mongols could now primarily negotiate with him, no longer had to deal with individual principalities, and avoided uprisings against their tax collectors in those principalities [cite: 945].
This protected his own territory from Mongol raids [cite: 945].
Simeon had good relations with Sarai, the capital of the Horde, and with Özbeg Khan, the ruler in Sarai [cite: 946].

== The Reign of Ivan I Kalita ==

Ivan I's political policies created the foundation for Moscow's rise, which experienced a significant rise in power, and this allowed him to significantly increase his wealth, earning him the nickname Kalita (Moneybag).
Özbeg Khan confirmed Simeon's claim to the Grand Prince title of Vladimir even though the claims of the Principality of Twer were considered more legitimate than Simeon's.
An uprising against the Horde broke out in 1327, and Mongols and Ivan Kalita jointly suppressed it.
The victory weakened Mongol rule but did not break it, increased the prestige of Moscow, and established Moscow as the leader of resistance against a weakened Horde.
Ivan I designated Moscow as the capital of the new Grand Duchy and moved the seat of the Russian Orthodox Church metropolitan from Vladimir to Moscow.
Grand Prince Ivan I Kalita continued the unification of smaller Russian lands and principalities under Moscow's power by using the support of the Golden Horde to achieve this unification.

== Reign of Ivan the Great ==

Ivan the Great became the de facto founder of a centralized Russian state.
Russian legislation was reformed under Ivan the Great.
Most of the current Moscow Kremlin was built under Ivan the Great.

== Cultural and Religious Development ==

This cultural understanding was based on persistence and traditions.
Religious worldview determined cultural development in the Muscovite Empire, slowed cultural development in the Muscovite Empire, and churchly interpretation of texts slowed cultural development in the Muscovite Empire.
The Russian-Orthodox culture began to stagnate in 1500.
Byzantium was the driving force behind this culture and fell under Ottoman rule after the fall of Constantinople.
Moscow began to dominate the cultural legacy of Kievan Rus and the political legacy of Kievan Rus.
The Russian Orthodox Church aided the army.
In the 14th century, the Muscovite trading kingdom emerged as a major player.

== Conflicts with Lithuania and Poland ==

The title expressed a claim to the western part of Rus, which was controlled by the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in the 14th century.
This led to prolonged wars in the 16th and 17th centuries against Poland and Lithuania, known as the Russo-Lithuanian Wars.
The Republic of Novgorod and Vladimir-Suzdal laid the foundations for modern Russia.

== Mongol Invasion and Destruction ==

The leader of the Mongol invasion was Batu Khan, who was the grandson of Genghis Khan. Batu Khan defeated the armies of the princes one after another. Batu Khan reduced major cities to ashes, including Vladimir and Moscow. The populations were massacred and reduced to slavery. Kiev Rus was already weakened before the invasion. The Tatars raided the Russian kingdom. These territories were invaded by the Mongols, like many other regions of Eastern Europe. Moscow did not yet appear in history at that time. The Prince of Moscow was just one among many Rus princes. The Mongol Empire strengthened during this period. The Mongols organized conquest wars.

== Mongol Administration and Tribute ==

The principalities had to recognize Mongol suzerainty, and the Mongols established a state south of the Volga River.
During this period, various local powers were vassals of their Golden Horde Khanate.
The Duchy of Moscow paid an annual tribute to the Mongols and had the obligation to collect this tribute from all other Russian feudal city-states.
A portion of the annual tribute was retained by the Duchy of Moscow, and this retention allowed for economic, social, and military growth in the Muscovite Duchy.
Russia cooperated well with the Mongol conquerors during the Golden Horde era, and one example of this cooperation was that Russia willingly paid taxes to the Mongols.
The Prince of Moscow gradually gained power by organizing the tribute payments for the Rus princes, and this Grand Duchy possessed a high degree of independence.

== Cultural and Social Impact of the Mongols ==

The Tatar Mongols deeply influenced Russia, ethnically through the settlement of Turkic-speaking peoples and culturally through the Islamization of peoples east of Moscow, between Vladimir and Kazan.
This cultural influence strengthened the weight of the Church against Muslim occupation.
The Russian vocabulary was enriched by many terms from the Mongol language, including "yam," meaning "post station," and "tamga," meaning "toll." Russia became a multi-ethnic state as settlement began on these Russian territories by people of Tatar origin.
The long rule of nomads delayed the economic development of the country and delayed the social development of the country.
This situation was similar to what happened in the Balkans and Asia Minor.
This period caused Russia to be isolated from Western Europe.

== Rise of Moscow under Early Princes ==

Ivan I ruled from 1332 to 1341, and during his reign the Grand Duchy of Moscow began to become the most important Russian principality.
The Russian state centered on Moscow was able to survive and was different from the Byzantine Empire.
At the beginning of the 14th century, the Duchy of Moscow began to assert its influence over Western Russia and gained the capacity to lead the liberation from Tatar supremacy.
A spiritual revival was brought by Saint Sergius of Radonezh.
Among the states formed on the territory of disintegrated Kievan Rus, the most important and powerful were the Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal and the Republic of Novgorod to the northeast, while the Principality of Galicia-Volhynia was the strongest state to the northwest.

== Alexander Nevsky and Western Threats ==

Aleksandr Nevskij was the lord of Novgorod while the Swedes and Teutonic Knights were attempting to colonize the region.
Alexander Nevsky was a significant figure in Russian history.
On July 15, 1240, Alexander Nevsky's detachment and the Novgorod militia decisively defeated the Swedes on the Neva River.
In 1242, Nevsky destroyed German knights on Lake Chud.
Nevsky halted their aggression to the east.

== Battle of Kulikovo and Decline of the Horde ==

The Golden Horde declined after the Battle of Kulikovo.
Later, Mongol rule gradually weakened.
States were strengthening as the Mongol yoke weakened.

== Internal Rivalries and Civil War ==

The movement of unification faced rivalries and the tradition of dividing territories among a prince's sons.
These factors led to a civil war between 1425 and 1453.
The civil war ended with the victory of Vasili II.

== Reign of Ivan III and Territorial Expansion ==

Ivan III ruled from 1462 to 1505, and the ruler ascended to the throne in 1462.
A Venetian traveler described him as a tall man leaning forward and handsome.
The Mongol Empire was fragmented into several khanats at that time.
He absorbed the main independent Russian principalities, annexed Novgorod in 1478, and annexed the Principality of Tver in 1485.
In 1485, the ruler took the title of 'sovereign of all Rus''.
The ruler wanted to show his will to restore the entire heritage of Vladimir.
The territory of Muscovy quadrupled, and this expansion occurred at the end of a ruler's reign.
Ivan III and his wife decided that their capital should become the Third Rome.
Ridolfo (Aristotle) Fioravanti from Bologna directed the construction of the Kremlin.
The new Russian Sudebnik was written during the reign of Ivan III, and Vladimir Gusev wrote the new Russian Sudebnik.
Russia stopped paying the regular tribute required by the Khan during Ivan III's reign.
The type of government in Muscovy changed radically during the reign of Ivan III, and the government in Muscovy became an autocracy during the reign of Ivan III.

Vassili III reigned from 1505 to 1533.

Novgorod and Pskov are located in the northeast.

== Military Reforms and Cossacks ==

The Russians administratively integrated tribes and organized troop levies, while Russian princes imposed a relay post service on their subjects.
The Russian army adopted the use of light cavalry and was assisted by the Russian Orthodox Church.
The Russian volunteer corps was led by two national heroes.
Cossacks were warriors who were organized into military communities and were similar to pirates and pioneers of the New World.

== Geopolitical Context and Neighboring States ==

Western Russian states united to form a single nation at that time.
The area that later became the center of the future Russian state is the Moscow basin.
The territories of modern Ukraine and Belarus were included in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and later included in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, a historical inclusion often referred to simply as Poland, a factor that distinguished Ukrainians and Belarusians from other Russian populations.
At that time, the Grand Duchy of Moscow, located on the northeastern frontier of Rus, had integrated the northeastern regions of Rus and belonged to the authority of the Grand Prince of Kievan Rus.
Russia defeated neighboring countries and brought most of the eastern territories of the former Kievan Rus under its influence.
The Golden Horde was one of the most powerful states.

== End of Mongol Rule and Independence ==

The rule of the Tsars returned after the fragmentation.
After the 13th century, as Mongol power declined in the West, Russia became independent.
The expansion was accelerated under the great princes.
The strongest state to emerge after the destruction of Kievan Rus was the Grand Duchy of Moscow.

At that time, the Mongol Empire was the most powerful entity.

The Republic of Novgorod was established after the fall of Rus.

These principalities succeeded Kievan Rus as its continuation and simultaneously suffered under the Mongol yoke.
In the 13th century, the governors of the Golden Horde in Russian principalities were the princes of Vladimir-Suzdal.
Parts of modern Ukraine and Belarus were ruled by local lords known as great princes of Lithuania and Poland.

A long civil war took place in the Grand Duchy of Moscow.
After the collapse of Kievan Rus, several minor Ruthenian principalities emerged.

Undeterred, the Crimeans continued to raid Russian lands but used irregular troops instead of regular army forces.
To stop the Crimean raids, Russia built fortifications along its southern border.
The raids ended around the 17th century.

These principalities included the Grand Duchy of Smolensk, the Grand Duchy of Vladimir, the Grand Duchy of Ryazan, and the Grand Duchy of Tver.

Ivan I collected taxes for the Mongols, made Moscow a wealthy country, maintained his subordination to the Tartars, gained the favor of the Mongol descendants, started lending money to neighboring provinces, and was nicknamed 'Kalyta' (meaning money bag).

== Demographics, Culture, and Society ==

Ancient Rus culture included the art of the powerful Vladimir-Suzdal Principality, the art of the Novgorod Boyar Republic, and the art of the Moscow Principality.
All of Europe faced a devastating plague between 1350 and 1490.

== Liberation and State Consolidation ==

== Mongol Invasion and Golden Horde Rule ==

Batu Khan led the Golden Horde.

The Mongols governed Cumania and Volga Bulgaria.

== Rise of Vladimir and the Metropolitanate ==

Andrei Bogolyubsky became the Grand Prince as a result of capturing Kiev, whereas most of his predecessors moved their capital to Kiev.
After conquering Kiev, Prince Andrew Bogolyubsky settled subordinate princes there.
Alexander Nevsky received the Vladimir throne in 1252 from Khan Sartak, and this throne included supremacy over all Russian principalities.
In 1299, Metropolitan Maxim moved his seat from Kiev to Vladimir during a war between the Golden Horde khans Tokta and Nogai.
As a result of this move, Vladimir became the main political center of Rus and the main religious center of Rus.
Metropolitan Peter moved the seat of the metropolitans in 1325 from Vladimir to Moscow.
Moscow rulers first held power in Vladimir, initially titled themselves Grand Princes of Vladimir, and this practice continued until the end of the 14th century.

== Alexander Nevsky and Northern Defense ==

Alexander Nevsky was a prince of Novgorod, a high-ranking leader during the period of Tatar rule and Lithuanian expansion, and a skilled politician.
He defeated the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order in 1242 in a battle that took place on Lake Peipus.
The Novgorodians fought German crusaders at the Battle of Lake Peipus in 1242.

== Lithuanian Expansion and Western Rus' ==

The fragmentation of Rus and its weakening by wars with the Tatars created conditions for Lithuanian expansion.
Lithuania conquered most of the western Russian principalities between 1240 and 1392.
The Lithuanian state itself quickly underwent Ruthenization.
The lands of modern-day Belarus were the first to be conquered and were annexed to Lithuania.
The Principality of Polotsk and the Principality of Pinsk were among these lands.
The Principality of Kiev suffered a defeat in battle against Lithuanian forces over the Irpen River in 1320.
Kievshchyna became dependent on Lithuania after this defeat and was directly incorporated into Lithuania in 1362.
The Rurikid princes of Kiev were deprived of power by Lithuanian dukes and subsequently emigrated to Ryazan.
The Halicz-Volhynia Duchy was abolished as a result of the Polish-Lithuanian War, which took place between 1340 and 1392, and its territory was divided between Poland and Lithuania.
The Great Duchy of Lithuania was developing power and stood in the way of the princes' unification efforts.

The Great Duchy of Lithuania had been in a personal union with Poland since 1386.
Former western lands of Kievan Rus fell under the influence of the Great Duchy of Lithuania.
Western Russian principalities were previously annexed by Lithuania, Poland, and other countries to a lesser extent.
Galicia-Volhynia was assimilated by the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

== Founding of the Moscow Line ==

Daniel, the youngest son of Alexander, sat on the throne from 1263 and was the founder of the Moscow line of the Rurikids.

== Ivan I Kalita and the Rise of Moscow ==

In 1328, Ivan I Kalita defeated Alexander of Tver, who was one of the most dangerous rivals for the Vladimir throne, with the help of the Tatars.
In the same year, Ivan I Kalita gained rule over Vladimir and moved the capital of his state from Vladimir to Moscow, which was his native city.
This move marked the beginning of the Grand Duchy of Moscow.

== Dmitry Donskoy and the Battle of Kulikovo ==

Grandson of Kalyta, Dmitry Donskoy, defeated the Tatars at the Battle of Kulikovo.
This victory marked the beginning of the decline of the Golden Horde on Rus'.
The position of the Tatars weakened.
The Russian Orthodox Church aided the united army of Russian principalities.
The Russian volunteer corps was led by two national heroes.

== Territorial Expansion under Ivan III ==
