According to Russian propaganda, this coup led to an outbreak of dissatisfaction among residents in southern and eastern Ukraine, while the new Ukrainian authorities persecuted the Russian population and attempted genocide.
Viktor Yanukovych was the president of Ukraine who fled the country in 2014 following street demonstrations.
Russian President Putin did not accept the Euromaidan in Ukraine, which took place in 2014.
Russia claimed to protect the Russian-speaking population as a pretext for the annexation.
Opinions arose that Putin attempted to recreate a Russian quasi-empire of the Cold War era modeled after the former Soviet Union.
US Senator John McCain declared that Russia was a 'gas station disguised as a country' in 2014.

== 2022 full-scale invasion ==

This recognition occurred on February 21, 2022.
Russia launched a military invasion of Ukraine three days after recognizing the independence.
The goal of the invasion was to destroy Ukraine's statehood and to seize additional territories.
The invasion occurred shortly after Russia recognized the independence of the republics in Donbas.
The deployment of troops happened after the Revolution of Dignity.
Putin requested authorization to deploy Russian troops in Ukraine and received authorization from the Russian legislature to deploy troops in Ukraine.
Putin announced the military operation around 06:00 Moscow time.
Ukrainian cities were attacked by Russian missiles minutes after the announcement.
The letter 'Z' symbol is viewed as a new swastika.

== 2022 annexation of four regions ==

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched an annexation process on September 30, 2022, targeting regions controlled by Russia in Ukraine.
Putin stated he would sign laws to absorb these regions despite international condemnation and stated he would protect the newly incorporated regions using all available means.

== International sanctions and travel restrictions ==

Most European countries, the entire European Union, and some other countries around the world banned Russian airline flights from their airspace after the invasion.
In retaliation, Russia banned foreign airlines from flying to Russia.
Significant restrictions were introduced on the ability of Russian citizens to cross European land borders with Norway, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland.
These restrictions significantly affected tourist traffic.

== Historical border disputes ==

A territorial dispute between Ukraine and Russia initially existed between 1991 and 2013.
The dispute revolved around the lack of a defined border between the two countries.
The undefined border involved the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.

== Military operations in Crimea ==

Russian Federation military forces conducted a special operation in Crimea in 2014.
The majority of the Ukrainian military on the peninsula surrendered as a result of the operation, switched sides to Russia following the surrender, and were mostly incorporated into the Russian armed forces.
The special operation allowed Crimea to separate from Ukraine relatively peacefully.

== Kosovo precedent ==

On July 22, 2010, an International Court of Justice ruling was issued.
The International Court of Justice ruled that a unilateral declaration of independence by Kosovo does not violate international law.

== Georgia conflict precedent ==

The war in Georgia began on August 8, 2008.
After the war, Russia officially recognized Abkhazia as an independent state and officially recognized South Ossetia as an independent state.

== Background and origins of the conflict ==

The Euromaidan protest movement occurred in Ukraine while Viktor Yanukovych was the president of Ukraine, and he was ousted following the protests.
Tensions arose between Ukrainians and ethnic Russians in eastern Ukraine, and these tensions escalated into the Donbas war.
The country illegally annexed the Crimean Peninsula from Ukraine in the spring of 2014, an event known as the Crimea crisis.
The annexation of Crimea from Ukraine occurred in the spring of 2014 and resulted from the merger of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and Sevastopol.
Russia escalated its war-making against Ukraine continuously, and the Russian government was condemned by many world leaders.
The Donbas region consists of the Luhansk and Donetsk oblasts, and the seizure by paramiliters led to a regional war.
Russia began a large military buildup in March 2021 along the Ukraine border that included equipment alongside troops, with the number of troops involved reaching up to 190,000.
Russia had plans to invade or attack Ukraine, and various Russian government officials denied these invasion or attack plans until one day before the invasion despite the buildup of military forces.

== War in Donbas and hybrid warfare ==

Russia supported the self-proclaimed Donetsk People's Republic (DNR) and Luhansk People's Republic (LNR) during the war in Donbas.
The ambition of the Russian Federation was to recover territories lost after the dissolution of the USSR.
Russia supported pro-Russian entities in eastern Ukraine.
Russia aimed to make eastern Ukraine part of Putin's 'Novorossiya'.
The sanctions were related to the war in Donbas.
A military operation conducted by Russia began on September 30, 2015, and targeted terrorist groups and opposition forces.
Russia recognized the independence of the Donetsk People's Republic (DPR) and the Luhansk People's Republic (LNR) on February 21, 2022.
Russia supported separatists in the internationally unrecognized Donetsk People's Republic and the internationally unrecognized Luhansk People's Republic.
Russia and Ukraine did not officially enter a mutual war.
The period between 2014 and 2022 is often described as a period of hybrid war.
The country provided economic support to the two Ukrainian breakaway republics, Donetsk and Lugansk.
The support enabled the republics to resist Ukraine's attempts to retake the areas.
Russian-backed paramiliters seized a portion of the Donbas region in southeastern Ukraine.

== Escalation and recognition of separatist republics ==

In July 2021, President Putin made a statement that Ukraine is an 'inseparable part of Russia', after which Russian military presence increased in border areas against Ukraine and Belarus.
On February 21, 2022, Russia decided to recognize the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic, which had declared independence unilaterally in the Donbas region.
Russia recognized the independence of the Donetsk and Luhansk republics in February 2022.
Russian troops entered both regions, and the Russian Federation Council approved the use of military force by a unanimous vote.

== Launch of the full-scale invasion ==

Russian President Vladimir Putin declared a 'special military operation' and Russia openly invaded Ukraine upon announcing it.[4164,4165,4166,4167,4168] The occupation began around 06:00 Moscow time on February 24, 2022.[4164,4165,4166,4167,4168] Putin stated the purpose was to 'purge Ukraine of military and Nazism'.[4164,4165,4166,4167,4168] In his speech, Putin supported irredentism, opposed Ukraine's right to exist as a state, and falsely claimed that Ukraine was ruled by neo-Nazis who oppressed the ethnic Russian minority.[4169,4170,4171,4172,4173,4174,4175] Missiles and rockets targeted many Ukrainian cities, including the capital city of Kyiv.[3028,4176,4177] Ground invasions from different fronts followed these air strikes.[3028,4176,4177] Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy declared martial law and a mobilization.[4178,4179,4180]

== Military operations and territorial changes ==

Russian attacks initially began from the northern front, which advanced from Belarus towards Kyiv, the northeastern front, which advanced towards Kharkiv, the southern front, which advanced northwards from Crimea, and the southeastern front, which advanced from Luhansk and Donetsk.
Russia's advance towards Kiev stopped in March, Russian troops withdrew from the northern front by April, Russia captured Kherson in March, Russia advanced in the southern and southeastern fronts, Russia captured Mariupol in May following a siege, Russia launched a new attack in the Donbas region on April 19, and the Luhansk Oblast was completely captured by Russian forces by July 3.
Ukrainian forces launched counter-offensives in August in the south and in September in the northeast.

== Annexation of four Ukrainian regions ==

In September 2022, Putin announced that Russia had annexed over 15% of land in the Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia regions.
The annexed regions include parts of the Kherson Oblast, parts of the Zaporizhzhia Oblast, parts of the Donetsk Oblast, and parts of the Luhansk Oblast.
These regions were occupied by Russia at the time of the announcement.
The annexation followed internationally unrecognized referendums.
The United Nations General Assembly declared the annexation illegal.

== War crimes and human rights abuses ==

The atrocities included massacres.
Victims in the camps suffered rape, torture, starvation, and were killed.
1.6 million Ukrainians were deported, 250,000 of whom were children.
Russia denies the deportations and refers to them as 'evacuation'.

== International response and sanctions ==

The international community demanded the immediate withdrawal of Russian forces from Ukraine.
Western countries primarily expanded sanctions against Russia.
Massive sanctions were imposed against Russia and its loyal ally Belarus.
Business contacts with the Western world were severed.
An economic iron curtain was established west of Russia and loyal Belarus.
This assertion occurred after Western sanctions and aid to Ukraine.
The aid to Ukraine was part of an effort to stop the invasion.
The United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution.
The resolution condemned the occupation.
The resolution demanded the complete withdrawal of Russian forces.
The International Court of Justice ordered Russia to suspend its military operations.
Many countries provided humanitarian aid to Ukraine.
Sanctions were imposed on Belarus, a Russian ally.
Russia applied sanction policies in response.
Russia's sanctions were directed at those Western countries.

== Recognition of other breakaway states ==

One of the recognized states is Abkhazia and the other recognized state is South Ossetia.
Russian military patrols occupied parts of the territory in all four countries.

== International condemnation and legal actions ==

The International Criminal Court launched an investigation covering crimes against humanity committed in Ukraine since 2013 and including war crimes from the 2022 occupation.
The annexation occurred in defiance of the Budapest Memorandum, which stipulates that Russia acts as a guarantor of Ukraine's territorial integrity.
The Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine declared Russia a 'state-terrorist'.
The forcible annexation of Crimea is not recognized by the Ukrainian state, the UN General Assembly, the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE), the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly, and contradicts the Venice Commission's opinion.
Russia was recognized as a military aggressor.

== Economic impact and corporate response ==

The world economy and Russia's economy were primarily affected by these widespread sanctions.
Over 1,000 companies withdrew from Russia and Belarus.

== Domestic protests and repression ==

Protests were organized against the occupation and took place around the world, including in Russia.
The protests were suppressed by mass arrests, during which media censorship was increased and the use of the words "war" and "occupation" was banned.

== Crimean annexation details ==

The annexation took place on March 18, 2014, when Russia signed an Agreement to admit Crimea and Sevastopol into the Russian Federation.
The event occurred on May 29, 2014.
The annexation of Crimea and Sevastopol by Russia is a military aggression by Russia aimed at forcibly and illegally detaching the Crimean autonomy and Sevastopol from Ukraine to annex these territories to the Russian Federation as subjects of the Russian Federation, actions that were carried out during March 2014.
The Russian authorities interpret the annexation as the 'return of Crimea to Russia'.

== Russian military involvement and support for separatists ==

On June 30, 2014, Philip Breedlove, the Supreme Allied Commander of NATO in Europe, made a statement acknowledging that Russia financially and materially supports separatists, uses mercenaries against Ukraine, and that regular Russian armed forces facilitate the movement of fighters, equipment, and funds across Ukraine's border.
The organizations 'DNR' and 'LNR' are supported by Russia.
According to the SBU, a serious component of the conflict involves real Russian military personnel, including employees of the GRU and the FSB, while the next component consists of recruited mercenaries from the Russian Federation who are participants in illegal armed bands existing in the Luhansk region and the Donetsk region.
The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation began direct participation in combat operations against the Armed Forces of Ukraine from mid-July 2014, with units operating from the territory of the Russian Federation and directly on the territory of Ukraine.

== Sabotage, intelligence operations, and detainments ==

Saboteurs from Russian intelligence operate in Ukraine, where Russian intelligence saboteurs are established or detained daily. [4315,4316,4317]
The Security Service of Ukraine detained a group of Russian saboteurs on July 3, 2014, who were preparing a terrorist attack against the leadership of the anti-terrorist operation. [4315,4316,4317]
All instructions and weapons for this group came to Ukraine from specific military units of the Russian Federation. [4315,4316,4317]
On July 4, 2014, the counterintelligence of the Security Service of Ukraine established the involvement of Valeriy Yurievich Travkin, a citizen of the Russian Federation and staff member of the Main Intelligence Directorate of the General Staff of the Russian Federation. [4318,4319]
Travkin was involved in supplying weapons from Russia to band formations and mercenaries in eastern regions of Ukraine, including the organization of heavy weaponry supplies from the Rostov region of Russia. [4318,4319]
He acted together with an associate from the GRU of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation nicknamed 'Greek', and the supplies were transported using so-called 'corridors' on the Ukrainian-Russian border. [4318,4319]
Travkin had combat experience in Chechnya and recruited fighters for replenishing terrorist organizations. [4318,4319]

Terrorist organizations were located in the Luhansk region.
The event occurred on July 4, 2014.
The group was led by I.
Bezler.
Two Ukrainian citizens were detained on the territory of Kharkiv region.
The two citizens were part of a reconnaissance and sabotage group of the GRU of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation.
The group seized administrative buildings of state authorities and law enforcement agencies in Ukraine.
The group took hostages.
The group engaged in combat operations against Ukrainian military personnel.
According to the militants' testimony, their group was formed by representatives of the GRU of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation.
The group underwent special combat training at a camp of the Russian intelligence service on the territory of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea.
The detention took place in Odesa.
Russian saboteurs were detained on July 5, 2014.
The activities of an intelligence network were stopped.
The group launched extensive efforts to destabilize the situation in the region.
According to the SBU, a group of individuals arrived in Odesa.
The group included two Russians and one Belarusian.
The group came to carry out tasks assigned by Russian intelligence.

== Weapon smuggling and logistics ==

All weapons from occupied Crimea are being transported along a route that goes from occupied Crimea to Russian territory and continues from Russian territory to the Luhansk region, including T-90 tanks.
Russian state agencies engage in the smuggling of weapons, transport terrorists to Ukrainian territory, and display weapons and military equipment at the exhibition.
The Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation provides this weapons and military equipment to band formations for the purpose of conducting military operations on the territory of Ukraine.

== War crimes and atrocities ==

The organizations 'DNR' and 'LNR' kidnapped members of the OSCE international mission who enjoyed diplomatic protection.
They fired during the ceasefire and continued firing after the ceasefire.
They shoot at children and at refugee camps.

== Propaganda and information warfare ==

The Navalny team published an investigation on December 22, 2021, about Alexander Borodai that called on Russians not to participate in possible combat operations against Ukraine.
The invasion was launched jointly with the Lukashenko regime.
A concert was held in support of the 'annexation' of southeastern Ukraine by Russia, where Ivan Okhlobystin called for a 'holy war' and used the slogan 'Goyda!' associated with Ivan the Terrible's oprichniki.
Evidence of Russian Federation's information aggression against Ukraine through the Internet was presented.
War propaganda is used as one of the directions of information warfare by the aggressor, disseminated through mass media and used by representatives of the country's leadership and political figures close to the leadership.

== Evidence exhibitions and documentation ==

A special exhibition was opened in Kyiv and is located in the memorial complex of the National Museum of the History of Ukraine in the Second World War.
The exhibition features materials evidencing financing by the Russian Federation of terrorists and materials evidencing military training by the Russian Federation of terrorists.
State structures of the Russian Federation recruit these terrorists on the territories of Russia and Ukraine.

== Historical context of Russian aggression ==

The conflict began on August 8, 2008, and Russia attacked Abkhazia in August 2008.
Russia's participation in the war in Syria began in 2015.
The National Council for the Defense of the Ukrainian Language (NKSDU) made a statement on September 20, 2023.

== Ukrainian designation of terrorist groups ==

Ukraine has recognized the organizations 'DNR' and 'LNR' as terrorist groups.

== Ideological origins and key figures ==

Putin calls opponents of the war with Ukraine 'traitors' and a 'fifth column'.
Alexander Dugin has been making demands since September 2008, is referred to as 'Putin's brain', demanded an invasion of Ukraine, demanded an invasion of other countries that were previously part of the USSR, and stated that the Soviet Empire would be restored by various means.
The President of Russia claims that Ukraine was created by Russia and puts forward theses about protecting Russian-speaking people in Donbas from the 'Kyiv regime'.

== Propaganda and media campaigns ==

Scientists use war propaganda.
In April 2014, four Russian television channels were banned from retransmission in Ukraine for inciting interethnic hatred and war propaganda.
Two Russian channels were banned in Lithuania.
A promotional video commissioned by the Russian Ministry of Defense in autumn 2013 appeared online in May 2014.
The video encouraged enlistment in the Russian Armed Forces and faced criticism for promoting war.
The original version of the video was removed from Vimeo and is now only published on YouTube.
Propaganda is used in television programs, including those for children.

== War symbols and public mobilization ==

The symbols 'Z' and 'V' became widely used from late February to early March to support Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
The symbol 'Z' is used more frequently than the symbol 'V' and is often compared to a swastika.
The letter 'Z' is painted on clothing items, buildings, and vehicles, while the state sponsors 'Z' flash mobs on social media.
By the beginning of 2023, the symbols 'Z' and 'V' were losing popularity and are now mainly used by the most radical war supporters.

== Annexation of territories and legal status ==

Russia considers the partially occupied Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Kherson Oblast, Donetsk Oblast, and Luhansk Oblast as its own oblasts, and it considers the Autonomous Republic of Crimea as its own republic and the city of Sevastopol as its own federal city.
The UN General Assembly considers the Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, Kherson, and Luhansk regions to be part of Ukraine.
One hundred and forty-three UN member states consider the Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, Kherson, and Luhansk regions to be part of Ukraine.
Seventy UN member states consider the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and Sevastopol to be part of Ukraine.
Russia and Crimea signed a treaty on March 18, 2014, for the accession of the Republic of Crimea to the Russian Federation, which included the city of Sevastopol.
President Putin signed the treaty with the Russian State Duma.
A transition period was established.
Vladimir Putin issued a decree on March 21, 2014.
The annexed territories account for approximately 15% of Ukraine's total land area.

== International condemnation and diplomatic actions ==

On April 13, 2014, NATO Secretary General Anders Fog Rasmussen made a statement accusing Russia of promoting war and wanting to overthrow the government in Ukraine.
The action was condemned by the United Nations.

== Criminal investigations and domestic repression ==

On July 5, the SBU opened a criminal case against Sergey Glazyev, an advisor to the President of Russia, due to public calls for military conflict with Ukraine.

== Historical context and related conflicts ==

Some of these groups became extreme Islamists, and an estimated 200,000 people died.
Smaller conflicts occurred in North Ossetia and Ingushetia.
The purpose of the war was to retaliate against Georgian military attacks on Russians and Russian peacekeepers in South Ossetia, and Russia made this recognition on August 26, 2008.
The Maidan Revolution took place in Ukraine in 2014, and Russia invaded Ukraine after the Maidan Revolution.

Russia's vast landmass stretches over the easternmost part of Europe and the northernmost part of Asia.
It spans the northernmost edge of Eurasia; and has the world's fourth-longest coastline, of over .
Russia lies between latitudes 41° and 82° N, and longitudes 19° E and 169° W, extending some east to west, and north to south.
Russia, by landmass, is larger than three continents, and has the same surface area as Pluto.

Russia has nine major mountain ranges, and they are found along the southernmost regions, which share a significant portion of the Caucasus Mountains (containing Mount Elbrus, which at is the highest peak in Russia and Europe); the Altai and Sayan Mountains in Siberia; and in the East Siberian Mountains and the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Russian Far East (containing Klyuchevskaya Sopka, which at is the highest active volcano in Eurasia).
The Ural Mountains, running north to south through the country's west, are rich in mineral resources, and form the traditional boundary between Europe and Asia.
The lowest point in Russia and Europe, is situated at the head of the Caspian Sea, where the Caspian Depression reaches some below sea level.

Russia, as one of the world's only three countries bordering three oceans, has links with a great number of seas.
Its major islands and archipelagos include Novaya Zemlya, Franz Josef Land, Severnaya Zemlya, the New Siberian Islands, Wrangel Island, the Kuril Islands (four of which are disputed with Japan), and Sakhalin.
The Diomede Islands, administered by Russia and the United States, are just apart; and Kunashir Island of the Kuril Islands is merely from Hokkaido, Japan.

Russia, home of over 100,000 rivers, has one of the world's largest surface water resources, with its lakes containing approximately one-quarter of the world's liquid fresh water.
Lake Baikal, the largest and most prominent among Russia's fresh water bodies, is the world's deepest, purest, oldest and most capacious fresh water lake, containing over one-fifth of the world's fresh surface water.
Ladoga and Onega in northwestern Russia are two of the largest lakes in Europe.
Russia is second only to Brazil by total renewable water resources.
The Volga in western Russia, widely regarded as Russia's national river, is the longest river in Europe; and forms the Volga Delta, the largest river delta in the continent.
The Siberian rivers of Ob, Yenisey, Lena, and Amur are among the world's longest rivers.

== Location and Political Geography ==

Russia is politically located in Europe, where the most significant part of the country lies.
Moscow, the capital of Russia, is in Europe and is located in the west of Russia.
Vladivostok is located in the east of Russia.
The Russian Kaliningrad region is located between Lithuania and Poland.

== Borders ==

Russia borders Norway, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, the People's Republic of China, Mongolia, and North Korea.
Russia shares a border with Norway, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland via the Kaliningrad Oblast, Ukraine, Georgia, Azerbaijan, and Kazakhstan.

Russia shares a border with China, Mongolia, North Korea, and Belarus.
Russia is bordered by Belarus to the west, and by China, Mongolia, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, and Georgia to the south.
North Korea is located to the extreme southeast of Russia.

== Maritime Borders and Neighbors ==

Russia is separated from Canada, Turkmenistan, Iran, Turkey, and Sweden by a sea or narrow strait.
Russia has a maritime border with Japan in the Sea of Okhotsk and a maritime border with the United States via the Bering Strait.

== Plains and Lowlands ==

Most of Russia consists of extensive plains, and approximately three-quarters of Russia's total area is made up of these plains.
The East European Plain and the West Siberian Plain are the largest plains on Earth.
These plains are mainly steppes in the south and mainly dense forests in the north.
Tundra exists in the East European Plain and is found along the northern coast.
The European Plain is one of these regions, forms the largest part of European Russia, and has the highest population density in that part of Russia.
The European Plain is flat in most of its parts and contains hills that do not exceed 180 meters above sea level.
Forests cover most parts of the region.
The West Siberian Plain is one of the most flat regions in the world, covers more than 2.6 million square kilometers, and has an average elevation of less than 150 meters above sea level.
The West Siberian Plain drains the Ob River system, and the Ob River flows into the Arctic Ocean.
The river drainage is poor in this region, and the poor drainage has led to a high number of marshes.

Plains and valleys dominate the landscape and cover three-quarters of the territory.
Relatively flat areas are predominant in the country, and plains dominate the northern part.
The territory consists mostly of vast plains, which applies to both the European and Asian parts.
These flat areas are covered by tundra, taiga, forests, or steppes depending on latitude.
The East European Plain and the West Siberian Plain are the largest plains on Earth and are divided by the Ural Mountains.
The East European Plain extends from north to south and is also known as the Russian Plain.
The European part of Russia is located on the East European Platform, which forms the foundation of the region.
The foundation of the European part of Russia consists of Precambrian rocks that are igneous and metamorphic in nature.
The West Siberian Plain is very flat, extends to the Yenisei River, and is traversed by extensive swamp landscapes.
The territory between the Ural Mountains and the Yenisei River is occupied by a young platform.
The Valdai Hills are a hilly landscape between Moscow and St.
Petersburg.

More than 70% of Russia's territory is occupied by plains and lowlands.
The western part of Russia is located within the vast East European Plain, which is characterized by an alternation of lowlands and uplands including the Caspian Lowland, the Valdai Upland, and the Central Russian Upland.
The Ural mountain system separates the East European Plain from the West Siberian Lowland, which is part of the West Siberian Platform.
The Siberian platform extends to the Lena River and corresponds mainly to the Central Siberian Plateau.
The Central Siberian Plateau is located to the east of the West Siberian Lowland and gradually transitions into the Central Yakutia Lowland.

== Mountain Ranges ==

The Ural Mountains are an eroded mountain range located in the center with a length of approximately 2000 km that extend from the Arctic Ocean to the border with Kazakhstan. [308,309] The Ural Mountains are a mountain range with an average elevation of 610 meters. [308,309] The central and southern parts of the Ural Mountains are rich in minerals such as iron and copper. [308,309] The central part of the Ural Mountains is more densely populated than other regions due to its population and various industries. [308,309] The Caucasus Mountains border the European plain from the south and are located between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea. The Caucasus Mountains form the border of southern European Russia with Georgia and Azerbaijan.
Mount Elbrus has an elevation of 5,642 meters (18,511 feet) and is 5,642 meters above sea level. Mount Dykh-Tau follows Mount Elbrus in height and has an elevation of 5,205 meters.
The Verkhoyansk Range is located in the eastern parts and in the eastern parts of Eurasia.
Volcanoes on the Kamchatka Peninsula are located in the eastern parts.
The Altai Mountains are this other mountain range.

Mount Elbrus has an elevation of 5,633 meters.
Beluha is a peak in the Altai range with an elevation of 4506 meters.
Klyuchevskaya Sopka is a peak on Kamchatka with an elevation of 4750 meters.
Examples of these ranges include Sikhote-Alin, Verkhoyansk, and Chersky.
This area includes the Caucasus region.
This area includes the foothills along the coasts of the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea.
The Central Mountains are located on the Kamchatka Peninsula.
Eastern Siberian mountain ranges begin to the east of this plain.
The Eastern Siberian mountain ranges include the Verkhoyansk Mountains, the Chersky Range, the Chukotka Mountains, the Koryak Mountains, and the Central Mountains.
Southern Siberian mountain ranges extend eastward from the southern part of the West Siberian Plain.
The Jablonovy Mountains, the Borschtovochne Mountains, the Stanovoy Mountains, and the Stanovoy Range are part of these southern Siberian ranges.

Geologists have divided Russia into five relief regions.
The previous classification of Russia was based on soil and vegetation.

== Rivers and Lakes ==

Surface waters make up 12.4% of Russia, and 84% of these surface waters are concentrated east of the Ural Mountains.
Russia has approximately 2 million lakes and the world's largest reserves of lakes.[7,118,119] Lake Baikal is located in Asia and in Buryatia, has an area of 31,700 square kilometers, and is the largest source of fresh water.[7,1522,1480] Lake Baikal is the main source of fresh water.[1522,1523] The Volga is the most famous of Russia's rivers, is central to Russian history, and played a significant role in Russian history.[1524,12] The Lena River is the longest river in Russia and is 4,400 kilometers long.
The Yenisei River is the most water-rich river in Russia.
The Ural River is a significant river in Russia.
The Don River, the Kama River, and the Oka River are major rivers in Russia.
The Diomede Islands are only three kilometers away from the group of islands owned by the United States.

Lake Baikal is the largest and most important freshwater body in Russia.

The Irtysh is one of the largest rivers.
The Caspian Sea is a closed basin and is included among the major lakes.
The Volga River, the Ural River, and the Terek River flow into the Caspian Sea.

== Coastlines and Ports ==

Russia has many ports on the Baltic Sea, in the Barents Sea to the north, and on the Black Sea to the south, while there are also ports in Vladivostok located on the Pacific Ocean near Japan.
The coastline runs along the Baltic Sea, the Azov Sea, the Black Sea, and the Caspian Sea.

== European Russia ==

The European part includes most of the East European Plain, the northern slopes of the Greater Caucasus Mountains, and the Ural Mountains.
Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Nizhny Novgorod are among the largest cities in Central Russia.

== Siberia and the Central Plateau ==

The Asian part includes Siberia.
The Central Siberian Plateau slopes down towards the Arctic Ocean, has an average elevation of 610 meters, and increases in elevation as one moves south.
Deep rivers cut through the surface of the Central Siberian Plateau, while mountains such as the Sayan and Baikal ranges rise to over 3,350 meters along the southern edge of the plateau.
Dense coniferous forests cover most of the region, which contains rich mineral deposits [310,312].
Krasnoyarsk and Irkutsk are one of the most important cities in the region [310,312].

== Eastern Siberia and the Far East ==

The Asian part includes the Far East.
Eastern Siberia Highlands consist mostly of mountains and barren plateaus, and the mountains in Eastern Siberia Highlands rise to 3,000 meters [313,314].
These mountains form part of a mountain range system extending along the eastern coast of Asia and along some islands adjacent to the Asian coast [313,314].
The Verkhoyansk mountain range is located on the eastern side.
There are 25 active volcanoes in the Kamchatka Peninsula, and many active volcanoes are located in the Kamchatka Peninsula [313,314].
The highest volcano in the Kamchatka Peninsula reaches an elevation of 4,750 meters [313,314].
The harsh climate of the region prevents the exploitation of mineral wealth [313,314].
Vladivostok is one of the most important cities in the region, and Khabarovsk is one of the most important cities in the region [313,314].

== Rivers ==

The Volga River originates from the Valdai Hills west of Moscow and flows for 3,531 kilometers before emptying into the Caspian Sea.[315,316] The Lena River is 4,400 kilometers long.[317,318] The Don River flows into the Black Sea and is connected to the Volga River by a canal.
The Ural River flows into the Caspian Sea.
The Northern Dvina River exists in Russia.
The Volga, Don, and Dnieper rivers flow through the European part of Russia.
The source of the Volga river is in northwestern Russia.
The Volga river empties into the Caspian Sea.

The three rivers are the Ob, the Lena, and the Yenisei.
The Ob is located in western Siberia.
The region covers the western coasts of the Arctic Ocean.
The Volga region covers the Ural economic region.
The Volga River played an exceptional role in the formation of the Volga economic region.
The Volga River is a major geographical feature of the Volga economic region.
Most major cities are located on the banks of the Volga River.

== Lakes and Inland Waters ==

The Caspian Sea is the largest lake in Russia and the largest inland body of water in the world, and it is a saltwater sea.
There are 200,000 lakes in Russia.
Lake Ladoga is located near St.
Petersburg and has a surface area of 17,703 square kilometers.
Lake Baikal is located in Siberia and has a depth of 1,620 meters.

== Mountains and Volcanoes ==

More than 5,000 caves were discovered and studied in the Caucasus, Altai, and Ural regions.
Mount Elbrus is the highest point in Russia and Europe at 5,642 meters.

== Cultural and Natural Monuments ==

Some of these monuments have been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
There are ancient pagan stone idols in the region that date back two thousand years.

== Regional Development and Resources ==

The marshes are particularly common in the northern parts of the region.
The region is experiencing significant development due to its oil and natural gas resources.

== Relief and Mountain Ranges ==

The terrain is predominantly flat, with the Ural Mountains forming an exception and a border between European Russia and Siberia.
Mount Elbrus is 5,642 meters high.
One of the largest plains in the world, the West Siberian Plain, lies east of the Ural Mountains.
Altai is the highest region, has numerous glaciers in the west, and extends across the territory of four countries.
The Sayan mountain range extends eastward from the Altai, with the Eastern Sayan peaking at the Mongolian border.
Plateaus alternate with long mountain ridges in the area east of Lake Baikal, including the Vitim Plateau, the Aldan Plateau, the Jablonovy Range, and the Stanovoy Range.
This landscape extends to the Sea of Okhotsk.
The Chukchi Mountains traverse the Chukotka Peninsula and are the easternmost mountain range.
The Koryak Mountains stretch southeast along the Bering Sea.

The Koryak Mountains transition into a mountain range on the Kamchatka Peninsula, which is separated from a belt of high and active volcanoes by the depression of the Kamchatka River.
A belt of high and active volcanoes lines the Pacific coast.
Russia is covered by plains.

Most of Russia consists of vast plains, with the southern part mostly comprising steppe plains.

== Rivers and Drainage ==

The West Siberian Plain is traversed by major rivers, including the Ob, the Irtysh, and the Yenisei.
The Yenisey is the largest river in the Russian Federation [cite: 746], and the Ob and the Irtysh together form the seventh longest river in the world [cite: 746].
Three rivers belong to the Arctic Ocean basin: the Severnaya Dvina, the Pechora, the Lena, the Yana, and the Kolyma.

These rivers are characterized by enormous discharge volumes and rank among the largest in the world by water discharge and drainage basin size [cite: 448].
They experience particularly violent spring floods when summer arrives that move waters previously trapped in ice, and the river is very wide in some places.

Lawrence River's lower reaches.

The total length of rivers in Russia is 8 million kilometers, and almost all of them have a mixed type of feeding.
Russian rivers belong to five main basins: Black Sea, Caspian, Arctic, Baltic, and Pacific.

== Time Zones ==

The time zones in Russia range from UTC+2 to UTC+12 and the country has the largest number of consecutive time zones in the world.
Moscow and St.
Petersburg are located in the Moscow Time zone, which is 3 hours ahead of UTC.
Only two regions in Russia are divided by time zones: the Sakhalin Oblast and Yakutia.
The western part of the Sakhalin Oblast uses Vladivostok time while the eastern part uses Srednekolymsk time.
The western part of Yakutia uses Yakutsk time, the central part uses Vladivostok time, and the eastern part uses Srednekolymsk time.
One such line is the boundary between Moscow Time and Yekaterinburg Time, one such line is the boundary between Yekaterinburg Time and Krasnoyarsk Time, and one such line is the boundary between Krasnoyarsk Time and Yakutsk Time.
Daylight saving time was abolished in Russia between 2011 and 2014, during which period summer time was observed year-round across Russia.
Russia faced sustained criticism from the public and returned to standard time on October 26, 2014.

Russia has 11 time zones in its southern part and 7 time zones north of the 65th parallel.
The eastern part of Chukotka lies in the Western Hemisphere.
The International Date Line was shifted eastward, moving the line to the border with the United States.
The existing time zone division creates three lines where the local time changes by two hours instead of one when crossed, one such line being the boundary between Vladivostok Time and Kamchatka Time.
The actual astronomical time difference in Russia reaches 11 hours and 25 minutes.
Only nine time zones are used for practical reasons.
The Russian government decided to reduce the number of time zones to promote economic development.
The number of time zones was reduced from 11 to 9.
The number of time zones was even reduced to 5.

== Major Landscapes ==

Russia is divided geographically into eight major landscapes.
This division runs mainly in a west-east direction.

== East European Plain ==

The East European Plain occupies most of European Russia and consists of vast lowlands interrupted by weakly structured ridges.
Few elevations reach heights greater than 300 meters, though the relief in Karelia and on the Kola Peninsula is more differentiated in the north.
Karelia and the Kola Peninsula belong to the Baltic Shield geologically.
The maximum height is reached in the Chibins, which are located on the central Kola Peninsula and reach 1,191 meters.
The East European Plain transitions into the Caspian Depression in the south.
A chain of terminal moraines formed during the last Ice Age starts from the border area with Belarus, runs north of Moscow, reaches the Arctic coast, and is located west of the Pechora River.
The region north of the terminal moraine chain consists of many lakes and many swamps.

== West Siberian Lowland ==

The West Siberian Lowland is a vast plain that extends east of the Ural Mountains as far as the Yenisei River.
The area is extremely flat and consists of extensive wetland landscapes.

== Central Siberian Uplands ==

The North Siberian Lowland adjoins the Central Siberian Mountainous Region to the north, which rises northward toward the Taimyr Peninsula.
The Central Siberian Mountainous region extends east of the Yenisei River as far as the Lena River.
The terrain of the Central Siberian Mountainous region is rolling with an average elevation between 500 and 700 meters.
The Putorana Mountains are located in the northwest of this region and have a maximum height of 1701 meters.

== Southern and Eastern Siberian Mountains ==

Further mountain ranges continue eastward in southern Central and Eastern Siberia and extend to the Pacific Ocean.
This group of mountains is known as the Southern Siberian Mountains.
The Eastern Siberian Mountains are located east of the Lena and Aldan rivers and consist of branched mountain chains.
The Verkhoyansk Range, the Chersky Range, and the Kolyma Range are among these higher mountains.
These mountains reach heights between approximately 2300 and 3200 meters.

== Siberian Lowlands ==

The Central Yakutian Lowland includes the lower Lena River valley, the lower Viluy River valley, and the lower Aldan River valley.
The depression covers an area of approximately 1 million square kilometers and is bounded by the Central Siberian Mountains to the west and the Eastern Siberian Mountains to the east.
The vast East Siberian Lowland is located south of the East Siberian Sea and lies exclusively north of the Arctic Circle.
The landscape includes the lower reaches of the Jana River, the lower reaches of the Indigirka River, and the lower reaches of the Kolyma River.
The western part is the Jana-Indigirka Lowland and the eastern part is the Kolyma Lowland.
The East Siberian Lowland borders the East Siberian Mountains to the south.

== Volcanic Regions ==

There are approximately 160 volcanoes on the Kamchatka Peninsula, which contains a volcanic mountain range that continues southward onto the Kuril Islands.
There are approximately 100 volcanoes.

== Hydrography Overview ==

Russia has 120,000 rivers and streams and nearly two million lakes.
The forest belt covers two-thirds of the area and acts as a huge water reservoir together with the precipitation surplus.

== The Volga River ==

The Volga is the most important river and flows exclusively within Russia.
It drains a large part of the East European Plain and has two tributaries named the Kama and the Oka.
The Volga flows 3,534 kilometers to the Caspian Sea in the southeast and connects Eastern Europe with Central Asia.
The North Russian Upland forms a watershed that separates the Volga basin from the White Sea and the Barents Sea, which are located to the north.

== The Dnieper River ==

The Dnieper holds great significance for Slavic states.
The river originates west of Moscow, flows through Belarus and Ukraine, and empties into the Black Sea.
The Dnieper is indirectly connected to the Memel via the Oginskaya Canal System and is connected to the Polish rivers Bug and Vistula via the Dnieper-Bug Canal.

== The Ob and Irtysh Rivers ==

The longest rivers in Russia are located in far-eastern Russia.
The Ob River originates in the southern Siberian Altai and flows into the Arctic Ocean.
The river is over 4,300 km long, and its source stream is the Katun.
The river forms one of Asia's longest river systems together with the Irtysh, and the total length of this river system is over 5,400 km.

== The Yenisei River ==

The Yenisei river system has a longer flow path, and its water flows partially from Mongolia, north through West Siberia, and to the Arctic Ocean.
The Angara is the only outflow of Lake Baikal.
The Yenisei River discharges approximately 600 cubic kilometers of water annually into the Arctic Ocean.
The Yenisei has the highest discharge volume of all Russian rivers.

== The Lena River ==

The Lena River is approximately 4,300 kilometers long and is the longest river that flows entirely within Russia.
Its drainage basin is located entirely within Russia, and it originates only 5 kilometers away from Lake Baikal.
The river initially flows in a northeasterly direction and bends north after the Aldan joins it.
It empties into an extensive delta that empties into the Laptev Sea, a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean.

== Other Arctic and Far Eastern Rivers ==

The Chatanga, Kolyma, and Indigirka are important rivers that flow into the Arctic Ocean.
The Amur is an important river system.

== Size, Extent, and Location ==

Russia's geographical location gave it a bridge position between Europe and Asia, and the lack of natural borders contributed to Russia's historical development.
The country has an area of 17,075,400 square kilometers, which is equivalent to slightly more than one-ninth of the planet's landmass.
The Asian part is significantly larger in area than the European part, with the European part accounting for 23% of Russia's total area and the Asian part accounting for 77%.
Russia extends approximately 9000 km from east to west and approximately 2500 to 4000 km from north to south.

== Coastline and Time Zones ==

Russia has a coastline length of 37,653 km.

== Major Mountain Ranges ==

Approximately 40% of Russia's land area is covered by mountains.
The Ural Mountains do not constitute a real barrier due to their low height.
The highest peak of the Urals, Narodnaja, is 1895 meters high.
The West Siberian Lowland is bounded to the southeast by the Central Siberian Mountains, which extend as far as the Lena River and slope down into the narrow North Siberian Lowland in the north.
The Sayan Mountains belong to the Central Siberian Mountain range.
The Altai Mountains are the highest mountain range in Siberia and are located in the border region between Russia, Kazakhstan, China, and Mongolia.
The East Siberian Mountains rise east of the Lena River, branch into various mountain ranges including the Verkhoyansk Range and the Chersky Range, and reach heights of nearly 3000 meters.

== Volcanic Activity ==

The Kamchatka region is a volcanic area where the Kamchatka Peninsula has 160 volcanoes that reach heights of up to 4,688 meters, and 29 of these volcanoes are still active.
The Right Kamchatka system is a high-grade terrigenous geosynclinal complex that was incorporated into the gneiss-granite and schist basement, and Paleogene-Neogene rock formations were deposited on top of the system after folding.
The eastern region has characteristics of a modern volcanic zone and contains 28 active volcanoes.
Klyuchevskaya Sopka has an elevation of 4750 meters.
The Kuril Islands are located on the eastern border of the Kamchatka region and are part of a volcanic area.

== The Caspian Sea ==

The Caspian Sea is the largest inland body of water in the world with a surface area of 386,400 square kilometers.

The Caspian Sea has no outflow, and water escapes only through evaporation.
The climate in the region is dry, and evaporation leads to salt crystallization in the Caspian Sea.

== Vegetation and Landscapes ==

European Russia is defined as the part of the country located west of the Ural Mountains, though this definition is arbitrary.
Moving from north to south, European Russia presents a succession of landscapes where the northernmost and coldest part is dominated by tundra.
South of the tundra are coniferous forests, followed by mixed forests of deciduous and coniferous trees, then meadows, and finally the southernmost semi-desert steppe near the Caspian Sea.
Vegetation changes follow climate changes, with tundra vegetation found near the northern coasts and plains consisting primarily of dense forests in the north.
Siberia is the part of Russia located east of the Ural Mountains and presents the same succession of landscapes as European Russia.
Taiga predominates in Siberia, where it is a more or less sparse forest composed mainly of conifers.
A significant portion of Arctic and sub-Arctic regions are located within Russia.

== European and Asian Division ==

One quarter of Russia's territory is located in Europe, while the remaining three quarters are located in Asia.
Russia includes the Kaliningrad Oblast exclave and is traditionally divided between European Russia and Asian Russia.
The territory is usually divided into European Russia and Asian Russia by the course of the Ural River, the northern coast of the Caspian Sea, and the Kuma-Manych depression.
The most commonly followed boundary line starts from the Arctic Ocean, follows the eastern edge of the Ural Mountains, continues along the course of the Ural River, proceeds along the northwestern coast of the Caspian Sea, goes through the Kuma-Manych depression, and finally reaches the mouth of the Don River in the Sea of Azov.

== Relief and Geological Features ==

Glaciation was one of the most powerful factors in shaping the current Russian territory, though these signs are not visible in the extreme southern zones.
Most of the European part is composed of plains that are often interrupted by very low elevations, including the Central Russian Upland, the Moscow Plateau, and the Volga Uplands.
Western Siberia is composed of plains, and the western Siberian plain is an extremely flat area where this extreme flatness causes major drainage problems for water.
Water is not abundant in this region due to its climatic characteristics.
Central Siberia practically coincides with the vast plateau of the same name, which covers nearly four million square kilometers and has its highest point located at its extreme north.
Eastern Siberia is a predominantly mountainous region where the highest peaks approach those of Kamchatka.
The far east is geologically very rugged and is located on the boundary between the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates, which includes the Chersky Mountains and the Verkhoyansk Mountains.
The Russian Far East is also located on the boundary between the Eurasian and Pacific tectonic plates, where the Pacific plate subducts beneath the Eurasian plate to create island arcs including the Kuril Islands.

== Lakes and Water Bodies ==

The two largest lakes, the Caspian Sea and Lake Baikal, are exceptions to the rule and are situated at the southern borders.
These lakes are generally shallow on average due to the weak undulation of the terrain.
Lake Ladoga, Lake Onega, Lake Il'men, and Lake Chudskoye (Lago dei Ciudi) are among these lakes.
Extensive swampy areas exist in the vast Siberian plains.
Artificial reservoirs, which were created by damming major rivers, are very important in the Russian landscape, and some of these reservoirs have worldwide significance.

== Geological Structure ==

The Kuma-Manych Depression divides Russia, and these geographical features separate the European part of Russia from the Asian part.
The European part of Russia's territory is located on the East European Platform, which is based on pre-Cambrian igneous rocks and metamorphic rocks.
The Western Siberian young platform occupies the area between the Ural Mountains and the Yenisei River.
The eastern part of the Yenisei is an ancient Siberian platform that extends to the Lena River and generally corresponds to the Central Siberian Plateau.
The Siberian Platform is of eparchean age.
The Ural-Mongolian epipaleozoic platform belt separates two ancient platforms, and its structure includes folding zones such as the Rifeian folding zone and the Baikal folding zone.
The Altai Mountains, the epipaleozoic belt of the Ural-Mongolian region, the northeastern part of the Pacific mineralized zone, and the outer zone of the Mediterranean Sea mineralized zone are included in the mineralized regions of Russia.
Mineralized areas contain the main reserves of metal ores.
The highest mountains of the Caucasus are bounded by young sedimentary rocks.

The Yenisei-Sayan-Baikal region covers the Siberian platform and consists of the Rifean and Baikal orogenic belts.
The Salair, Caledonian, and Hercynian folding zones are present in the belt.
Ancient pre-Rifeyan massifs, Mesozoic folded sections, Cenozoic folded sections, and modern tectonically active zones are located within this belt.
The Cis-Ural foreland exists along the boundary with the East European Platform and is filled with Permian strata.
The northern part of the Cis-Ural foreland contains coal deposits, while the central part of the foreland basin contains potash deposits.

== Mineral Resources ==

Diamonds are associated with kimberlite pipes.
Major coal, potassium salt, oil, and gas deposits in Russia are associated with the Siberian platform cover.
The Norilsk copper-nickel deposits are associated with intrusive bodies of a basin.
The Verkhoyansk-Chukotka region contains gold, tungsten, and mercury deposits.
The gold deposits are associated with the Tserdym lower sandstone intrusion.
Major coal deposits are covered by the Predverkhoyanskaya terrace.
The Zyryan deposit is covered by melassa.

Russia borders the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea to the southwest.
Russia borders the Arctic Ocean to the north.
Russia borders China, North Korea, Mongolia, and Kazakhstan to the southeast.

== Mountain Ranges and Relief ==

Mount Elbrus is 5,642 meters high and has an elevation of 5,642 meters.[11,1421,1422][3960,3961]
The Caspian Depression reaches approximately 29 meters below sea level.
The Caucasus Mountains run in a west-east direction and the Caucasus region extends north of the Greater Caucasus mountain range.[3960,3961]
The Ural Mountains separate the western Siberian Plain from the plain area of European Russia.[3960,3961]

== Regional Geography ==

European Russia extends from the western border to the Ural Mountains and is a vast plain.
The Don River and the Dnieper River flow through European Russia.
The Caucasus region is located in southern European Russia, lies between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea, and is a vast steppe area.
The western part of the country lies on the Baltic Shield and on the Russian Platform.
Russia borders Estonia to the west and Latvia to the west.
The European part of Russia constitutes a certain percentage of the total territory.
Siberia extends from the Ural Mountains to the Pacific coast.
The Ural Mountains contain important oil reserves.
The country consists largely of vast steppes in the south and deep coniferous forests in the north.
The part of Central Asia located in Russia consists of desert, steppe, and mountains, and some parts of this area lie below sea level.
The Kaliningrad Oblast is a separated region.

Yakutia and Chukotka are located in Siberia or the Far East region.
Russia was originally a European country.

== Lakes and Surface Waters ==

Surface waters occupy 12.4% of Russia's territory, and 84% of these surface waters are located east of the Ural Mountains.
Lake Baikal is located in the eastern part of the country, has an area of approximately 31,700 square kilometers, and a depth of 1,642 meters.
Lake Onega is the second largest lake in Europe.

== Soils and Vegetation Zones ==

Soils in Russia are arranged zonally on the plains of Russia.
Soils are formed on the islands of the Arctic Ocean and on the Taymyr Peninsula coast, where they are weakly developed, primitive, and arctic soils.
A tundra zone is located further south, where acidic tundra soils predominate and are usually strongly gleyed.
The transition zone between forest and tundra has specific soil types, including characteristic tundra gleysols, weakly podzolic soils, and gleyed taiga-permafrost soils.
Approximately 65% of Russia's territory is within the forest zone.
In the northern part of Russia, the soils are podzolic, while to the east of the Yenisei River, taiga-permafrost soils form.
There are many swamps in the taiga subzone, which is particularly prevalent in Western Siberia, and most of these swamps are raised bogs (oligotrophic).

Forest areas are often swampy.
The region south of the taiga is located on the East European Plain and has podzolic-forest soils.
The forest-steppe zone lies to the south and has gray forest soils.
Dark chestnut soils are characteristic of the steppe zone, which is also characterized by extremely fertile chernozem soils.
Chernozem soils have a powerful humus horizon that contains between 4% and 10% humus.

== Major Cities and Settlements ==

Saint Petersburg is the northernmost city in the world with a population of over one million people, Murmansk is the largest city in the world located north of the Arctic Circle, Norilsk is the largest Arctic city in Asia, and Sabetta is the largest settlement north of 70 degrees latitude.
Omsk is a major city in Russia.
Approximately 50 of these volcanoes are active.
Russia borders Norway to the west and Finland to the west.

== Maritime Borders and Proximity ==

Russia shares a maritime border with Japan, the United States, and Turkey.
The length of the maritime border with the United States is 49 kilometers, and the length of the maritime border with Japan is 194.3 kilometers.
38,808 km of the Russian Federation's border is a maritime border.
The Diomede Islands are located only 3 kilometers apart.
Kunashir Island is approximately 20 kilometers away from Hokkaido.

== Extent and Extremes ==

Cape Fligely, located on Rudolf Island in the Franz Josef Land archipelago, is the northernmost point of Europe and Eurasia at a latitude of 81°49' North.
The northernmost mainland point is Cape Chelyuskin on the Taymyr Peninsula, situated at 77°43' North latitude.
The southernmost point lies southwest of Mount Bazardüzü, which is on the border between Dagestan and Azerbaijan.
The Curonian Spit is located in the Gdańsk Bay, part of the Baltic Sea, at a longitude of 19°38' East.
Ratmanov Island is the easternmost point at 169°00' west longitude, while the easternmost continental point is Cape Dezhnev on the Chukchi Peninsula at 169 degrees and 40 minutes west longitude.

== Geology and Relief ==

The main geological features of Russia are platforms and folded regions.
The European part of Russia is located on the East European Platform, the foundation of which consists of Precambrian rocks.
The territory between the Ural Mountains and the Yenisei River is occupied by the young West Siberian Platform.
In terms of relief, the ancient Siberian Platform corresponds to the Central Siberian Plateau.
Oil, natural gas, and coal deposits are found in the edge parts of the platforms.
The Baltic Shield, the Ural-Mongolian Paleozoic Folded Belt, the northwestern part of the Pacific Folded Belt, and a small section of the outer zone of the Mediterranean Folded Belt belong to Russia.
The Caucasus Mountains belong to younger folded regions.
Folded regions contain the main reserves of metal ores.

== Plains and Mountain Ranges ==

The majority of the European part of Russia is located within the East European Plain, which encompasses most of the European territory of Russia.
The southern part of the European portion of Russia features the northern slopes of the Caucasus, while the northwestern part features the Khibiny Mountains.
The West Siberian Plain is located east of the Ural Mountains and is bordered by mountains in southern Siberia to the south.
The Altai Mountains, Sayan Mountains, Baikal Mountains, and Transbaikal Mountains are part of the southern Siberian mountain range bordering the plain.
The Central Siberian Plateau is located between the Yenisei and the Lena rivers.
Mountain ranges and highlands of Northeast Asia are located between the Lena River and the Pacific Ocean.
Mount Elbrus has an elevation of 5,633 meters.
The Verkhoyansk Range is an example of an eastern mountain range, and volcanoes on Kamchatka are an example of eastern mountain features.
The Ural Mountains are a famous mountain range.

== Area and Spatial Characteristics ==

Russia has an area of 17,098,246 square kilometers and 6,601,670 square miles, a measurement that refers to internationally recognized borders.
Russia covers nearly one-ninth of Earth's continental land area.
Russia's territory extends across the entire northern part of Asia and covers 40% of Europe [126,4385,4386,4387,4388,4389].
Most of Russia's land consists of vast plains located in both Europe and Asia.
This region is known as Siberia, which has large distances and vast spaces.
The plains are primarily steppes to the south, while tundra exists along the northern coast.
Most of the southern part of this region has more diverse landscapes and climates.
Economic activity in Russia is lower per unit area compared to most other regions.
Physical diversity per unit area in Russia is lower than in most other regions.

== Territorial Composition ==

The most common practical way to describe Russia is to divide it into two parts.
One part is the main territory, which borders large groups of islands or offshore islands.
The other part is a separate region known as Kaliningrad, which is located in the southeastern part of the Baltic Sea.

== Rivers and Water Bodies ==

Many large rivers flow through plains and reach the ocean.
The Volga River flows into the Caspian Sea, is the longest inland river in the world, and has the largest discharge of any inland river in the world.
Khabarovsk is located at the confluence of the Ussuri River and the Amur River.
Moscow is located on the Moskva River.

== Kazan Kremlin ==

The Kazan Kremlin is the oldest part of the city of Kazan and is a complex of architectural, historical, and archaeological monuments.
There are three residential sites on the Kremlin grounds that belong to different historical periods, with the first settlement dating to the 12th and 13th centuries, the second to the 14th and 15th centuries, and the third to the 15th and 16th centuries.
The Kremlin is a fortress made of white stone where the office of the President of the Republic of Tatarstan is located.
The Kremlin area is rectangular in shape, repeats the form of the hill it is located on, and extends from the north-west to the south-east from the Kazanka River in the north-west to Red Square (May 1st Square) in the south-east.
The Volga River is located on the left bank.
The site has been included in the UNESCO World Heritage List effective since 2000.
The Blagoveshchensky Church is the oldest historical architectural monument located in the Kremlin grounds.

== Red Square ==

Vasily Блаженный Church and the Spasskaya Tower are located in Red Square, which was built in the 15th century and has an area of approximately 73,000 square meters.
The Mausoleum of Vladimir Lenin is located in this square.
Numerous demonstrations, parades, and rallies have historically taken place in the square, and executions have taken place on the square.
Soviet troops held a victory parade in the square.
Matias Rast, a German amateur pilot, landed on May 28, 1987, using a Cessna aircraft to land in Red Square after flying from Germany to Iceland, then from Iceland to Norway, then from Norway to Finland, and crossing the airspace border from Finland.
No radar detected the aircraft at that time.

The size of Russia and the remoteness of many of its areas from the sea result in the dominance of the humid continental climate throughout most of the country, except for the tundra and the extreme southwest.
Mountain ranges in the south and east obstruct the flow of warm air masses from the Indian and Pacific oceans, while the European Plain spanning its west and north opens it to influence from the Atlantic and Arctic oceans.
Most of northwest Russia and Siberia have a subarctic climate, with extremely severe winters in the inner regions of northeast Siberia (mostly Sakha, where the Northern Pole of Cold is located with the record low temperature of ), and more moderate winters elsewhere.
Russia's vast coastline along the Arctic Ocean and the Russian Arctic islands have a polar climate.

The coastal part of Krasnodar Krai on the Black Sea, most notably Sochi, and some coastal and interior strips of the North Caucasus possess a humid subtropical climate with mild and wet winters.
In many regions of East Siberia and the Russian Far East, winter is dry compared to summer; while other parts of the country experience more even precipitation across seasons.
Winter precipitation in most parts of the country usually falls as snow.
The westernmost parts of Kaliningrad Oblast and some parts in the south of Krasnodar Krai and the North Caucasus have an oceanic climate.
The region along the Lower Volga and Caspian Sea coast, as well as some southernmost slivers of Siberia, possess a semi-arid climate.

Throughout much of the territory, there are only two distinct seasons, winter and summer; as spring and autumn are usually brief.
The coldest month is January (February on the coastline); the warmest is usually July.
Great ranges of temperature are typical.
In winter, temperatures get colder both from south to north and from west to east.
Summers can be quite hot, even in Siberia.
Climate change in Russia is causing more frequent wildfires, and thawing the country's large expanse of permafrost.

== Climate Zones and Classification ==

Four climate zones are found in the Russian Federation and range from north to south.
The northernmost zone is the Arctic zone, the next zone moving south is the Subarctic zone, the third zone is the temperate zone, and the southernmost zone is the Subtropical zone.
Climate zones in Russia run largely parallel to lines of latitude.
More than half of the country is located north of 60 degrees latitude.
The climate types are Dfb, Dfa, Dwb, and Dwa according to the Köppen classification.

Russia is essentially divided from north to south based on different climate zones.

Russia's climate is moderate in summer, with summer temperatures ranging from 1 to 25 degrees Celsius above zero, while the climate is cold in autumn and winter temperatures range from 0 to 50 degrees Celsius below zero.
Northern regions and areas near the North Pole have long, cold winters and short, relatively cool summers.

== Permafrost and Hydrology ==

This phenomenon is called permafrost, where water stagnates on the surface to create huge swamps that are a recurring landscape in Siberia.
