== Precipitation Patterns and Snow Cover ==

Precipitation in Russia is characterized by a summer maximum, with annual precipitation in the European part of Russia and Western Siberia at 600 mm.
Coastal areas and high mountain regions receive relatively large amounts of precipitation, where levels reach up to 1000 mm in the Far East, up to 2000 mm in the Altai and North Caucasus, and up to 1000 mm in high mountains.
Annual precipitation in the Urals is 1400 mm, while precipitation reaches up to 700 mm in the European plains.
Precipitation levels decrease in the Asian part of Russia, where the annual precipitation is approximately 200 mm in Central and Eastern Siberia and below 200 mm on the Trans-Caspian Lowland.
The annual precipitation is over 600 mm at the western and eastern edges, and rainfall is drizzly in very cold regions.
The snow cover period on the East European Plain lasts 40 to 200 days per year, while the snow cover period in Siberia lasts 120 to 250 days per year.
Snow cover persists for one month over the Black Sea and for nine months on the coasts of the Arctic Ocean.

== Permafrost and Hydrological Effects ==

The duration of negative temperatures causes permanent snow cover in some regions, which cover 10 million square kilometers and constitute almost 60% of the country's territory.
The total area covered by permafrost is approximately 9 million square kilometers.
The thickness of multi-year permafrost varies from south to north, ranging from 1 meter in the south to hundreds of meters in the north.
Meltwater from southern rivers cannot drain away while northern rivers are still frozen, causing large areas to flood in the spring as a result of the continental climate.

== Regional Climate Characteristics ==

The climate in western Russia is temperate continental, while the climate in eastern Russia becomes extreme continental.
Seasonal temperature differences are large in the Asian part of Russia, and daily temperature differences are large in the Asian part of Russia.
The climate in the Russian Far East is moderate.
Winter is long and snowy, spring is temperate, summer is short and hot, and autumn is rainy.
BWk is a desert climate that has an average annual temperature of less than 18 degrees and is found in a very small area adjacent to the BSk climate.
Cfa is a humid subtropical climate.

== Environmental Impacts and Human Activity ==

Russia's geography is deeply related to its continental climate, which is due to the frequency of forest fires.
In winter, south-westerly winds prevail in parts of Europe, southerly winds prevail over the largest territory of Siberia, and north-westerly winds prevail in the far east.
Low-pressure fields in the north are influenced by cold air from Arctic and Atlantic regions.
Most greenhouse gas emissions in Russia are caused by fossil fuels.[1441,1959,1960,2513,2514,2515,2516,2517,2518,2519,2520,2521,2522,2523,2524,2525,2526] Oymyakon is located in Siberia above the Arctic Circle and is known as the coldest inhabited place on Earth.

== Climate Zones and Continental Gradients ==

The majority of Russia's territory is located in the temperate zone, and the country has climate zones arranged in a latitudinal direction from north to south.
Latitudinal zonality is most clearly manifested on plains, while the European part of the country has the most complete spectrum of natural zones.
The climate of the country changes in a meridional direction, becoming increasingly continental as one moves east, which causes the number of natural zones within a single latitudinal interval to decrease significantly.
Russia has several climate belts distinguished by the heat supply of the climate, including the subpolar climate zone and the temperate climate zone.
In addition to the division into landscape zones, there is a division into physical-geographical sectors that differ from each other by atmospheric circulation and by continentality of climate.
Eastern Europe and Western Siberia are examples of such physical-geographical sectors.
Large parts of the world's arctic and subarctic climate areas are located in Russia, with Siberia and Russia's Arctic islands serving as examples of such areas.
Southwestern Russia has a warm-tempered climate.

The climate begins with a maritime type on the extreme northwest, transitions to a sharply continental climate in Siberia, and further transitions to a humid monsoon climate in the Far East.
These factors led to a humid continental and subarctic climate type that is common in European Russia and Asian Russia, with the exception of the southeastern polar region.
Most of Russia lies within the North Temperate Zone.
The western part of the East European Plain has a milder climate and belongs to a temperate continental humid climate.
Continental climate strengthens gradually from west to east.
Most of Siberia belongs to a subarctic coniferous forest climate.
The Pacific coast has a monsoon climate.

== Precipitation and Aridity ==

Interior continental areas are the driest, as inland regions experience the least rainfall and are drier than coastal or other regions.
The semi-desert zone is located further south on the territory of the Caspian Lowland.
Annual precipitation ranges from 150 to 2000 millimeters.

== Permafrost and Frozen Ground ==

Permafrost covers 65% of Russia's territory.
It is found in the northern regions of the European part of Russia, in Siberia, and in the Russian Far East.
Permafrost is widespread in many areas of Siberia and in many areas of the Russian Far East.

== Soils and Semi-Desert Regions ==

Light chestnut soils, brown soils, and saline soils (solonchaks) are found in this area.

== Oceanic Influence and Sea Ice ==

Russia's coastal waters have long freezing periods, and sea ice in the Arctic Ocean is gradually melting.
Siberia has a harsh climate, and the cold originating from Siberia spreads across a large part of Asia.

Russia, owing to its gigantic size, has diverse ecosystems, including polar deserts, tundra, forest tundra, taiga, mixed and broadleaf forest, forest steppe, steppe, semi-desert, and subtropics.
About half of Russia's territory is forested, and it has the world's largest area of forest, which sequester some of the world's highest amounts of carbon dioxide.

Russian biodiversity includes 12,500 species of vascular plants, 2,200 species of bryophytes, about 3,000 species of lichens, 7,000–9,000 species of algae, and 20,000–25,000 species of fungi.
Russian fauna is composed of 320 species of mammals, over 732 species of birds, 75 species of reptiles, about 30 species of amphibians, 343 species of freshwater fish (high endemism), approximately 1,500 species of saltwater fishes, 9 species of cyclostomata, and approximately 100–150,000 invertebrates (high endemism).
Approximately 1,100 rare and endangered plant and animal species are included in the Russian Red Data Book.

Russia's entirely natural ecosystems are conserved in nearly 15,000 specially protected natural territories of various statuses, occupying more than 10% of the country's total area.
They include 45 biosphere reserves, 64 national parks, and 101 nature reserves.
Although in decline, the country still has many ecosystems which are still considered intact forest; mainly in the northern taiga areas, and the subarctic tundra of Siberia.
Russia had a Forest Landscape Integrity Index mean score of 9.02 in 2019, ranking 10th out of 172 countries; and the first ranked major nation globally.

== Zonal Geography and Climate ==

Russia can be divided into four zones based on soil conditions and vegetation that form wide and broad belts across the country from north to south with no clear transitional areas between them.
The northernmost zone is the tundra zone, followed to the south by the forest zone, then the steppe zone, and finally the southernmost semi-desert and mountain zone.
The tundra zone is located in the far north of Russia and has an extremely cold climate with a short summer and a long winter where the soil freezes during the winter and permafrost soil covers half of the zone.
The forest zone is located south of the tundra zone and has a more moderate climate with higher humidity.
The steppe zone is located south of the forest zone, while the semi-desert and mountain zone is located in the extreme south of Russia.
The population is low in these arid areas.

The semi-desert and mountain zone is characterized by diverse soil and climate due to varied topography.

== Tundra Ecosystem ==

The tundra consists of treeless plains.
Vegetation consists of short shrubs, dwarf trees, and mosses.
Reindeer, arctic foxes, wild rabbits, ptarmigan, and snow geese live in these areas.

== Forest and Taiga Ecosystems ==

The northern part of the forest zone is known as the taiga, where coniferous trees are abundant and include spruce, pine, and fir.
The soil in the taiga is podzol soil, which is poor quality and unsuitable for agriculture.
The southern part of the forest zone is characterized by tree diversity, featuring conifers, willows, birches, maples, and oaks.
In some areas of the southern forest zone, the soil is suitable for agriculture.
Forests in central Russia, on the slopes of the Caucasus mountains, in Siberia, and in the Russian Far East are rich in animals and birds.
The Far East region in the Primorye and Khabarovsk regions is characterized by forests, rivers, and mountain slopes.

Russia contains one-fifth of the world's forests.
Wild animals and rare plants exist in these regions, where pine trees and cypress trees grow in the same location.[646,647] Siberian salmon are abundant in the deep waters of rivers within the taiga forests, and the famous Siberian tiger lives there.[646,647] Forest fires and illegal logging are major problems in the Siberian taiga.[744,745]

== Steppe and Southern Ecosystems ==

Most of the steppe land is agricultural, while the northern part of the steppe zone consists of meadows and plains covered by forests and the southern part consists of vast treeless grasslands.
Black chernozem soil exists in the steppe zone, is considered one of the best types of soil in Russia, and is the most fertile soil in Russia.
The semi-desert and mountain zone includes dry semi-desert depressions around the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus Mountains.
The Caucasus Mountains have a humid climate and feature dense green forests.

== Unique Ecosystems and Biodiversity ==

Lake Baikal is a unique ecosystem.

== Environmental Challenges ==

The ecological situation is severe in the western regions, including the Urals, particularly severe in the Central and Volga regions, and severe in the large coal-producing areas of the east.

== Global Ecological Significance ==

The country is known as 'the lungs of Europe'.
The forest provides a huge amount of oxygen to Europe and to the entire world.

== Protected Area System Overview ==

Russia possesses a well-developed nature conservation system with a long tradition.
The Russian protected area system is large in terms of area.
Since the 1980s, national parks established according to international criteria have been added to these classic categories, and other international protected area classes have also been added.

== Zapovedniks ==

Zapovedniks are strictly protected areas that represent the most important national protected area category in Russia and belong to the highest possible international protected area category.
Entering the core zone of a Zapovednik is forbidden for visitors, though exceptions are granted on a limited scale for scientists.
There are currently 100 Zapovedniks in Russia, with individual areas ranging from 2.31 to 4,169 square kilometers and a combined total area of 27,000 square kilometers.

== Zakazniks ==

Zakazniks are wildlife protection areas that serve as landscape reserves to protect and regenerate natural ecosystems, rare animal and plant species, fossil sites, hydrologically significant sites, and geologically significant sites.
There are restrictions on economic use within Zakazniks, which cover an area of up to 6,000 km² each.
There are approximately 3,000 Zakazniks in Russia with a total area of approximately 78,000 square kilometers.

== National and Nature Parks ==

National parks have existed in Russia since the early 1980s, while other countries had known the national park protected area category for a longer time than Russia.
National parks in Russia have a lower protection status than Sapowedniki and serve the protection of natural and cultural treasures, research purposes, educational purposes, and controlled tourism.
The area of these national parks ranges from 7 km² to 18,900 km² and they cover a total area of 90,000 km² of the state territory.
Nature parks are a relatively new protected area category that serve purposes other than nature conservation and also serve the purpose of recreation.

== World Heritage Sites ==

The Convention for the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage was adopted in 1972, and Russia joined the Convention in 1988.
Natural heritage includes unique physical formations.

In 1996, Lake Baikal was added and the Kamchatka Volcanic Region with Nature Reserve was added.
In 1998, the Altai Mountains were added.

== Arctic and Tundra Ecosystems ==

Vegetation zones and ecozones in Russia run largely parallel to lines of latitude.
The Arctic Ocean is a life-hostile cold desert that affects the northern part of the Taimyr Peninsula.
A treeless landscape belt characterized by permafrost begins from the northernmost part of the Eurasian continent and extends approximately to the Arctic Circle.
This landscape belt has a north-south extent between 200 and 800 km, though in the Central Siberian Mountains it extends up to 70 degrees north latitude.
The northern coastal landscape is characterized by tundra, with the White Sea bay as an exception.
These conditions prevent the formation of forests, and the ground thaws only at the surface.
Abundant precipitation accumulates on the frozen subsoil, causing the tundra to transform into a sea of swamps and bogs in summer.
The vegetation consists of lichens, grasses, and dwarf shrubs.
Agriculture is not possible in this region, and only indigenous reindeer nomads can survive there.
There are few permanent settlements and few human settlements in this zone.

Human settlements are scarce in this region.
Polar bears, seals, walruses, and seabirds live in this region.

== Forest Tundra and Taiga ==

Moving further south from the cold steppe, spruce trees begin to grow individually and eventually form forest tundra together with bog birches and aspens.
This forest tundra is interspersed with swamps and transitions gradually and continuously into the forest zone at its southern boundary.
This zone forms the boreal zone and the Taiga, running north along the line from St.
Petersburg to Ufa to Irkutsk to Sakhalin with a width of 1,000 to 2,000 kilometers.
The forest zone runs through all of Northern Eurasia and is divided into several broad parallel latitudinal sub-zones due to its vast extent.
The coniferous belt, or true Taiga, in the north dominates by far in terms of area, while the zone continues as Sub-Taiga in Central Siberia as a transition zone to the steppe.
The mixed forest belt only adjoins southern European Russia, and the Taiga consists of three subzones.
The northern taiga consists of low pine forests with scattered birches.

The southern taiga is characterized by a high proportion of deciduous trees in the undergrowth, which is caused by more fertile soils.
The Siberian taiga is characterized by open forests and consists of Siberian larches and spruces.

== Forest resources and composition ==

Russia is known as the 'lungs of Europe' because of its forests.
Russia's forests produce a significant amount of oxygen that is supplied to Europe and the rest of the world.
Russian forests account for more than one-fifth of the world's trees, and the volume of Russian forests is estimated at 111 billion cubic meters.
Russia possesses more than one-fifth of the world's forests and owns 22% of the world's forests [2125,2126].
The forest coverage per capita in Russia is 5.3 hectares, and Russia ranks first globally in terms of forest coverage per capita.
Coniferous trees are the most common type of tree and make up 90% of the total forest stock.
A large portion of the forest area consists of larch trees, while spruce, fir, and pine trees are also prevalent in the forest.
Most of the forests are located in the eastern part of the country, with concentrations in Eastern Siberia and the Far East as well as in Western Siberia and the Urals.
Forest fires are a frequent cause of the reduction in forest area and occur frequently in the Asian part of Russia.

== Fauna and species diversity ==

The fauna of Russia is based on the various environments present in the country.
Large mammals characterize Russia's diverse nature.
Reindeer, elks, muskoxen, wapiti, roe deer, and saiga antelope are large herbivores found in Russia.
The polar bear, the Amur leopard, and the Siberian tiger are apex predators found in Russia.
The Amur leopard lives along the Amur River.
The rare Siberian tiger lives exclusively on the mountains of south-eastern Siberia.
The Greenland seal and the walrus are types of marine mammals found on the coasts.
The steppe zone of Russia is a habitat for ground squirrels, the weasel, and the steppe fox.
The reason for the Russian national animal being the Eurasian brown bear is that Russia has the largest population of these bears.
The Eurasian brown bear population can currently be confirmed in the forests of eastern Ural Mountains and Siberia.

Polar bears and seals live in Arctic deserts, where cliffs host bird colonies such as guillemots in summer.
Fur-bearing animals are abundant in the forests, including the Baikal area and the area around Lake Telec.

== Threats to wildlife ==

Predators are threatened by overhunting of their prey animals, habitat loss, poaching for fur, and poaching for use in Chinese medicine.
The Siberian tiger, Amur leopard, snow leopard, green peafowl, goral, and Amur plover require special protection.

== Environmental pollution and degradation ==

The quality of many water bodies is deteriorating as industrial plants and cities discharge inadequately treated wastewater into them, with St.
Petersburg still discharging part of its wastewater untreated into the Gulf of Finland.
Nuclear waste from the Kola Peninsula and the Ural region, along with emissions from metal smelters, are environmental problems.
Many of the world's most polluted places are located in Russia.

== Conservation efforts and regulations ==

Environmental protection regulations have been in place since the 1960s, are very strict, are not followed, and are not monitored.
Wastewater treatment plants have been built through international cooperation since the 1990s.
There are serious problems related to nature conservation.

== Latitudinal Zonation and Soil Types ==

Russia has a wide expanse of land with similar terrain and climate, to which plants and soil have adapted.
These adaptations form long zonal belts running east to west that transition sequentially from north to south.
Vegetation and soils are arranged in latitudinal zones, and there are four main zones distinguished.
From north to south, the tundra follows, then the taiga, then mixed forests, then plains (steppe), and deserts near the Caspian Sea are also present.
Vegetation varies across Russia due to these geographical differences.
Soil types vary across Russia due to these geographical differences.

== Tundra and Forest-Tundra Zones ==

The northern part of Russia's territory is a tundra zone that accounts for approximately 5% of Russia's total area.
The tundra zone is devoid of trees, and the soil is peatland.
Lichens and mosses are abundant in the area, and mosses and lichens grow primarily in the tundra zone.
Reindeer husbandry is the only form of animal farming conducted.
The southern region transitions through a narrow forest-tundra zone mixed with shrubs.
Tundra exists on the East European Plain from north to south.
The tundra zone occupies approximately 25% of the surface area.
Dwarf shrubs grow in the southern part of the tundra zone.
Reindeer, Arctic foxes, snow hares, lemmings, polar bears, Svalbard reindeer, and snowy owls are typical animals inhabiting this zone.

The tundra zone gradually transitions into a forest-tundra zone.
The forest-tundra is covered with dwarf trees that are spruce or birch.
Cattle are raised in the forest-tundra zone.
Various vegetables are cultivated to a small extent in the forest-tundra zone, including potatoes, cabbage, and radishes.
The musk ox was reintroduced in the 20th century on Wrangel Island.

== Forest Zone Characteristics and Flora ==

The southern region eventually transitions into the forest zone, which covers approximately 30% of Russia's territory and accounts for approximately 80% of all forests in the country.
The forest zone is divided into northern coniferous forests and southern mixed forests, consisting mainly of coniferous trees that account for approximately 85% of the area and also including deciduous trees that account for approximately 15% of the surface area.
Siberian larch is the dominant species among coniferous trees, forming a type of larch forest known as typical Siberian larch taiga found in eastern Siberia east of the Yenisei River, while birch is the dominant species among deciduous trees.
Taiga covers larger areas in Siberia compared to other regions.
Broadleaf forests occupy a large area in the European part of Russia, are not found in Siberia, and reappear in the Russian Far East.
The southern part consists of mixed forests with deciduous trees.
The soil in the forest zone is podzol, which is not very fertile.
These forests reduce carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere together with the Amazon rainforests.

Birch forests are primarily located in the central part of the country and are also found in western Siberia, where they form a complex known as white taiga.
The summer in this forest zone is short, and large numbers of mosquitoes appear in these forests during the summer.

== Steppe, Forest-Steppe, and Semi-Desert Zones ==

The southern edge of the forest zone is a transitional forest-steppe zone, and as one moves further south, the forest gradually decreases until the area transitions into a steppe zone.
The steppe zone is continuous and extends from Russia's western border eastward to the Altai region.
The region has warm summers, a long frost-free period, and receives between 200 and 500 mm of annual precipitation.
The soil in the southern part of the forest-steppe zone and the central part of the steppe zone is chernozem, which is famous for its fertility.
Taiga, mixed forests, broadleaf forests, steppes, and semi-deserts exist on the East European Plain from north to south.

== Fauna of the Forest and Tundra Zones ==

The rock racer, the common adder, and the common viper are among the animals living in the forest and tundra zones.
Typical birds of this zone include tits, warblers, capercaillies, and hawks.
The Siberian tiger, the snow leopard, the Eurasian lynx, the brown bear, the Himalayan bear, the beaver, the European otter, the Siberian roe deer, the moose, the eastern elk, the common weasel, and the European mink are found among the mammals.

== Biomes and Natural Zonation ==

The Eastern European plain is primarily covered by tundra, coniferous forests (taiga), and grasslands (steppe), and includes arid regions near the Caspian Sea.
Siberia supports a similar sequence of biomes, and most of Siberia is covered by taiga forests.
These forests are known as 'the lungs of Europe'.
These plains are predominantly composed of steppes in the south and dense forests in the north.
There are fields and steppes in the south.
The lightest forests are located in central Russia, and these forests are mixed forests dominated by birches, poplars, and oaks.
The forests of the central regions are divided by steppes.
The region is covered by Arctic tundra in the north, and coniferous forests (taiga) are found further south.
Siberia presents a similar vegetation sequence, and taiga predominates in Siberia.

Natural (landscape) zones are identified within these climate belts, and the climate zones consist of zonal landscape types.
The Arctic belt includes specific zones and subzones, one of which is the Arctic zone that includes an ice cap subzone and a polar desert subzone.
The subarctic belt includes the tundra zone, which includes arctic tundra, typical tundra, and southern tundra, as well as the forest-tundra zone.
The forest-tundra zone is followed by the taiga forests zone, which is followed by the mixed forests zone, which is followed by the forest-steppe zone, which is followed by the steppe zone, which is followed by the semi-desert zone.
The subtaiga zone is characterized by a predominance of subtaiga landscape types, within which broad-leaved forest landscapes and other landscape types can occur in isolation.
These forests are known as the 'lungs of Europe'.

Natural zonation is most clearly expressed west of the Yenisei River, while it is less distinct east of the Yenisei River where the complex nature of the terrain contributes to weaker zonation.
The moderate belt includes boreal landscape types and subboreal landscape types.
The Taiga subzone includes Northern Taiga, Central Taiga, and Southern Taiga.
Typical steppe and dry steppe are types of steppe zone or subzone.
Sub-Mediterranean landscapes are pre-subtropical landscapes.

== Regional Distribution of Ecosystems ==

Tundras occupy the Arctic coast of Russia, part of Kamchatka, and the Pacific coast of Chukotka.
Forest tundras occupy the Arctic coast of Russia, part of Kamchatka, and the Pacific coast of Chukotka.
The southern boundary of the taiga passes through Pskov, Yaroslavl, Yekaterinburg, Tomsk, Chita, and Komsomolsk-on-Amur.
Mixed forests of European Russia, the Kaliningrad region, and Northern Primorye (Samarga and Anuy), along with coniferous-broad-leaved and birch-aspen forests of southern Western Siberia and coniferous-broad-leaved forests of southern Sakhalin Oblast, belong to the subtaiga.
The broad-leaved forest zone includes the southern part of the Bryansk region.

The broad-leaved forest zone covers the south of the Amur region and most of the Primorsky Krai.
Steppes and forest-steppes cover the main part of the Chernozem region, Southern Pre-Urals, Trans-Urals, Southern Siberia, the Middle Volga region, and the North Caucasus.
Southern Siberia includes Altai, Tuva, Omsk Oblast, Novosibirsk Oblast, and Southern Zabaykalye.
Deserts are found in the Lower Volga region and Kalmykia, while semi-deserts are found in Kalmykia.
