== Forest Resources and Conservation ==

Russia has more than one-fifth of the world's forests, and only the Amazon rainforest absorbs more carbon dioxide than Russia's forests.
A 2012 study by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization and the Government of the Russian Federation was conducted, which found that the potential of Russian forests is significantly underutilized and that Russia's share in global trade of forest products is less than four percent.
A total of 415 animal species were included in the list starting in 1997, and these 415 animal species are now protected.

== Notable Natural Landscapes ==

Lake Baikal is the most famous natural destination in Russia and is known as the Blue Eye of Siberia.
Lake Baikal has clear waters and is surrounded by mountains covered in taiga.
Kamchatka has geysers.
Karelia has lakes and granite rocks.
Tuva has wild steppes.

== Climate and Geographic Zonation ==

The sharply continental climate contributes to weaker zonation east of the Yenisei River.
A significant portion of the country's territory is occupied by mountains, and many regions in the country exhibit altitudinal zonation.
Russian vegetation is divided into several regions according to floristic zonation.
Most of the biodiversity is concentrated in southern European Russia, the mountains of southern Siberia, and southern the Russian Far East.

== Flora Statistics and Composition ==

Russia's flora contains approximately 24,700 plant species, of which approximately 11,400 are vascular plants, approximately 1,137 are mosses, approximately 9,000 are algae, and approximately 159 are ferns.
The Arctic islands of Siberia have the fewest plant species, with between 100 and 150 plant species present.
The forest cover of Russia is 45.4%, covering 796.2 million hectares.

== Floristic Regions and Provinces ==

One of the floristic regions is the Circumboreal region.
The Arctic, Central European, Euxine, Caucasian, Eastern European, West Siberian, Altai-Sayan, Central Siberian, Transbaikal, Northeastern Siberian, and Okhotsk-Kamchatka provinces are part of the Circumboreal region.
Saint Petersburg and Kaliningrad are located in the Central European province.
Sochi and Tuapse are located in the Euxine province.
The Manchurian and Sakhalin-Hokkaido provinces are part of the East Asian region.
The Manchurian province includes the Amur basin and Primorye.

The Turan province includes the Lower Volga area and Kalmykia.
The Junggar-Tianshan province includes the southern Altai area.

== Regional Plant Diversity ==

The Caucasus region is rich in plant species and contains approximately 6,000 plant species.
The Far East region is rich in plant species and contains approximately 4,300 plant species.
Caucasus and Crimea have flora distinct from the previously mentioned European species.

== Arctic and Tundra Vegetation ==

Mosses, Arctic poppies, and buttercups grow in the Arctic deserts of the Russian Far North.
Dwarf birch, willow, and alder grow in the tundra.

== Taiga Forest Vegetation ==

The taiga is characterized by spruce, fir, cedar, pine, and larch.
Blueberries, rosehip, and blackcurrant grow in the understory.

== Southern and Mixed Forest Vegetation ==

South of this area, coniferous-broadleaf and broadleaf forests begin.
These southern forests include pine, oak, linden, ash, elm, maple, hornbeam, pear, and cherry.
The understory in these southern forests includes hazel, elderberry, rosehip, blackcurrant, honeysuckle, and privet.

== Far East and Steppe Vegetation ==

Taxus, walnut, barberry, Daphne, Kalopanax, Aralia, mulberry, lilac, Maackia, rhododendron, magnolia, hydrangea, eleutherococcus, weigela, grape, schisandra, actinidia, clematis, Pueraria, Schizophragma, and other species are found in the southern Far East.
Bay forests and mixed meadows from families such as grasses, legumes, asters, pinks, buckwheats, and others are widespread in the forest-steppe and steppe regions.

== Caucasus and Crimea Flora ==

Juniper trees, firs, chestnut trees, walnuts, fig trees, persimmon trees, sea buckthorn bushes, pistachio trees, sumac plants, mulberry trees, strawberry trees, boxwood shrubs, holly trees, vitex plants, rhododendrons, almond trees, laurel cherry trees, cornus shrubs, laburnum trees, and frankincense plants are found in the Caucasus and Crimea.

Bittersweet vines and hop plants are found in the Caucasus and Crimea.

== Invertebrate Diversity ==

Russia has 100,000 species of insects and 10,000 species of arachnids.

== Biodiversity Hotspots ==

The concentration of biodiversity in southern European Russia is especially high in the Caucasus region.

== Arctic and Tundra Fauna ==

The Arctic and tundra zone is inhabited by the polar bear, the wolf, the arctic fox, the reindeer, the muskox, the snow sheep, the lemming, the collared lemming, seals, walruses, and the snowy owl.

== Taiga Fauna ==

Brown bears, wolves, lynxes, weasels, sables, minks, beavers, and snowshoe hares live in the taiga.

== Biomes and Geographic Distribution ==

Natural zones alternate in a latitudinal direction from north to south across the territory of Russia, and the biomes are arranged from north to south.
The northernmost biome is the polar desert, the next biome to the south is the tundra, the next biome is the forest, the next biome is the forest-steppe, the next biome is the steppe zone, and the southernmost biome is the semi-desert zone.
Most of these ecosystems are located in subarctic tundra regions.
The Russian Plain is covered by Arctic tundra, coniferous forests (taiga), mixed forests, grasslands (steppes), and semi-deserts [8,2179].
The semi-deserts surround the Caspian Sea [8,2179].
The primary vegetation in Siberia is taiga [8,2179].

== Fauna of the Taiga ==

Squirrels, flying squirrels, wood lemmings, field voles, shrews, and adders live in the taiga.
Goshawks, capercaillies, partridges, woodpeckers, and taiga flycatchers nest in the taiga.

== Fauna of Mixed and Broadleaf Forests ==

Mixed and broad-leaved forests are inhabited by foxes, badgers, hedgehogs, moles, bison, boars, red deer, roe deer, and minks.
These forests are also inhabited by numerous bird species, lizards, vipers, and grass snakes.

== Fauna of the Caucasus and Far East ==

Leopards, hyenas, raccoon dogs, and tur live in the Caucasus region, where a large number of reptiles also live.
The Himalayan bear, tiger, forest cat, hare (harza), spotted deer, and serow are found in the forests of the Russian Far East.

== Fauna of Steppes and Deserts ==

Hamsters, ground squirrels, marmots, and field mice are the predominant animals in steppes.
There are many saiga antelopes.
The large steppe birds include cranes.
Gazelles, jackals, sand cats, and numerous rodents are found in the desert.

== Endemism and Species Distribution ==

Most animals living in Russia are also found in other parts of the temperate region and other parts of the Arctic region.
The country has 57 endemic fish species, 22 mammal species found only there, and one bird species that does not breed outside the country.

== Red Data Book and Conservation Status ==

The red list was published in 1995 and included 533 plant species, of which only 276 are found in some kind of nature reserve.
Russia's 1995 Red List included 64 mammal species, 109 bird species, 11 reptile species, 4 amphibian species, and 9 fish species.
As of 1997, a total of 415 animal species were included in the Russian Federation Red Data Book [324,2493].
Additionally, 415 mammal species were added to the Red Book in 1997 [324,2494].

== Hunting and Poaching ==

Hunting of mammals and birds is common, and an agency determines which animals can be hunted and how many animals can be hunted.
In the early 2000s, there were approximately 60 mammal species and approximately 70 bird species on the agency's list.
Many of the country's residents hunt illegally to compensate for their low standard of living.
Poaching cases were documented in 1997, and approximately 50,000 poaching cases were recorded that year.

== Forest Ecology and Carbon Sequestration ==

Russia accounts for one-fifth of the world's total forest area.
Russia is known as the 'lungs of Europe' because its carbon dioxide absorption is second only to the Amazon rainforest.
Russia's forests are known as the 'lungs of Europe' and rank second only to the Amazon rainforest in CO2 absorption capacity.

== Deforestation and Timber Industry ==

Russia is currently the world leader in deforestation, where timber is harvested intensively and forests are being heavily destroyed in the Far East, the Northwest, and Siberia.
Numerous Chinese timber factories have been established in Russia, creating jobs and income, though all finished wood production lines are located in China.
There is concern that forest resources are being over-exploited, and deforestation is becoming increasingly difficult to control.
The total area of forest destroyed from 2000 to the present is 40 million hectares, of which only half has been replanted.
The area of Russia's forest reserves is 8,087,900 square kilometers, and dry deciduous forests are found in the country.[7,831,2522,4010][1117,2495,2496,4041,4042]

== Environment ==

During the Soviet era, the Russian environment was heavily burdened, polluted with factory waste, and chemically and radioactively contaminated.
Russia currently faces serious environmental problems, though there is a growing environmental awareness among the Russian population.
Citizens have a right to a healthy environment and to reliable information about the state of the environment, a right enshrined in Article 42 of the Russian Constitution.
Environmental protection has a relatively low priority in Russian politics, a situation repeatedly criticized by international environmental organizations such as WWF or Greenpeace.
Environmental standards were often insufficiently met in the past during the exploration of new oil or gas reserves, with the development of the Sakhalin II oil and gas fields serving as a well-known example from recent times where environmental regulations were allegedly violated to a greater extent.
Corruption is widespread within state environmental agencies, enabling multiple violations of environmental regulations during house construction and large-scale illegal logging.
There are numerous environmental hazards from the Soviet era, including dilapidated factories.

Some cities with factories that cannot meet current environmental standards are considered ecological emergency zones.

Russia, by 1993 constitution, is a symmetric federal republic with a semi-presidential system, wherein the president is the head of state, and the prime minister is the head of government.
It is structured as a multi-party representative democracy, with the federal government composed of three branches: Legislative: The bicameral Federal Assembly of Russia, made up of the 450-member State Duma and the 170-member Federation Council, adopts federal law, declares war, approves treaties, has the power of the purse and the power of impeachment of the president.
Executive: The president is the commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces, and appoints the Government of Russia (Cabinet) and other officers, who administer and enforce federal laws and policies.
The president may issue decrees of unlimited scope, so long as they do not contradict the constitution or federal law.
Judiciary: The Constitutional Court, Supreme Court and lower federal courts, whose judges are appointed by the Federation Council on the recommendation of the president, interpret laws and can overturn laws they deem unconstitutional.

The president is elected by popular vote for a six-year term and may be elected no more than twice.
Ministries of the government are composed of the premier and his deputies, ministers, and selected other individuals; all are appointed by the president on the recommendation of the prime minister (whereas the appointment of the latter requires the consent of the State Duma).
United Russia is the dominant political party in Russia, and has been described as "big tent" and the "party of power".
Under the administrations of Vladimir Putin, Russia has experienced democratic backsliding, and has become an authoritarian state under a dictatorship, with Putin's policies being referred to as Putinism.

== Constitutional framework and system of government ==

The Russian Constitution was adopted on December 12, 1993.
The Russian Federation has a dualist system of governance that reflects some elements of a limited presidential system.
The President exercises power autocratically, and the political system of the Russian Federation can be characterized as a mix of unstable democratic institutions and authoritarian practices.
Russia was ranked 124th in the democracy index in 2020.
The current political system is described as a 'super-presidential rule' or post-democracy.
According to the official self-presentation, the President does not belong to any of the three branches of state power, ensures the functioning and interaction of the three branches of state power, is the central figure of the Russian state, and has access to all means of power of the state.

== The Presidency: Election and powers ==

The last election was held on 18 March 2018, and this election method and term length are based on a constitutional amendment made on December 31, 2008.
A candidate must be at least 35 years old and have lived in the country for more than ten years, and the same person cannot be elected President more than twice in a row.
The President makes an annual address to the Federal Assembly in which a government program concerning the country's political and economic development is declared.
The President has the right to veto draft laws, bill proposals, and laws passed by the Duma and the Federation Council before they become effective.
Such decrees have immediate legal effect, and a veto can theoretically be overridden by a two-thirds majority vote in both houses of parliament.
The Kremlin is the official residence of the President of Russia.

== The Security Council ==

The President appoints and chairs the Security Council, which deals with defense issues.
The Security Council nominates candidates for the head of the National Bank, the Prosecutor General, and members of the Supreme Court.

== The Federal Assembly: Structure and elections ==

The State Duma is the lower house.
Voters cast a ballot for a candidate from their electoral district and also cast a ballot for a political party.
Deputies are elected based on party lists for a five-year term.
The State Duma is elected for a five-year term.
The minimum age requirement for deputies of the Duma is 21 years.
Deputies of the Duma cannot engage in any paid activities from the moment they are elected and cannot hold other responsible government positions from the moment they are elected.

== Legislative process and veto powers ==

The Federal Assembly can veto a bill adopted by the State Duma.
Executive power resides with the government of the Russian Federation, and key ministries and agencies are not subordinate to the Prime Minister or the Parliament.
The President does not have the right to dissolve the State Duma for the first 12 months after the State Duma is formed, and the Constitutional Court must agree with this decision.

== Executive branch: Government composition and powers ==

Executive power resides with the government [15,16].
The President appoints and dismisses the Prime Minister at their discretion.
The Council of Ministers consists of 30 members.
The government is a technocratic cabinet.
Ensuring the implementation of a unified state financial and monetary policy is within the powers of the Government of the Russian Federation.
Preparing the federal budget, submitting it to the State Duma, and overseeing its execution are within the powers of the Government of the Russian Federation.
Implementing state policy in the fields of culture, science, education, healthcare, social security, and ecology is within the powers of the Government of the Russian Federation.
Ensuring the implementation of the country's defense and foreign policy strategies is within the powers of the Government of the Russian Federation.
The Prime Minister is a secondary figure in the executive power.
The President can preside over cabinet meetings.
The President can issue binding orders to the Prime Minister and other members of the government.
The President can annul any act of the government.
Government decisions can be annulled by the President of the Russian Federation when there is a conflict between government decisions and the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws, or presidential decrees.
Mikhail Mishustin is the current Prime Minister.
Key ministries and agencies are directly subordinate to the President [978,979,980].
The Russian Presidential Administration is directly subordinate to the President [978,979,980].

The government is not a political parliamentary government with its own support base.
The cabinet is mainly responsible for economic and financial issues and administrative tasks.
The cabinet meets weekly in public sessions.
The President has the right to chair cabinet meetings but does not always exercise this right.
The President of Russia proposes the Prime Minister.
The government is not bound by the parliamentary term but is bound by the president's term of office.
When a new president is elected, the government resigns its powers.
The government determines unified financial, credit, and monetary policy.
Cultural, education, healthcare, social security, and ecological policy are fields of government responsibility.

== Relationship between President, Government, and Duma ==

The Federal Assembly and the President cannot strongly influence each other.
The State Duma can dismiss the government, express a vote of no confidence in the government, or reject the government's question of confidence.
This action requires a vote of no confidence supported by a large majority, and a vote of no confidence requires a majority of all deputies.
The Duma has the right to propose a vote of no confidence, which can be exercised twice within a three-month period until the President makes any mandatory decision.
The President can dissolve the Duma, and the head of state has the right to dissolve the Duma and declare new elections.
Dissolving the Duma allows for new elections to be appointed, and this right is exercised if the Duma rejects the presidential nominee three times.
The Duma must give absolute approval for the appointment of a new Prime Minister and for the appointment of a new government.
Both chambers of the Federal Assembly must vote to initiate impeachment.
The distribution of power does not necessarily reflect the political balance of forces in the State Duma, and the composition of the government does not necessarily reflect the political balance of forces in the State Duma.

== Political parties and parliamentary composition ==

The Communist Party, the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia, and Just Russia are main political parties in Russia.
Leading political parties in Russia include the Communist Party, the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia, and Fair Russia.
United Russia holds 54% of the seats, the Communist Party of the Russian Federation holds 13% of the seats, the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia holds 13% of the seats, and Just Russia holds 6% of the seats.
A non-parliamentary opposition was organized.
This exercise of executive power is based on Article 114 of the current Constitution.

== Presidential powers and executive appointments ==

Following a 2020 constitutional amendment, the same approval requirement applies to Vice Prime Ministers and Ministers proposed by the Prime Minister, and the Russian President is obligated to appoint the nominated individuals without the ability to reject them.
The President retains the right to dismiss the Prime Minister in case of a loss of confidence or improper performance of duties, as well as the right to dismiss the Prime Minister's deputies and Ministers.
The President has the right to dissolve the Duma.
The President of Russia is the guardian of the Constitution, must take any measure to protect the integrity of Russian sovereignty, protects the rights and freedoms of citizens, and represents the country in diplomatic meetings.

== Legislative process and parliamentary structure ==

A political party must receive at least 7% of the votes to gain a seat in parliament.
One representative is from the regional parliamentary representation and serves for the duration of their region's legislative period, as the term of office is tied to that legislative period.
All laws passed by the State Duma must be submitted to the Federation Council, which has the discretion to review these laws within two weeks or not at all, and failure to review the laws within two weeks is considered approval.
The Federation Council can forward laws passed by the Duma to the President for signature or reject laws passed by the Duma, and if the Federation Council rejects a law, the Duma can override this rejection with a two-thirds majority.
A presidential veto can be overridden, and the override requires a two-thirds majority in each parliamentary chamber.

== The Federation Council and regional representation ==

In constitutional reality, the Federation Council functions as a representative of the center in the regions rather than representing the regions in the center.
The Kremlin influences elections in the regions and the selection of regional personnel.

== The Security Council of the Russian Federation ==

The Security Council of the Russian Federation (SCRF) is a body of high-ranking politicians that makes joint decisions on foreign policy, security policy, and defense policy.
The Council is organized as part of the presidential Kremlin administration and possesses a certain degree of autonomy.
The body consists of 13 permanent members who are appointed based on their proximity to office, including examples such as the Minister of Defense and the Minister of Foreign Affairs.
The body also consists of 18 members appointed by the President who do not have voting rights.
The body meets approximately 35 times per year, while the permanent members meet weekly and are chaired by the President.
The Council has its own secretariat that coordinates voting processes between the actors and has insight into the planning processes and operations of the actors.
Employees of the secretariat are frequently promoted to high positions in the administration.
The secretary of the Council plays a special and influential role.

The Council was founded in 1992 and is sometimes compared to the former Politburo or described as an inner circle.
Nikolai Patrushev is the long-term secretary of the Council, where important people remain members for years even as they may change their positions in administration and politics.
The President ultimately decides on membership in the Council, which serves as a place where elite actors, particularly the Siloviki, deliberate on politics and resolve potential conflicts.
It is now believed that important decisions are not made within the Council itself but are instead prepared in a smaller framework.
The Council and its Secretariat play an effective role as agenda-setters and as a coordination center.
Security-related laws are pre-drafted in the Council.
The National Security Strategy is developed within the Council through consensus.
The Council's scope extends beyond internal and external security issues and influences the ideological orientation of the state.

== Personalization of power and political reality ==

The process demonstrated that the Council could not constrain Putin and that power in Russia was becoming more radicalized.
Power in Russia stems from Putin as a person rather than institutions, and the authoritarian regime in Russia is highly personalized.
The parliament plays only a weak role, and the written constitution and the political reality diverge.
Political meetings take place there.
The Russian Federation is recognized under international law.

== The party system and political cartel ==

This cartel is referred to as a 'four-party cartel'.
Parties outside the Duma include Jabloko, the Patriots of Russia, and the Right Cause party.
The parties Just Russia and Right Cause were deliberately built by the Kremlin as spoiler parties to address the electorate of competing opposition parties with related themes and to weaken these opposing parties.
The cartel of pro-system parties enables the Kremlin to control the Duma.
According to political scientist Petra Stykow, there are only slight programmatic differences in the 'cartel of systemic opposition', there is no real ideological competition over content, and there is only competition between groups that want power.
The parliament serves as a decision-making body for elite groups that use it to decide on issues and conflicts that the Kremlin considers not significant enough to require its own direct decision, and it facilitates the inclusion of potential opposition members through parliamentary privileges.
United Russia has been described as a 'catch-all' party.

== Elections, manipulation, and opposition ==

Putin can stop initiatives he initiated if they are recognized as too unpopular among the public by using his veto power and can stage himself in the public eye when exercising his veto.
Elections are characterized by the exclusion of unpopular candidates, the criminal prosecution of unpopular candidates, strong state support for government-aligned candidates and parties, and strong media support for government-aligned candidates and parties.
It is incorrect to assume that Putin has no support among the population, and election fraud was not decisive for his election victories.
Manipulated elections do not primarily serve to ensure election victories but are used to demonstrate the loyalty of the regime's clientele, discourage opposition voters, and discourage dissatisfied parts of the elite, with the overall purpose being the consolidation of the system.
Promising opposition candidates were not included on election lists and were eliminated from the process.
The opposition led by Alexei Navalny resorted to the concept of 'Smart Voting' in 2018 after Alexei Navalny was not allowed to run as a presidential candidate prior to this event, and the goal of the concept included mobilizing apathetic segments of the population.
United Russia received significantly fewer votes than expected in some regional elections, and in Tomsk, United Russia lost its majority.

Navalny exposed the corruption of local elites in Tomsk.
Tactical voting helped the Communists.
Regional deputies of this party, which is actually pro-Kremlin, found favor in tactical voting.
These deputies positioned themselves more strongly against the Kremlin as Nawalny had hoped.

== Constitutional framework and amendments ==

Constitutional amendments were made in 2020, including an amendment to Article 67 of the constitution that establishes continuity of the Russian state in history based on preserving the 'memory of ancestors' and preserving general ideals and belief in God transmitted by ancestors.
The Constitution of Russia established the basis for a presidential system of government, under which the administration is regulated according to the principle of separation of powers and the government is regulated by a system of checks and balances.
The current Constitution of Russia states that the President is not a member of the Russian government, an authority established under Article 24 of the Federal Constitution.
The vice presidency institution was abolished, and Aleksander Ruskoi was the Vice President.
Ruslan Khasbulatov was the chairman of parliament from Chechnya.
After joining the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), the term of office for the President was four years, but a constitutional amendment in 2008 changed the presidential term to six years.

== The Presidency ==

Vladimir Putin is the president of the country, and the President of Russia decides on foreign policy [cite: 1620,1621].
The President is elected using a two-round system [cite: 2088,2089], where a runoff occurs if no candidate obtains an absolute majority of valid votes in the first round [cite: 2088,2089].
In the second round, the candidate with the most votes faces the second candidate with the most votes [cite: 2088,2089].
The last presidential election occurred on March 18, 2018.
The presidential term was extended to six years in December 2008 [cite: 2088,2089], and the term length was increased from four years to six years.
The six-year term length applies since the 2008 constitutional amendments.
The President can veto legislative bills, and the President of Russia can veto bills.
The president submits candidates for state positions.
The president serves as the head of the National Security Council.
These decrees have the force of law.
The President's official residence is the Kremlin, and the president is based in the Kremlin.
Kremlin.ru is the official website of the Kremlin.
The Prime Minister of Russia is officially the second most powerful person in the Russian political structure.

The presidential term was originally set at four years, and the extended term applies starting from the next election.
The President can force the resignation of the entire government, express dissent regarding such a motion, choose between accepting the government's resignation, or choose between dissolving the assembly.
The president resides in the Kremlin and can veto bills before they become law.
The President serves as the head of the Security Council of the Russian Federation.

== The Prime Minister and Government ==

The Prime Minister of Russia holds the presidency of the Government of Russia and is responsible to parliament.
The President proposes the composition of the government to the Duma, which confirms the proposed government composition.
The Duma can reject the government's confirmation up to three times, and if the Duma rejects the government three times, the president may dissolve it and call for new elections.
The Duma can approve a motion of no confidence in the government, which requires an absolute majority.
The Duma can reject a proposed candidacy three times [cite: 1598], and if the Duma rejects the candidacy three times, the President can dissolve it [cite: 1598].
The Federal Assembly promotes federal laws [cite: 448].

== The State Duma ==

The Federal Assembly consists of the State Duma as its lower house.
Members of the State Duma are elected in direct nationwide elections from party lists using a proportional representation system that has been in place since 2012.
Deputies to the State Duma serve five-year terms [cite: 448].
The State Duma is presided over by Viatcheslav Volodine.
United Russia won a majority of seats in the State Duma in the 2021 elections.
Major political parties represented in the State Duma include the Communist Party of the Russian Federation, the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia, and Just Russia.

The new law governs the distribution of parliamentary seats among party lists that have surpassed a national threshold of 7%.

== The Federation Council ==

The Federation Council is the senate of the Russian Federation and is composed of representatives from at least 85 subjects of the Russian Federation.
These representatives are called senators and are not directly elected by the people.
Each of the 85 federal units sends two representatives to the Federation Council, while each of Russia's 89 regions is represented by two members in the body.
Each of the 85 administrative subdivisions nominates two delegates to the Federation Council [cite: 448], and each federal subject sends one representative from its executive branch to the assembly.
Members of the Federation Council are appointed for a four-year term, and delegates in the Federation Council serve four-year terms [cite: 448].
The Federation Council is presided over by Valentina Matvienko.

== Political parties and elections ==

The main political parties include the Communist Party of the Russian Federation, Fair Russia, and the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia.
The Communist Party of the Russian Federation, the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia, Just Russia, and Russia of the Future are one of the main political parties, though Russia of the Future is not registered.
The main political parties are regulated by a specific law.
Since 2003, the system has effectively become a dominant party system led by the ruling party 'United Russia', which is led by Vladimir Putin.
Opposition candidates are excluded from elections.
A two-thirds majority is required to remove the head of state.
The political system is criticized domestically and internationally for its authoritarian nature aimed at ruling by 'dictatorship of law'.

== Executive agencies and security ==

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Russia implements foreign policy.
The MVD (Ministry of Internal Affairs) and the MCHS (Ministry for Emergency Situations) guarantee citizen security.
FSTEK is the Federal Service for Technical and Export Control, FSVNG is the National Guard, and FSIN is the Federal Penitentiary Service.

== Political culture and institutions ==

The legislative body is a parliament, and the people of Russia elect members of the legislative council at the federal level.
The President is often the initiator of legislation.
The Kremlin in Moscow has been the center of Russian political affairs since the Soviet Union, and Russia still retains part of its Soviet political culture today.
Gov.ru is a portal of the Russian government and is the official government portal of Russia.
There are domestic political reasons for hosting mega-events, and the organization of mega-events is justified by strengthening national unity.

== Executive branch and presidential powers ==

The Russian Federation is a presidential republic where the executive power is held by the President.
The head of state is President Vladimir Putin, who has been president since 2012, and the head of government is Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev, who has been prime minister since 2012.
The president is the center of the executive branch, and these powers cover all aspects of state affairs.
The President has the power to veto legislation, call general elections, and dissolve the parliament.
The President serves as the chairman of the Security Council, appoints the Secretary of the Security Council, and proposes candidates for Governor of the Central Bank.
A candidate must receive a majority of votes to be elected president, and if no candidate receives a majority, a runoff election is held between the top two candidates.
To run for president, a candidate must receive the recommendation of a political party within the parliament or gather signatures from 2 million voters.
The President has veto rights over legislation before its adoption.
The last presidential election took place in 2018.

The head of state and his cabinet are located at the Kremlin.
The Prime Minister is selected by the President of the country, and this appointment or dismissal is based on a proposal from the Prime Minister.
In case of war or threat of war, the President has the right to issue a decree for the entire territory of the country or part of it.
The extension applied to the President.

== Legislative structure and election mechanics ==

Each federal subject sends one representative from its legislative branch to the assembly.
Members of the lower house served four-year terms, with half elected via single-member districts and half via proportional representation.
An electoral reform passed in the lower house on April 23, 2005, transitioned the system to full proportional representation and raised the threshold for obtaining seats from 5 percent to 7 percent.
The term of office was extended to five years in 2008, and the deputies serve a term of 5 years.
The most recent election was held on September 10, 2023.
Elections for local government mayors, such as republic governors or state governors, and local councils are held annually on the second Sunday of September each year.
The new constitution requires approval from the upper house, the Federation Council [cite: 2571], and mandates that legislation passed by the Duma must receive Federation Council approval [cite: 2571].
A two-thirds majority vote is required to override a presidential veto [cite: 2571], and impeachment requires a two-thirds majority vote of present deputies in the lower house to be finalized [cite: 2571].
The Prime Minister requires the confidence of the parliament.
The number of eligible voters in Russia was approximately 190 million [cite: 2582], and the deputies are elected by universal direct vote.

The State Duma is the lower house of parliament and is located in Moscow.
Members of the State Duma are elected through direct elections using a proportional representation system based on party lists.
The legislative body is elected through proportional representation voting, and all members are elected using a proportional representation system.
The State Duma consists of representatives from all parties that meet the 5% threshold, while the threshold for entering parliament was 7%.
The term of office for the deputies is five years.
The upper house is known as Sovet Federatsii, and representatives from all 83 regions sit in the upper house.
Russia has universal suffrage, which dates back to 1918, and the voting age is 18 years.
Until 2006, a turnout threshold applied to parliamentary elections, and the turnout threshold for parliamentary elections was 25% until 2006 [cite: 2771].
A turnout threshold applied to presidential elections until 2006, and the turnout threshold for presidential elections was 50% until 2006 [cite: 2771].
On November 17, 2006, these turnout thresholds were abolished [cite: 2771].
The thresholds were possibly abolished to allow governing even with very low turnout without interruption [cite: 2771].

== Political parties and party system ==

The ruling party United Russia holds an overwhelming majority, while various parties exist as opposition.
The Liberal Democratic Party of Russia is an extreme right-wing party, and the Communist Party of the Russian Federation is an extreme left-wing party.
Parties with liberal, centrist, nationalist, patriotic, socialist, and communist ideologies exist.
These parties are considered loyal to the Putin administration and are classified as 'systemic opposition'.
There is an indication that these parties have lost their function as opposition.
The Communist Party of the Russian Federation is the first opposition party that checks the United Russia Party.
The Communist Party of the Russian Federation has roots in the former Soviet Union.
The ideology of the Communist Party of the Russian Federation is based on communism associated with Stalin, Trotsky, and Lenin.
Russia shows caution towards the Communist Party of the Russian Federation.
The Communist Party of Russia exists or existed.
The Communist Party is a leading political party in Russia.
The Liberal Democratic Party of Russia is a leading political party in Russia.
Just Russia is a leading political party in Russia.
United Russia is currently one of the largest political parties.

United Russia is the largest party in Russia and is the Kremlin party.
The Communist Party of the Russian Federation is currently one of the largest political parties and is led by Gennady Zyuganov.
Just Russia is a democratic socialist party that was formed by the merger of three smaller parties: Rodina (Motherland), the Pensioners' Party, and the Russian Party of Life.
LDPR is an extreme right-wing ultranationalist party.
The Duma includes two smaller parties.
Right Cause, a center-right party that supports a free-market economy, participated in the 2011 parliamentary elections but did not reach the 7% threshold.
Patriots of Russia participated in the 2011 parliamentary elections but did not reach the 7% threshold.
Yabloko participated in the 2011 parliamentary elections but did not reach the 7% threshold.

== Local government and administrative structure ==

In December 2004, the method for electing local government leaders changed from a direct election system to one where the President nominates local leaders and the local parliament must approve the President's nominees.
The government is the head of the state administration.
The system of federal bodies consists of federal ministries, federal services, and federal agencies.

== Civil society and political dissent ==

The authorities have strengthened regulations, including harsher penalties under assembly laws.
Despite these difficulties, protests organized by anti-government activists are still held in Moscow, sometimes involving tens of thousands of participants and currently being conducted peacefully.
Participants in some unauthorized gatherings have been arrested by security authorities.
Checks on the President by the parliament are almost impossible, and the President has the right to veto all laws approved by parliament before they become official law.

== Constitutional framework and state structure ==

Russia is a democratic federal legal state based on a rule of law system.
The three branches are independent from each other, and political decisions are made in the Federal Assembly of Russia.
The Constitution is currently in effect with several amendments, including major amendments adopted in 2008 and 2020.
Constitutional norms were introduced in 2008.
The highest official is elected for a term of no more than 5 years and cannot hold the position for more than two consecutive terms.
Previously, the head of state was elected every four years.

== Powers and role of the President ==

The President has broad powers in the legislative branch and acts as an arbiter in matters between central and regional authorities.
The President is a guarantor of the constitution and a guarantor of citizens' rights and freedoms.
The President of Russia is the guardian of the Constitution and the guardian of citizens' rights and freedoms.
The President of Russia must take any measure to protect the integrity of Russian sovereignty.
The President has veto power over legislative bills before they become law.
The President directs the country's foreign policy and decides on the resignation of the government.
The President heads the Security Council and appoints and dismisses the command of the Armed Forces.
The President has the right to propose candidates for the position of Chairman of the Central Bank.
This right can be exercised in case of aggression or in case of an immediate threat of aggression.
The state of war can be declared on the entire territory of the country or on specific territories.
The president is obligated to immediately inform the Federal Assembly about this decision.
These decrees are mandatory for execution throughout the entire territory of Russia.

== Presidential elections and term limits ==

The president is elected through free, universal, and secret voting [3049,3050].
A candidate must be over 35 years old and have resided in Russia for at least 10 years [3049,3050].
The election is conducted by secret ballot.
A President cannot serve more than two consecutive terms.
Former presidents of Russia can be members of the Federation Council [3461,3462].

== Impeachment and removal of the President ==

The President can be removed from office by the Federation Council, a process that requires an indictment by the State Duma for treason or another serious crime.
Removal also requires positive rulings from the Supreme Court and the Constitutional Court, meaning the President can only be removed by the Federal Assembly with the Supreme Court.

== The Government and the Prime Minister ==

The highest executive body of state power is the Government of the Russian Federation, which constitutes the executive branch and is accountable to the President of the Russian Federation while being under the control of the State Duma.
The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation assists the President in performing their duties as head of state, and the Prime Minister of Russia assumes the presidency in case of the President's death or resignation.
Mikhail Vladimirovich Mishustin is currently the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation and holds the position of Prime Minister, having assumed this position on January 16, 2020.[3260,3261,3262,3263,3264]

== The Federal Assembly and legislative process ==

The Duma is the lower house, and all laws applicable throughout the Federation must be approved by an absolute majority in the Duma.

== The State Duma: composition and elections ==

Deputies are elected in general elections for a 5-year term since 2012, whereas before 2012 the term lasted 4 years.
Any citizen with native or acquired Russian nationality who is over 21 years old can be elected as a deputy.
225 deputies are elected from single-member constituencies, while the remaining 225 deputies are elected from a federal electoral district.
The 225 seats in federal constituencies are filled based on a proportional representation system using party lists, and the 225 seats in single-member districts are filled in single-member districts.
Deputies from the federal district are elected proportionally based on votes for federal candidate lists.

== The Federation Council: composition and history ==

There are two representatives from each of the 83 federal subjects, with one representative delegated by the head of the region and one representative delegated by the local parliament.
Members of the Federation Council were elected by the population in 1993.
In 1995, governors (presidents) and speakers of regional legislative assemblies directly took their place.
Since 2000, appointed and elected representatives have taken their place respectively from executive and legislative bodies of federal subjects.

== Dissolution of the State Duma ==

If the State Duma does not approve, the president has the right to dissolve it.
In such a case, the newly elected State Duma approves the prime minister.

== Political party system and major parties ==

Political parties compete for seats in a bicameral parliament.
Eight parties were represented in the State Duma following the 2021 elections, and five of these parties won more than one seat.
United Russia received 49.82% of the votes, the Communist Party of the Russian Federation received 18.93% of the votes, the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia received 7.55% of the votes, Just Russia received 7.46% of the votes, and New People received 5.32% of the votes.
Russian political life is dominated by the United Russia party and its satellites.
Other tolerated parties include the Communist Party, an ultranationalist group, and the socialist party Right Russia.

== Ideologies and leadership of specific parties ==

The LDPR is led by Leonid Slutsky and is politically far-right and authoritarian.
Jabloko is a social-liberal party that is strongly pro-Western and led by Sergey Mitrochin.
The party supports Russian membership in the European Union and opposes the war in Chechnya.
The Patriots of Russia are led by Gennady Semigin and is a left-nationalist party.
Right Cause is a liberal center-right party and is a project of the Kremlin.

== Minor parties and political organizations ==

These organizations represent nearly all social and political ideas of the modern world.
The Autonomous Action, the Anarchists' Movement Association, the National-Patriotic Front 'Memory', Another Russia, the Libertarian Party of Russia, the Pirate Party of Russia, the Revolutionary Workers' Party, Working Russia, the Russian Social Democratic Youth League, the Russian Civic Alliance, the Socialist Party of Workers, the Social Democrats Alliance, the Romanov Family Association, the Association of Initiatives Citizens of Russia, the Democratic Union, Great Russia, the All-Russian People's Front, the All-Union Communist Party of Bolsheviks, and Green Alternative are one such organization.

The President of Russia has the function of choosing the Prime Minister, and these proposals are submitted to the State Duma for consideration.
The proposed Chairman of the Central Bank does not belong to the government.

== Executive structure and composition ==

Federal Ministers head ministries, oversee various state programs, and carry out special assignments, while Deputy chairmen oversee several ministries and agencies.
The government includes heads of agencies that do not hold ministerial positions, and these heads of non-ministerial agencies are officially equated to ministers in status.
The structure and quantitative composition of the government are not regulated by law, as the President determines both the quantitative composition and structure of the government.
These appointments include the Prime Minister, who is formally known as the Chairman of the Government.
Russia currently has 19 ministries and other bureaus at the same level as ministries, among which there are 9 special ministries.
These powerful ministries are directly overseen by the President and include the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Civil Defense, Emergency Situations and Elimination of Consequences of Natural Disasters, and the Federal Security Service.

The Foreign Intelligence Service, the Federal Protective Service, and the National Guard are powerful departments.
There are 10 ministries that report directly to the Prime Minister, including the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Federal Ministry of Health, the Federal Ministry of Education and Science, the Federal Ministry of Industry and Trade, and the Federal Ministry of Agriculture.
The Federal Ministry of Regional Development was one of these ministries but has been abolished.

== Presidential powers and elections ==

Proposing the Prime Minister to the Duma is a formal element of parliamentarism.
The President of Russia can dissolve the Duma and call for new elections.
The president has been elected every six years since 2012, whereas previously the president was elected every four years and the presidential term was 4 years before the 2008 constitutional amendment.
The President can veto bills before they become law, has the right to veto laws passed by the legislature, and can veto bills before they become effective.
The election is won by the candidate with the most votes and there are a maximum of two rounds in the election.
The President must have resided in Russia for at least 10 years and must be at least 35 years old.
The most recent election was held in 2018.
The President is the Chairman of the Security Council of the Russian Federation.

== Legislative powers and procedures ==

The composition of the Russian Federation's upper house resembles that of the US Senate, and its structure traces back to earlier traditions in Russia.
During the Soviet era, the Supreme Soviet of the USSR was divided into two chambers that had different representation from various regions.
State Duma members have been elected every five years since 2011, with half elected through a proportional representation system and the other half through majority votes in single-member districts.
The main task of the Duma is to approve the state budget, and it appoints and removes the Chairman of the Audit Chamber and half of the inspectors.
One representative comes from the state representative body, and one representative comes from the state executive body.
The main function of the Federation Council is to approve federal laws, changes to the boundaries of federal subjects, and presidential decrees regarding states of war and emergency.
The Federation Council decides on foreign military deployments and addresses issues relating to the relationship between the center and local regions.

== Political parties and ideology ==

As of July 6, 2020, 44 political parties were registered, though only six of these parties are represented in the State Duma.
The United Russia party was founded in 2001 through the merger of political movements including 'Unity' and 'Fatherland — All Russia'.
The party holds positions of liberal conservatism and maintained its position as the dominant party.
In 2012, the party had a membership of 2 million people.
The party received 343 seats in the 2016 State Duma elections, and Dmitry Medvedev is the chairman of the party.
The Communist Party of the Russian Federation (CPRF) was founded in 1993 as a restored Communist Party of the RSFSR.
The party positions itself as the direct heir of the CPSU and received 42 seats in the 2016 elections.
Gennady Zyuganov is the Chairman of the Central Committee.
The Liberal Democratic Party of Russia (LDPR) was founded in 1992.
The party adheres to the theory of a mixed economy and the ideas of nationalism.

The party 'Fair Russia' (SR), also known as the 'Socialists', was founded in 2006, holds positions of social democracy, belongs to the Socialist International, and is chaired by Sergey Mironov.
The party had 160,000 members, a count recorded in 2016, and received 23 seats in the 2016 elections.
The party 'Rodina' was founded in 2004, adheres to the ideology of left-wing nationalism, and had a membership figure recorded in the year 2004.
The party received one seat in the 2016 elections.
The Civic Platform party was founded in 2012, adheres to the ideology of conservatism, adheres to the ideology of economic liberalism, and had a membership count recorded in 2014.
R.
G.
Shaikhutdinov is the chairman of the Federal Political Committee of the party.
The party adheres to the ideas of patriotism, is chaired by L.
E.
Slutsky, and received 39 seats in the 2016 elections.

A federal law titled "On Political Parties" was adopted on July 11, 2001, and prohibits the creation of political parties based on religious affiliation.
The Communist Party, Justice for Russia, the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia, and Fair Russia are political parties in Russia.
The Communist Party, the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia, and Fair Russia are major political parties in Russia.

== Democratic principles and context ==

Russia made a choice in favor of democracy and did not intend to create a special type of democracy unique to Russia.
Russia intended to establish the fundamental principles of a democracy that has been established in the world.
Modern democratic institutions must be adapted to the current development status of Russia.
Democratic principles must align with Russia's history and traditions.
There may be some differences in the operation of major democratic institutions.
Applying democratic principles and standards cannot be linked to national collapse or to the poverty of the people.
Olga Golodets is a Deputy Prime Minister of the Russian government.
The judicial branch includes the High Arbitration Court.

== Ministries ==

The Federal Ministry of Culture, the Federal Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection, and the Federal Ministry of Energy are among these ministries.

Russia, by 1993 constitution, is a symmetric (with the possibility of an asymmetric configuration) federation.
Unlike the Soviet asymmetric model of the RSFSR, where only republics were "subjects of the federation", the current constitution raised the status of other regions to the level of republics and made all regions equal with the title "subject of the federation".
The regions of Russia have reserved areas of competence, but no regions have sovereignty, do not have the status of a sovereign state, do not have the right to indicate any sovereignty in their constitutions and do not have the right to secede from the country.
The laws of the regions cannot contradict federal laws.

The federal subjects have equal representation—two delegates each—in the Federation Council, the upper house of the Federal Assembly.
They do, however, differ in the degree of autonomy they enjoy.
The federal districts of Russia were established by Putin in 2000 to facilitate central government control of the federal subjects.
Originally seven, currently there are eight federal districts, each headed by an envoy appointed by the president.

== Federal cities ==

Federal cities are comparable to oblasts and constitute a separate administrative unit.
The three federal cities are Moscow, Sevastopol, and Saint Petersburg.
These three cities function as separate regions and have the status of a separate federal subject.
Russia has three autonomous cities, which are Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Sevastopol.

Petersburg are the two federal cities [cite: 883].

Each federal city consists of other cities within it.

== Republics and ethnic federalism ==

Each republic often represents one or more ethnic groups and was defined based on the dominant non-Russian ethnic groups, though the boundaries of the republics do not always align with ethnic lines.
The regions in the rest of the country, which are predominantly inhabited by Russians, were formed based purely on administrative criteria, while territories with smaller non-Russian minorities receive a lower status of an Autonomous Territory or Autonomous Okrug.
Only the republics have the right to enact their own constitutions, and each republic has its own constitution, an elected government, and its own budget.
These republics determine the directions of socio-economic policy in the region, oversee land use issues, and are responsible for the use of the state budget.

== Autonomy and division of powers ==

Republics and oblasts possess broad autonomy, and most of the republics have autonomy in their internal affairs.
Defense matters, foreign affairs matters, energy supply matters, social policy matters, and tax-related matters are under the authority of the federal government.
Public security matters, culture matters, and land use matters are under the control of local authorities.

== Historical evolution and centralization ==

According to the 1993 Constitution, the Russian Federation consisted of 21 republics, 6 krais (territories), 49 oblasts (regions), and 11 autonomous okrugs.
The Russian Federation has 21 republics and 68 oblasts (regions) according to the 1993 Constitution.
There were originally 89 federal subjects in 1993.
Asymmetric contractual federalism allowed constituent states to negotiate their power with the center in Moscow at times.
Attempts were made to limit asymmetric 'contractual federalism' under President Boris Yeltsin.
Putin's centralization policy led to a reduction in the number of federal subjects.

== Treaties and secession attempts ==

Several national regions, including Tatarstan, Bashkortostan, Yakutia, and Chechnya, adopted a line to easily leave the Federation.
Federal treaties were signed between the Russian Federation and Federation subjects on March 31, 1992.
Tatarstan and Chechnya refused to sign the federal treaties.
Bashkortostan signed the treaty under certain conditions.

== Federal districts and economic regions ==

Russia is divided into 12 economic regions.
The federal districts and economic regions are further divided into 85 subjects.
A new North Caucasian Federal District was established in 2010 and was separated from the Southern Federal District in 2010.
The Crimean Federal District was established in 2014, its establishment was temporary, and it was merged into the Southern Federal District two years later.

== Territorial changes and mergers ==

There are recent efforts in the Russian Federation to merge regions, including oblasts, republics, and autonomous okrugs.
There are currently 83 federal subjects.

== Disputed territories ==

Two of Russia's federal subjects have limited international recognition, specifically the Republic of Crimea and the Federal City of Sevastopol.
These territories are claimed to be part of Russian territory.

== Demographics and geography of subjects ==

Besides Moscow and St.
Petersburg, the most populous federal subjects in Russia are the Krasnodar Krai, Moscow Oblast, and Rostov Oblast.
The Republic of Bashkortostan and the Republic of Tatarstan are also among the most populous federal subjects in Russia.
The Republic of Sakha is the largest federal subject, with an area of over 3 million square kilometers that is equal to three-quarters of the European Union's area.
The population of the Republic of Sakha is only 950,000.
The smallest federal subjects are densely populated Caucasian republics and central Russian regions.

The Republic of Tatarstan holds a favorable position at the Volga-Kama water junction, and its capital is the city of Kazan.
The Kalmyk Republic is located along the lower Volga.
One representative is from the regional executive.

== Constitutional status and federal structure ==

The subjects of the Federation are the highest-level territorial units of the Russian Federation and have variable political and economic autonomy.
The federal subjects differ significantly in terms of population, area, and relative wealth.
Another characteristic is the number of deputies in regional parliaments, and a further characteristic is specific legislative competencies.
The federal subjects share the characteristic that their tax sovereignty exists only minimally.
The competencies of the federal subjects have been significantly curtailed in favor of the central authority.
Shared responsibilities between the federation and lower levels are effectively perceived by Moscow, which exercises control over shared competencies.
Questions have arisen regarding whether Russia still functions as a federal state or has become a unitary state.
The Republic of Tatarstan had previously negotiated special rights.
The use of the title 'President' for a head of a federal subject was explicitly banned, a ban that specifically applied to the Republic of Tatarstan.

== Federal districts and administrative hierarchy ==

Each federal district combines multiple federal subjects into a larger unit.
The North Caucasus Federal District was created in 2010 by being split off from the Southern Federal District and became the eighth federal district.
Crimea formed its own ninth Federation Circle starting March 21, 2014, but this circle was dissolved on July 28, 2016, after which Crimea was attached to the Southern Russia Federation Circle.
There is a third independent administrative level alongside two hierarchical federal levels, where the first federal level is the Federation Circle and the second federal level is the Federation Subject.
Federal districts are not subjects of the Russian Federation, are not subordinate to federal subjects in terms of administration, and belong directly to the subordination of the Federation's administration.
Representatives of the Federation in the federal districts act as liaisons that connect the federal subjects with the Federation itself and are responsible for ensuring that the subjects act in accordance with the Federation's laws.

== Municipal self-government ==

This third level is municipal self-government and is called Rajon.
The administrative heads of the districts are directly elected by the population.
Regions are administratively superior to municipal self-government bodies and have the authority to issue instructions to them.
This distinction applies in contrast to republics.

== Executive leadership and titles ==

A head of state stands at the top of the federal subjects, which are led by the head of administration commonly referred to as a governor.
The subjects of the Russian Federation have an executive power that includes a head, governor, or mayor, and the region has a governor appointed at the federal level.

== Legislative bodies and representation ==

The subjects of the Russian Federation have a legislative power.
Each republic has its own parliament, and some of these legislative bodies are single-chamber systems while others are two-chamber systems.
The parliamentary representation in the oblasts and krais consists of only one chamber.
The region has locally elected legislators.

== The special case of Chechnya ==

Chechnya plays a special role within the federal system of Russia and is de facto a 'state within a state' that is largely detached from Russian justice and federal police forces.
Religious freedom is no longer granted due to a Sunni Islamist ruling ideology.
Kadyrov has his own troops, and the Republic of Chechnya is bound to Russia solely by the personal loyalty between Kadyrov and Putin.
Kadyrov publicly demonstrated the loyalty of these troops to Putin, and the existence of these troops serves as a warning.

== Types of federal subjects ==

There are several autonomous divisions within Russia, and the remaining 39 federal subjects are other types of administrative divisions.
Forty-six of these parts are oblasts (provinces), 21 are republics, 9 are krais (territories), 4 are autonomous oblasts (autonomous regions), 2 are federal cities, and 1 is an autonomous province.

== Republics ==

Republics are territories administered by a president as head of state and a prime minister as head of government.
Each republic has its own constitution, a parliament, and a head of state or a similar position elected directly.
Republics are represented by the federal government in international affairs and are intended to be entities dedicated to specific ethnic minorities.
One of these regions is Buryatia.
One of these regions is Tuva.
Kazan is the capital of Tatarstan.

== Oblasts and Krais ==

Oblasts are regions administered by a governor, and each region has a governor and a locally elected legislature.
Krais are essentially the same as regions, though the name 'krai' is historical in origin and krais were originally border regions.
Later, krais included administrative divisions containing autonomous districts or autonomous regions.
The Kaliningrad Oblast is a federal subject of Russia and is geographically separated from the rest of the Russian Federation by other countries.

== Autonomous divisions ==

Autonomous oblasts are regions administered by a governor, and the Jewish Autonomous Oblast is the autonomous province administered by a governor.
Each autonomous district is part of a territory or a province, and initially these districts were autonomous entities within regions and krais created for specific ethnic minorities.
In 1990, the status of these districts was raised to be equal to that of the subjects, though the autonomous district of Chukotka is an exception while all other autonomous districts are administratively subordinate to a krai or a region.
Historically, autonomous regions were administrative units subordinate to krais, and in 1990 autonomous regions were elevated to the status of republics, with all autonomous regions except the Jewish Autonomous Oblast being elevated to the status of republics in 1990.

== Regional government structure ==

Subjects of the Russian Federation have legislative bodies and executive bodies [cite: 2877].
Every region has a legislative (representative) body, which is called a legislative assembly or duma [cite: 2877].
Every region has an executive body, which is the government [cite: 2877].
All subjects of the federation have a position of highest official, referred to as head or governor [cite: 2877].
The head of a region appoints the regional government [cite: 2877].
The electoral system for regional bodies is analogous to elections for the Duma [cite: 2877].
The state bodies of power in federal subjects are defined by general principles established by the federation.
The President nominates the candidate for the regional head [cite: 2878].
The local parliament approves the candidate [cite: 2878].
A newly elected parliament approves the candidates [cite: 2878].
The president has the right to dissolve the parliament [cite: 2878].

== Internal administrative structure ==

Federal subjects have their own administrative-territorial structure.
As a general rule, the main administrative-territorial units within a federal subject are districts and cities of regional significance.
Districts and cities of regional significance are primary administrative-territorial units in a federal subject.
Regional significance includes republican, krai, and district levels.
Older postal address structures remain in use.

== Federal districts ==

Federal districts are a level of federal government administration that are not administrative units or subunits of state government.
They are directly subordinate to the federal government and are not mentioned in the state constitution [cite: 3885].
Federal districts do not manage regional affairs, do not have their own powers, and exist solely to monitor compliance between federal and regional legal bodies [cite: 3885].
They also exist solely to ensure government oversight of public administration, the judiciary, and federal agencies operating in regions [cite: 3885].
District envoys serve as liaison agents between the federal subjects and the federal government and are primarily responsible for supervising compliance by federal subjects with federal laws.
The administrators of federal districts are responsible for maintaining contact between the federal districts and the federal government.
The Central Federal District, the North Caucasian Federal District, the Northwest Federal District, the Far Eastern Federal District, the Siberian Federal District, the Urals Federal District, and the Privolzhsky Federal District are federal districts of Russia.

The administrators of federal districts are responsible for ensuring that federal districts act in accordance with federal laws.

== Municipalities ==

As of October 1, 2021, Russia has 1,118 municipalities with city rights, 18 of which are located in the annexed Crimea.

The merger of Evenkia and Taymyr was with Krasnoyarsk Krai and took place on December 1, 2005.

Two federal subjects are located on the Crimean Peninsula, one of which is Sevastopol.
The status of Crimea and Sevastopol as part of Russia is not recognized, and Sevastopol and the Republic of Crimea are not internationally recognized as part of Russia.

== Characteristics of republics ==

Republics are considered autonomous regions, and there is 1 autonomous oblast.
Each republic has its own constitution, its own parliament, and its own president.

== Characteristics of krais and oblasts ==

Each oblast is governed by an elected executive and has local legislative bodies.
Krais are essentially similar to oblasts, and there are 9 krais (regions).
Krais were initially established in border regions and later became administrative centers for autonomous oblasts and autonomous okrugs.

== Characteristics of autonomous okrugs and oblasts ==

There are four autonomous okrugs (autonomous regions) that were originally established within krais and oblasts for ethnic minorities.
In 1990, the status of autonomous okrugs was elevated, and as a result of this elevation, autonomous okrugs were included in the administrative region status.
The Jewish Autonomous Oblast is an autonomous oblast that was originally considered a type of oblast and was originally established as part of a krai.
In 1990, the status of the Jewish Autonomous Oblast was elevated, and the Jewish Autonomous Oblast now holds the status of an independent oblast.
The autonomous oblast is now an independent autonomous region and is directly within the state structure of the Russian Federation.

== Other administrative divisions ==

Russia's other administrative divisions include economic regions, military districts, and judicial districts.

This classification was established by a law passed in 1997.
