== Federal districts and their evolution ==

Eight large federal regions were recently added, with five located in Europe and three in Asia.
These regions function as an administrative institution between the aforementioned institutions and the national level.
Putin issued a decree on May 13, 2000, which established seven federal districts in Russia based on geographical principles: the Central Federal District, the Northwestern Federal District, the Southern Federal District, the Volga Federal District, the Ural Federal District, the Siberian Federal District, and the Far Eastern Federal District.
Medvedev issued a decree on January 19, 2010, establishing a new federal district called the North Caucasus Federal District that was separated from the Southern Federal District.
The decree also established a new federal district in the Crimean Peninsula named the Crimea Federal District.
The Southern Federal District and the Crimea Federal District were merged.
Russian President Putin signed an order on July 28, 2016.

Putin signed a presidential decree in November 2018 that transferred the Republic of Buryatia and the Zabaykalsky Krai to the Far Eastern Federal District.
The Republic of Buryatia and the Zabaykalsky Krai were no longer part of the Siberian Federal District.
The merger resulted in a new Southern Federal District.

== Economic disparities ==

The Moscow region has a prosperous lifestyle, and per capita income in the Moscow region quickly reached levels of top European economies.
Most other regions, rural areas, and regions inhabited by ethnic minorities in Asia have fallen far behind.

Russia had the world's fifth-largest diplomatic network in 2019.
It maintains diplomatic relations with 190 United Nations member states, four partially-recognised states, and three United Nations observer states; along with 144 embassies.
Russia is one of the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council.
It has historically been a great power, and a former superpower as the leading constituent of the former Soviet Union.
Russia is a member of the G20, the OSCE, and the APEC.
Russia also takes a leading role in organisations such as the CIS, the EAEU, the CSTO, the SCO, and BRICS.

Russia maintains close relations with neighbouring Belarus, which is a part of the Union State, a supranational confederation of the two states.
Serbia has been a historically close ally of Russia, as both countries share a strong mutual cultural, ethnic, and religious affinity.
India is the largest customer of Russian military equipment, and the two countries share a strong strategic and diplomatic relationship since the Soviet era.
Russia wields influence across the geopolitically important South Caucasus and Central Asia; and the two regions have been described as Russia's "backyard".

In the 21st century Russia has pursued an aggressive foreign policy aimed at securing regional dominance and international influence, as well as increasing domestic support for the government.
Military intervention in the post-soviet states include a war with Georgia in 2008, and the invasion and destabilisation of Ukraine beginning in 2014.
Russia has also sought to increase its influence in the Middle East, most significantly through military intervention in the Syrian civil war.
Cyberwarfare and airspace violations, along with electoral interference, have been used to increase perceptions of Russian power.
Russia's relations with neighbouring Ukraine and the Western world—especially the United States, the European Union, the United Nations and NATO—have collapsed; especially following the start of the Russo-Ukrainian War in 2014 and the consequent escalation in 2022.
Relations between Russia and China have significantly strengthened bilaterally and economically; due to shared political interests.
Turkey and Russia share a complex strategic, energy, and defence relationship.
Russia maintains cordial relations with Iran, as it is a strategic and economic ally.
Russia has also increasingly pushed to expand its influence across the Arctic, Asia-Pacific, Africa, the Middle East, and Latin America.
According to the Economist Intelligence Unit, two-thirds of the world's population live in countries such as China or India that are neutral or leaning towards Russia.

== Succession to the Soviet Union ==

The Russian Federation is recognized as the successor to the former Soviet Union under international law.
Russia has taken the place of the former Soviet Union and is often described as the successor to a previous superpower.[342,343,344,345,346,347,348,349,350,351,352,353,354,355] Russia continues to fulfill the international obligations of the Soviet Union and has assumed the rights and obligations of the Soviet Union under international treaties.
Russia has assumed the permanent seat of the Soviet Union in the United Nations Security Council and holds the permanent seat of the former Soviet Union in other international organizations.
Russia has assumed membership in other international organizations from the Soviet Union and has assumed rights and obligations regarding international treaties and debts from the Soviet Union.

== International Organizations and Forums ==

Russia is a member of the G8 and the Council of Europe.
Russia is a leading member of the G8, but its participation and membership in the G8 are currently suspended.
Russia joined the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in 2005 as an observer, not a member.
Russia maintains strong and positive relations with other BRICS countries.

== Relations with NATO and the West ==

The NATO-Russia Council was established in 2002 to promote cooperation between NATO and Russia.[18,19] The NATO strategy relies on military deterrence and simultaneous dialogue, constituting a dual-track approach towards the Russian Federation.[3,4,6] This strategy is interpreted in Moscow as confirmation of suspicions that the West follows an aggressive policy against Russia.[7,5] Russian politicians have protested against the 'demonization' of Russia, which is also found in Western media alongside Western claims about a 'threatening danger from the East'.[8,9,10] According to the Russian viewpoint, there is no threatening danger from the East.
Criticism of the Russian political system is a significant aspect of Russia's relations with the West.[356,357,358,359] Former President Vladimir Putin called for a strategic partnership that includes creating shared spaces between the European Union and Russia.[366,367] The NATO-Russia Council was established in 2002 with the goal of working together to seek opportunities for joint cooperation.[368,369] Russia's involvement in Georgia in 2008, the gas exchange between Russia and Ukraine, and the long-term cessation of gas supplied to Europe harmed Russia's integration with Europe.[17,18,19]

== Strategic Partnerships and Regional Relations ==

The country particularly sought to strengthen relations with the People's Republic of China, and a friendship treaty was signed between the countries.
An oil pipeline crossing Siberia was built to meet China's increasing energy needs.

== Multilateral Diplomacy and Conflict Resolution ==

Russia participates in the Middle East Quartet, the resolution of the Kosovo conflict, and six-party talks with North Korea.

== Foreign Policy Structure and Domestic Drivers ==

Russia is attempting to regain its historical status as a great power on the international level and acts as a rival to the superpower United States on the international stage.
Political analysts view these events as outcomes of Moscow's drastically changing domestic and foreign policy.
The hypothesis suggests that the rise of authoritarian-nationalist trends in Russia will lead to a more aggressive foreign policy.
Another theory links Moscow's changing foreign policy to Russian fears concerning so-called 'color revolutions' in countries such as Ukraine, which might also find supporters within Russia.
Moscow may be trying to focus the Russian public's attention on conflicts with other countries and to garner support for a more aggressive foreign policy.
These Western actors attempted to expand their sphere of influence into Ukraine.
Sergei Sipljaef is an expert in international law who fears that Russia's policy of self-isolation and political campaign against the West will lead to bankruptcy in the long term.
Foreign policy is determined by the president, while the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs is responsible for implementing it.
The Minister of Foreign Affairs is appointed by the President.
Russia has a multi-directional foreign policy.

These visits strongly accelerated the development of Russia-Azerbaijan relations.
