Russia began to see itself as a significant player in the Middle East, frequently intervenes in local conflicts in these regions, and adopted a new doctrine as part of this process.[775,1821] According to this doctrine, Russia is a natural ally of several of its Muslim neighbors, and this alliance is based on opposition to Western power.[775,1821] Relations with Saudi Arabia deteriorated after Saudi Arabia supported Chechen separatists.
The Syrian Civil War began in 2011, during which Western countries supported the opposition groups while Russia provided military and economic aid to the Bashar al-Assad regime and Iran also provided aid to the Bashar al-Assad regime.
This situation made the conflict resemble a proxy war between Western countries and Russia and deepened the rivalry between these opposing sides.
The Russian Federation Army began direct military intervention to support the Assad regime on September 30, 2015, involving air raids conducted by the Russian Aerospace Forces in Syria.
The situation in the war, which had been stalemate, shifted significantly in favor of the Assad regime, while Turkey initially supported opposition groups aiming to overthrow the Assad regime in coordination with Western countries.

In 2015, a Russian Air Force aircraft violated airspace near Turkey and Syria and was shot down by the Turkish Air Force.
Turkey opposed Western countries regarding their response to Kurdish forces and was brought into the process of post-war Syria settlement.
Egypt, Iraq, and Israel are skeptical about the stability of Syria after the fall of the Assad regime.

== Relations with the European Union and Council of Europe ==

The vote for Russia's exclusion from the Council of Europe took place on March 16 and was voted on unanimously because Russia no longer respects the values of the organization and failed to honor any commitments made during its accession.
Russian citizens no longer have access to the European Court of Human Rights, where Russian cases represent one quarter of all cases before the court, including the case of anti-corruption activist Alexei Navalny.
Former President Vladimir Putin advocated for a strategic alliance, one dimension of which is the establishment of four common spaces between Russia and the European Union.
The influence of Russia on the countries in the region weakened after the fall of the Warsaw Pact, and some of these countries joined Western alliances such as NATO and the European Union.
Russia began to intensify its reactions to perceived attempts by countries in its sphere of influence to approach the West [769,1822].
Russia intervened in votes and protests in Spain, where Spain traditionally tended to favor Russia, and these interventions shifted countries such as Spain to support alliances and actions aimed at reducing Russia's influence.
Turkey was previously an adversary of Russia in several regional disputes.

== Relations with Central Asia and the Caucasus ==

Russia has friendly relations with Azerbaijan, Armenia, and the Central Asian republics.
Russia considers Central Asia its "sphere of special influence".
Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan are members of the Eurasian Economic Union, of which Russia is one of five members.

== Relations with Belarus and the Union State ==

Russia holds significant influence over the government of some of these alliance members, such as Belarus.
The Union of Russia and Belarus is an economic project formed on April 2, 1996, that predicts a monetary union.
Concerns arose regarding Russia's cooperation with Belarus.

== Relations with the United States and Western interference ==

The country signed a bilateral agreement with the United States as a precursor to future accession to the WTO.
Simultaneously, reports began in the West linking Russia to election interference attempts in Western countries, an issue that became part of public discourse surrounding Russian interference in the 2016 United States presidential election.
Western governments accused Russia of a series of assassinations of Russian defectors with high profiles who were hosted by Western countries.

== Relations with Turkey and Spain ==

These countries sought to distance themselves from Russia and to align closer with the West.

== Relations with Africa and the Global South ==

Russia supported economically failed states and received cooperation from these states in exchange for its support.
Russia intensified its efforts to strengthen its standing in some Sub-Saharan African countries due to the war.
According to Pentagon reports, Russia's diplomatic activities in these regions are accompanied by military operations by Wagner Group.

== Relations with Israel and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation ==

Russia serves as an observer state in the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.
There are diplomatic relations between Israel and Russia.

== Relations with the Arctic and resource interests ==

A specific reason for monitoring the Arctic is oil resources.

== Relations with the G8 and G20 ==

Russia is a member of the G8, which consists of eight industrially most developed and economically most powerful countries.
Russia was excluded from the G8 after it annexed Crimea in 2014.

== Regional economic and security organizations ==

Russia is one of the founding members of the Eurasian Economic Community and leads the organization.
The founding members signed the project on October 10, 2000, and all member states ratified the project by May 31, 2001.
The Eurasian Economic Community evolved from the Commonwealth of Independent States project.
Russia joined the Central Asian Cooperation Organization, and the membership began in 2004.

== Multilateral diplomacy and conflict resolution ==

Russia participated in the Madrid Quartet and promoted a solution to the Kosovo conflict.
The country addressed matters regarding nuclear proliferation and participated in six-party talks with North Korea.
The country participates in the Middle East Quartet and Six-Party Talks with North Korea.

== NATO expansion and sphere of influence ==

Russia considers Eastern Europe part of its sphere of influence and views these regions as part of its sphere of influence.
The threat comes from the expansion of NATO into Eastern Europe.
According to reports from Western intelligence agencies, Russia acted during this period to undermine the stability of governments in various Eastern European countries.
The entity is a leading member of the Organization of Turkic States.
Russia continued the implementation of international commitments made by the Soviet Union.

== International organizations and legal frameworks ==

Russia became the 39th member to join the Council of Europe in 1996.
Russia ratified the European Convention on Human Rights in 1998.
The legal basis for the relationship between the European Union and Russia is the 1997 Cooperation and Partnership Agreement.
The Commonwealth of Independent States is composed of nine former Soviet republics and former constituent republics of the Soviet Union.
Russia was a member of the G8 until its membership was suspended in March 2014 because Russia forcibly annexed Crimea.
A treaty was signed on December 8, 1999, and the ratification took place in 1997.
The government of the Russian Federation is the official successor regime to the Soviet Union and has succeeded the Soviet Union in other international organizations.
Russia is a member of the Middle East Quartet and participates in the Six-Party Talks regarding North Korea.
South Africa and Brazil are members of BRICs.

== Relations with China ==

Russia maintains strong and positive relations with other BRIC countries.
China is a historical ally of Russia.
Russia and China signed a Treaty of Friendship.
The People's Republic of China signed the Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation with Russia in 2001.
The strengthening of ties included the signing of the Treaty of Friendship.
Russia and China built the Trans-Siberian oil pipeline.
The strengthening of ties included the construction of a trans-Siberian oil pipeline.
The trans-Siberian oil pipeline was aimed at meeting China's growing energy needs.
Russia and China built a gas pipeline from Siberia to China.
The country signed and built the Siberia-China gas pipeline.
China has deepened its relations within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.
China has deepened its relations within BRICS.
Russia's territory came into contact with Chinese territory after expanding into Siberia.
Since the Qing Dynasty, Russia occupied some territories of the Qing Empire through war, unequal treaties, and mediation.
Territories occupied by Tsarist Russia and the Soviet Union from Qing China included Sakhalin Island.
Territories occupied by Tsarist Russia and the Soviet Union from Qing China included lands east of the Ussuri River.
Territories occupied by Tsarist Russia and the Soviet Union from Qing China included lands north of the Heilongjiang River to Mount Khingan.
The Soviet Union played a key role in the founding of the Communist Party of China.
The Soviet Union played a key role in the establishment of the Chinese government by the Communist Party.
The European Parliament designated Russia as a state sponsor of terrorism.

The Soviet Union played a key role in the independence of Outer Mongolia.
The Soviet Union provided significant assistance to China's industrialization projects after the Chinese Civil War, which helped China establish a heavy industry system.
Relations between the two countries later deteriorated, leading to a rupture, and following the rupture, the industrialization projects were interrupted.
Diplomatic relations between the two countries were restored in 1989.
Chinese Foreign Minister Li Zhaoxing and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov signed the 'Supplementary Agreement on the Eastern Section of the China-Russia Border between the People's Republic of China and the Russian Federation' in Beijing.
The agreement was based on the previously signed 'Agreement on the Eastern Section of the Sino-Soviet Border' and the 'Agreement on the Western Section of the China-Russia Border'.
The agreement determined that the two countries would divide Heixiazi Island.

== Relations with the United States ==

Russia was friendly with the United States and NATO at the time of the founding of the Russian Federation.
Russia developed friendlier relations with the United States since the end of the Soviet Union [18,1609].
Russia and the US had a close relationship based on the anti-terror war following the September 11 attacks.
Relations between Russia and the United States deteriorated after Putin's initial presidency.
Relations worsened due to issues such as the Iraq War and Iranian nuclear program suspicions.
A previous agreement between Gorbachev and President Bush that NATO would not expand eastward was broken, and NATO actually expanded eastward despite the previous agreement.
The United States is Russia's most important trading partner, yet Russia and the United States often take opposite sides in conflicts.
A change in administration occurred in the United States in December 2016.
Donald Trump had previously stated he was pro-Russian.
Anti-Russian sentiment has been rising within the United States.
Russia interfered in the 2016 United States presidential election [2213,2214].
Retaliatory measures were taken due to Russia's failure to fulfill the Minsk peace agreement regarding the Ukraine conflict [2213,2214].
Russia withdrew from the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty after being accused of violating the treaty [2213,2214].
A change of government occurred in the United States in January 2021.
The new administration is led by Joe Biden.
Joe Biden has publicly stated he is anti-Russian.
Major Western European countries centered around the United States have not yet shown signs of lifting or easing sanctions.

In December, Russia adopted the 'Dima Yakovlev Law' in response to the American 'Magnitsky Act', and the Dima Yakovlev Law was enacted as a result of the so-called Dima Yakovlev case.
Since late 2016, there have been suspicions of Russian interference in the US presidential election.
Russia established companies in the West to secretly purchase electronic components, which were ordered from US manufacturers and shipped back to Russia for packaging and export to Russian companies.
These components are used by the Russian Ministry of Defense, the Federal Security Service (FSB) of Russia, and Russian legal entities involved in designing weapons and nuclear warheads.
The activity involved purchasing advanced, high-tech electronic components and smuggling them to Russia, which helped enhance the capabilities of Russian intelligence agencies and contributed to the modernization of the Russian military and Russia's nuclear weapons program.
FBI agents stated that this activity significantly undermined US national security.
Russian companies purchase electronic components from the United States with an annual value of approximately 2 billion USD.

== Relations with NATO and European security ==

The NATO-Russia Council was established in 2002, allowing the United States, Russia, and 27 other NATO countries to cooperate in the future.
Finland and Sweden applied for NATO membership, with Finland sharing a border with Russia.
Finland joined NATO in April 2023, making NATO a 31-member alliance.
NATO expanded to include Northern Europe, not just Eastern Europe, extending the border between NATO and Russia to over 2,600 kilometers.
This expansion was seen as militarily squeezing Russia, prompting the Russian government to strongly protest against the United States.
The United States stated that it would not encourage attacks or invasions into Russian territory.
The United States and NATO are expanding missile defense bases in Eastern European countries that were formerly Soviet satellite states without consulting the Russian government.

== Relations with Latin America and Africa ==

Russia is strengthening its relations with anti-American countries in Central and South America.
Cuba has maintained diplomatic relations with Russia after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
Russia has a partnership with Brazil that covers space, military technology, and telecommunications.
South Africa had formal diplomatic relations with the Soviet Union and has a close relationship with Russia as its successor state.
South Africa established full diplomatic relations with Russia on February 28, 1992.

== Relations with Japan ==

Another historical issue is the Northern Territories dispute, and Japan refers to the South Kuril Islands as the Northern Territories.
Japan was occupied by the Soviet Union with regard to the Southern Kuril Islands after World War II, and the occupation occurred in August 1945 following Japan's defeat in World War II.
The Soviet Union justified its occupation as a victor of the war and refused to return the islands.
Russia took over the Kuril Islands after the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
Japan demands the return of the Southern Kuril Islands, and Japan and Russia began negotiations over the Southern Kuril Islands in the 1990s.
Japan has been negotiating with Russia, and negotiations regarding the islands are currently ongoing.
The dispute over territory has prevented Japan and Russia from signing a formal peace treaty since the end of the war.
Incidents involving fishermen being shot and captured resulted from these issues, and resource disputes, such as Sakhalin-2, have also arisen.
Russians have a higher level of trust in Japan compared to the United States and compared to the United Kingdom.
A 2017 survey by the UK's BBC found that Russians have a favorable view of Japan.
According to a 2022 Cabinet Office survey of Japanese nationals, only 13.1% feel an affinity for Russia.
The figure is lower than that of China, and 20.6% of people in China feel affinity for Russia.

Japanese citizens are allowed to travel to South Sakhalin.
Civil cooperation between Japan and Russia has been gradually increasing since 2011.
Russia's attitude is to firmly defend the Southern Kuril Islands, and high-ranking Russian officials have visited the islands multiple times for inspections.
Japan has tended to respond with condemnation.
A Japanese yakuza organization sent bullets to the Russian embassy in Japan.
The Japanese government urged its citizens not to visit the islands with Russian visas, though some Japanese citizens visited the islands using Russian visas despite the warning.

== Relations with Georgia ==

Diplomatic relations between Georgia and the Russian Federation were established on July 1, 1992.
Georgia severed diplomatic relations with the Russian Federation starting September 3, 2008.
The Swiss Embassy's section for Russian Federation interests opened in Georgia in March 2009.

== Diplomatic structure and global strategy ==

The policy on international relations is determined by the President and executed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The world has transitioned to a multipolar system, and experts debate Russia's position in this new system.
Russia is classified as a potential superpower.
Since the 21st century, Russia has rapidly expanded its influence, particularly in Europe and Central Asia, by using abundant oil and natural gas resources as leverage.
The subject has regained significant influence compared to its weakness after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
The Novichok nerve agent scandal is one of the reasons for this criticism, and diplomatic relations were severed.
Russia sent weapons to 56 countries between 2010 and 2014, while the United States is the largest exporter of conventional weapons in the world.
These relations were strengthened through the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, and the country intensified cooperation in energy development with Central Asian countries.
This strengthening of ties is centered around the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.

== Diplomatic status and international organizations ==

Russia is considered the successor state of the Soviet Union in diplomatic matters and assumed the majority of the Soviet Union's international obligations and rights after its dissolution.
The Russian Federation assumed rights, obligations, and assets under international treaties [cite: 2650,2651].
Russia assumed the Soviet Union's permanent seat on the UN Security Council largely due to its retained status as a nuclear power and holds veto power in the UN Security Council [cite: 3267].
Russia's participation in international cooperation increased after the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
The relationship of the Russian Federation with other countries depends primarily on external trade links.
Russia is a member of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Investment Bank (IIB) [cite: 2754,2755,2756].
Russia is one of the founding members of the Commonwealth of Independent States, which was founded on December 8, 1991.
Russia is a member of the East Asia Summit.
The country was a member of the Council of Europe from 1996 to 2022.
The G8 is an informal grouping of economically developed states.
The country was part of the G8 from 1997 to 2014.
Russia is a member of the G8.

Russia is a member of the European Council and was formerly a member of the Group of Seven [22,831,2522,4035,4036].
The Russian Federation is recognized as the successor to the Soviet Union in international law.

== Relations with the European Union and Western states ==

A partnership and friendship agreement was signed between Russia and the European Union in 1994.
As a result, Russia increased its export share to European Union countries, with the increase reaching up to 40 percent.
Relations with highly developed Western European states were strengthened, and the share of trade with these states increased to between 50% and 60%.
Germany, Italy, Japan, the United States, and the United Kingdom are trade partners.
Russia's foreign policy has maintained an adversarial stance towards the West since the Cold War.
Russia signed a military cooperation agreement with NATO that included joint military exercises.
The Russia-NATO Council was established in 2002 and consists of the 26 NATO member states and Russia.
Russia places high importance on East Asia, including South Korea.
Russia's foreign policy became more aggressive starting in 2007.
Russia was excluded from the G8 due to its aggressive foreign policy.

== Relations with China and East Asia ==

A friendship treaty was signed between China and Russia, oil and gas business development occurred between the two nations, and relations between the two powers reached a special state due to these factors.
Russia places high importance on East Asia to a degree comparable to Europe.
President Yeltsin visited South Korea and Japan in 1992.
Russia is nominally an ally of anti-Western states such as China, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Iraq, and Vietnam.
North Korea, China, Cuba, Vietnam, Laos, and Syria are socialist countries closely linked to the Communist Party of the Russian Federation, and Russia maintains closer contact with these socialist countries than with others.
The Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Russia exists, as do the Consulate General of the Republic of Korea in Vladivostok and the Consulate General of the Republic of Korea in St.
Petersburg.
Russia participated in six-party talks with North Korea.
Russia is losing ground to China in Central Asia.

== Relations with Georgia and the South Caucasus ==

The Swiss Embassy's section for Georgian interests opened in the Russian Federation on the same day as the opening in Georgia.
Economic relations between Georgia and Russia were developing quite actively until the end of 2005, trade volume was increasing until the end of 2005, and an intergovernmental commission for economic cooperation was functioning until the end of 2005.
Starting from December 2005, exports of plant-origin products from Georgia to Russia were banned due to violations of phytosanitary norms.
By the end of March 2006, imports and sales of Georgian wine, wine materials, brandy, and shushpuna wines in Russia were banned.
Direct investments from the Russian Federation into Georgia's economy increased sharply in 2003, were primarily made in the energy sector and processing industry, and decreased sharply in 2006.
Russia severed diplomatic relations with Georgia, recognized the independence of the Republic of Abkhazia, recognized the independence of South Ossetia, and does not have diplomatic relations with Georgia.
The conflict between Russia and Georgia was caused by a territorial dispute, Russia stationed troops in South Ossetia and Abkhazia, and member states of the Collective Security Treaty Organization supported Russia.
A friendly agreement was signed on September 17 between Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

== Relations with the Baltic states and Lithuania ==

Lithuania established diplomatic relations in 1991, the Russian Embassy is located in Vilnius, and a consulate operated in Klaipeda until 2022.
Ambassadors from both countries were recalled, and in April 2022, the diplomatic representation level was downgraded by Lithuania's Ministry of Foreign Affairs to apply to both Moscow and Vilnius, with Chargés d'affaires now leading the missions in place of ambassadors.
Sergei Karaganov recommended actively exacerbating human rights issues in the Baltic states to slow down their accession to the European Union and NATO, a position Russia has held since 2001[23,375,376].

== Relations with CIS states and post-Soviet reintegration ==

Trade and economic relations with CIS countries were elevated to a new level.
Russia announced its position on March 14, 2009, and welcomed a proposal for a single currency presented by Kazakhstan for the Eurasian Economic Community.
Russia is currently seeking economic and political reintegration of the post-Soviet area, in which Kazakhstan and Belarus are participating.
The establishment of the Eurasian Economic Union is an example of this reintegration.

== Military interventions and security cooperation ==

Russia's intervention occurred in September 2015 to support the government of Syria, which fought against various terrorist groups including ISIS (Islamic State), Al-Nusra Front, and Al-Qaeda.
Russian armed forces joined the Syrian civil war on September 30, 2015.
Russian mercenaries (Wagner Group) engaged in military operations in several African countries.
Russia is a potential superpower state.
Political scientist Sergey Karaganov proposed a strategy in 1992 aimed to restore Russia's influence and implement Russia's interests in territories lost after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
Sergei Karaganov's doctrine is based on three considerations: that there are still large Russian communities in the lost territories which can help Russia implement its interests in countries that have gained independence; that economic levers and investments must be used to achieve influence; and that the role of the Russian language must be preserved and bilingualism is possible in these countries.

== Relations with developing nations and BRICS ==

Russia is criticized for using energy as a means of control.
Russia maintains close cooperation with developing nations such as Iran, China, Venezuela, and Cuba.
Russia is a major friendly country for Nepal, where it built the Pathlaiya-Dhulikhel section of the Mahendra Highway and established numerous factories.
Russia is an active global partner of ASEAN.
Tightening cooperation with BRICS countries is a clear trend in current politics.
The main goals of the group include creating a new currency system and increasing the role of developing countries in global financial institutions.

== Foreign policy structure and diplomatic network ==

The President of the Russian Federation determines its foreign policy, while the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation implements it.
Russia plays a major role in resolving international conflicts, participated in the Middle East Quartet, facilitated the resolution of the Kosovo conflict, and addressed issues regarding nuclear weapons proliferation.

== Non-diplomatic relations ==

Russia does not have diplomatic relations with Bhutan, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Solomon Islands, and Ukraine.
The general nature and structural changes in these relationships depend primarily on external trade links.

== International status and succession ==

The Russian Federation is recognized as the successor state to the former Soviet Union and is recognized by international law.
Russia assumed the permanent seat of the USSR in the UN Security Council, assumed membership in other international organizations, assumed rights and obligations provided by international treaties, and assumed the assets of the USSR.
Russia inherited the permanent seat of the USSR in the UN Security Council and inherited the permanent seat of the USSR in all other international organizations.
Russia continues to fulfill the international commitments of the USSR and continues to implement the international commitments of the USSR.
Russia assumed rights and obligations arising from international treaties.
Russia plays an important role in maintaining international peace and security.
Russia claims to be a major power and has ambitions of becoming a potential superpower.
In recent years, Russia has been characterized by world leaders, scholars, commentators, and politicians as an emerging superpower.
The characterization of Russia as an emerging superpower has been contested.
The geopolitical condition of Russia has been widely debated, and the debate focuses on unipolar and multipolar viewpoints in the global political system.

== Diplomatic structure and policy ==

The President of Russia represents the country in diplomatic meetings.
Russia has a multifaceted foreign policy that is determined and established by the President and implemented by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Russia.
In 2009, the country had 144 embassies.

== United Nations and global organizations ==

Russia became the 39th member state of the Council of Europe in 1996 and ratified the European Convention on Human Rights in 1998.
Russia initiated the procedure to withdraw from the Council of Europe on March 15, 2022.
The country participates in the Madrid Quartet and the Six-Party Talks with North Korea.
Russia is an active partner of ASEAN and a guest of the Non-Aligned Movement.
The main goals of the group include reforming the United Nations.

== Relations with the European Union ==

President Vladimir Putin advocated for a strategic partnership with the European Union and for close integration in various dimensions, including the creation of common spaces.
The legal basis for relations between Russia and the EU is the Partnership and Cooperation Agreement, which entered into force in 1997 and was renewed in May 2003.[1920,3142,1921] This agreement emphasizes mutual respect between the parties and recalls commitment to democracy, human rights, political and economic freedoms, and international peace and security.[1920,1921] In May 2003, the EU and Russia agreed on a framework based on shared values and interests that aimed to strengthen cooperation.[3142,4201] President Vladimir Putin advocated for a strategic partnership that included the creation of an EU-Russia Common Space and close integration in various dimensions.[4164,4165,4166,4167,4168] The partnership included the establishment of four common spaces between Russia and the EU.
Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated that Russia needs to build a 'modernization alliance' with European countries.

The purpose of this alliance is to acquire necessary technologies, and Lavrov stated that Russia needs to find opportunities to exploit the technological potential of the United States, which caused the United States to be extremely wary.
Russia considers Germany, France, Italy, and Spain to be its closest partners in Europe.

== Relations with NATO ==

The relationship between Russia and NATO has been volatile and is unstable.[18,1609] The NATO-Russia Council was established in 2002.[18,1609] The council was created to allow the alliance's 26 members and Russia to work together as equal partners.
The purpose of the council is to leverage opportunities for joint collaboration.
The organization was established in 2002.[18,1609] The organization allows the United States, Russia, and 27 NATO allies to collaborate.[18,1609] The purpose of the collaboration is to exploit opportunities for joint action.[18,1609] The council was formed to work together as equal partners.
The council was formed to track opportunities for joint cooperation.
The establishment required the approval of the United States, Russia, and 27 NATO allies.
General Philip Breedlove is the Supreme Allied Commander of NATO forces in Europe.[4291,4292] Due to Russia's occupation of Crimea, the alliance no longer considers Russia a partner.[4291,4292] The council allowed 26 Allied nations and Russia to work together as equal partners.[18,1609]

== Eurasian integration ==

Russia is a member of the Eurasian Economic Community (EurAsEC).
Russia is one of the five members of the Eurasian Economic Union, alongside Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan.
Russia maintains positive relations with other SCO member countries and other BRICS member countries.

== Relations with the West ==

Initially, after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, Russia developed a friendly relationship with Western nations.
Later, Russia's relationship with the Euro-Atlantic world deteriorated significantly.
This deterioration was caused by multiple conflicts.
A significant aspect of Russia's relations with the West is criticism from Western governments and global media.

== Territorial disputes ==

Most border disputes inherited from the Soviet Union were resolved.
The dispute concerns the southern part of the Kuril Islands, and the total area of the disputed southern part of the Kuril Islands is 5,175 square kilometers.
Japan made the return of the islands a condition for signing a peace treaty with the USSR, and a peace treaty between Japan and the USSR has not been signed to this day.
The sovereignty of the village of Aigba is a dispute, and the area surrounding the village of Aigba is also disputed.
The total area of the village and surrounding lands is approximately 160 square kilometers, and the disputed territory is located on the Russian-Abkhazian border.
The Soviet parliament did not ratify the 1990 Soviet-American agreement on the border with the USA in the Bering Sea, and the Russian parliament has also not ratified this agreement.
Western countries recognized the sovereignty of Kosovo.

== Arctic claims ==

The dispute involves claims in the Arctic, where Russia, Canada, the United States, Norway, and Denmark are making claims in the oil-rich Arctic.
Russia has been insisting since 2001 and is addressing the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf.
Russia is requesting an expansion of its exclusive economic zone in the Arctic Ocean based on geographical shelf research results.

== Kaliningrad corridor dispute ==

Russia proposed the creation of an international corridor intended to connect Belarus with the Kaliningrad Oblast and planned to pass through the territory of Lithuania.
The proposal was controversial.
The dispute was partially eased by the partial abolition of visa requirements for Russian citizens, a measure known as borderless border movement that allows Russians to move freely from the Kaliningrad Oblast to Belarus and Russia.

== Baltic minority issues ==

There is a dispute between Estonia, Latvia, and Russia regarding the discrimination of the Russian minority in the Baltic republics.
The Russian government is seeking to improve the situation for Russians who lost most of their civil rights in Latvia and Estonia after 1991.

== Post-Soviet conflicts ==

Russia supported separatist movements in other former Soviet republics, including conflicts in Abkhazia and South Ossetia in Georgia, Nagorno-Karabakh in Azerbaijan, and Transnistria in Moldova.

== Military intervention in Syria ==

The military intervention took place in September 2015 and was conducted at the request of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad [2912,2913,2914].
The operation consisted of airstrikes against groups opposing Bashar al-Assad's totalitarian regime, with targets including Islamic State militants, Front al-Nusra (al-Qaeda in the Levant) militants, Kurdish groups, and anti-Assad Syrian rebel groups [2912,2913,2914].
The target of the operation is the Islamic State and includes opposition groups attempting to overthrow the Syrian government by force [2912,2913,2914].
Government forces are accused of committing crimes against humanity, and the armed opposition is accused of committing crimes against humanity [2912,2913,2914].
The operation is conducted using a Russian naval base in the Syrian port of Tartus, which has existed since the 1980s, and a newly established Russian Air and Space Force base located on the territory of the Latakia airport in Syria.
Russia is a partner in ASEAN talks.

== Relations with China and economic pivot ==

The article stated that Russia began shifting its economy towards China as a response to increasing financial tensions following the annexation of Crimea and Western economic sanctions.
President Putin visited Shanghai for a two-day trip in May 2014, during which he signed a contract on behalf of Gazprom stipulating that the Russian energy giant would supply China with natural gas.
The contract agreed to an annual supply volume of 38 billion cubic meters, included an agreement to build a pipeline, and set Russia's contribution to the project cost at $55 billion while China agreed to contribute $22 billion.
Putin described the project as the largest construction project for the next four years, with natural gas deliveries scheduled to begin between 2018 and 2020 under a 30-year supply contract for which China agreed to pay $400 billion.
China is one of those countries, and Russia's relationship with China has been good for a long time due to growing trade between the two states.

== Relations with the European Union and Western nations ==

The European Union, the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom are among these countries.
Russia has a partnership and cooperation agreement regarding trade with the EU that came into force in 1995.
Restrictions on Russian exports to the EU were lifted.
Trade with the EU accounted for more than half of Russia's total foreign trade in 2012.
Russia's relationship with the EU was relatively good for a long time, with the Council of the Baltic Sea States serving as an example of such a regional cooperation organization.
Russia's actions created concern, dissatisfaction, and protests from large parts of the world, with the primary critics being the Western world.
This deterioration was caused by Russia's decision in February 2022 to expand its use of military power against Ukraine.
The Prime Minister of Sweden made a statement regarding the invasion, stating that it was unprovoked, illegal, and indefensible.
Russia's actions were called 'geopolitical terrorism' by Charles Michel, the President of the European Council.

Relations between Russia and the Western world, specifically the United States, the European Union, and NATO, collapsed after decades of instability.

== Relations with former Soviet states and the GUAM group ==

Ukraine and Kazakhstan share land and partially maritime borders with Russia, while Russia has exclusively land borders with Latvia, Belarus, and South Ossetia.
The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) was created in the former Soviet Union space with Russia's leading role.
Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan were founding members of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) in 2014, an international economic integration union created based on the Customs Union EurAsEC that began functioning on January 1, 2015.
The country has since then restored economic ties with many former Soviet republics, and the Eurasian Economic Union emerged as part of this process.
Russia has strained relations with several other former Soviet republics, which led to the formation of the GUAM cooperation involving Georgia, Ukraine, Azerbaijan, and Moldova.
All four countries have been directly or indirectly involved in military conflicts with Russia in recent years.
Several former members of the Soviet Union approached the West and NATO after the dissolution of the union, an approach Russia considered undesirable.

The CIS was established in 1992.

== Relations with specific non-aligned and neighboring states ==

Russia has exclusively land borders with China and Mongolia.
Russia does not have diplomatic relations with Georgia, Ukraine, Micronesia, Bhutan, or the Solomon Islands.
Russia has not had diplomatic relations with Georgia since 2008 and has not had diplomatic relations with Ukraine and Micronesia since 2022.
China and Japan are among these countries.
Slovenia-Russia economic exchange grew in 2022 despite sanctions due to the Russia-Ukraine war.
Turkey and Russia have joint defense strategies.

== International sanctions and economic consequences ==

Russia has been subjected to a greater number of international sanctions since 2014, with the increase being particularly significant after 2022 due to Russia's aggression against Ukraine.
Trade sanctions were imposed by a large number of countries, a number of Russian banks were excluded from the international payment system SWIFT, the assets of the Russian Central Bank were frozen abroad, and the foreign assets of a number of individuals believed to be close to the Putin regime were frozen.
Entities were banned from participating in various sporting competitions and international cultural events.
Civil society distanced itself from Russia, and Russia's participation in exchanges with these entities was significantly reduced.

== Countries abstaining from sanctions ==

Several countries abstained from participating in sanctions against Russia, including Brazil, India, China, and Mexico.
Some countries have not joined the sanctions and have not condemned the war.
India is one of those countries.
Three of these countries participate in the BRICS cooperation along with Russia.
BRICS is an economic cooperation organization that gathers large economies outside the G7 cooperation.

== Military interventions and foreign policy implementation ==

Russia's foreign policy is determined by the country's president and implemented by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Russia.
Putin strengthened Russia's influence abroad.
The country engaged in the civil war in Syria from 2015 and supported the Assad regime.
Russia's engagement in Syria began in 2015.

== Visa regimes and passport strength ==

A Russian passport holder can enter 76 countries without a visa and obtain a visa upon arrival in 32 countries.
Russia establishes visa regimes with countries worldwide based on reciprocity.
Relations between Russia and Ukraine collapsed after decades of instability.

== Legal status and international representation ==

Russia continues to implement the international commitments of the USSR, has assumed the permanent membership of the USSR in the UN Security Council, has assumed the membership of the USSR in other international organizations, and has assumed the rights and obligations of the USSR under international treaties.
As of 2009, Russia had diplomatic relations with 191 countries and 144 embassies.
Russia is a member of the G8 industrialized countries.
Russia became the 39th member of the Council of Europe in 1996.
Russia ratified the European Convention on Human Rights in 1998.
Russia is an observer member of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.
Russia is a member of the G8.
The Eurasian Economic Community (EurAsEC) is a regional organization.

== Foreign policy structure and geopolitical status ==

Foreign policy is determined by the President and conducted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.[1908,4197] Russia's geopolitical status is often a subject of debate concerning Russia's role in the global political system and involving perspectives on unipolarity and multipolarity.[344,346,348,349,350,352,355,1910,1912,1913,3052,4198,4199,4200] In recent years, Russia has been evaluated as a potential superpower by various world leaders, academics, commentators, and politicians.[344,346,348,349,350,352,355,1910,1912,1913,3052,4198,4199,4200] In recent years, some world leaders, scholars, commentators, and politicians have viewed Russia as a recovering superpower or a potential superpower, and these groups view Russia as lagging behind China.[348,352,353,757,1910,1912,1914]

== Relations with China and India ==

Russia maintains strong and positive relations with other BRICS countries.
There are comprehensive defense relations between Russia and India.
A Friendship Treaty was signed with the People's Republic of China.
The Russia-China alliance operates based on the principle of common interests.
Russia is a useful source of oil and gas for China.
This source is less important to China than the Gulf region.
This source is less important to China than Africa.

== Post-Soviet conflicts and frozen conflicts ==

The South Ossetia War is a reason for the strain in relations.
Russia was involved in the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict between Azerbaijan and Armenia starting in 1992, the Transnistria conflict in Moldova in 1992, and the South Ossetia civil war in Georgia from 1991 to 1993.
Russia uses a mechanism to create a 'frozen conflict' zone, and the purpose of this mechanism is to prevent any country in Eastern Europe from getting closer to the West.
Public display of the symbol to support Russian military actions is banned in certain regions of Germany.
Russia lost influence in Georgia due to the Rose Revolution, in Ukraine due to the Orange Revolution, and in Kyrgyzstan due to the Tulip Revolution.

== Deterioration of relations and sanctions ==

The 2014 Crimea crisis is a reason for the strain in relations.
The European Parliament recognized Russia as a state sponsor of terrorism.
The parliaments of Ukraine, Slovakia, Lithuania, and Latvia recognized Russia as a terrorist state.
Russia blocked a UN Security Council resolution project regarding Syria, and China blocked the same resolution project alongside Russia.
The resolution project threatened sanctions.
Public display of the symbol to support Russian military actions is banned in Estonia, Ukraine, Moldova, Lithuania, and Latvia.
The sanctions were imposed due to Russia's intervention in the Ukraine crisis.
Russian military and aerospace enterprises had to plan to switch to new partners.
These companies purchased electronic components from China.
Former President Vladimir Putin supported a strategic partnership.
Russia and the West frequently have disagreements.

== Multilateral organizations and global status ==

Russia is one of the world's eight major industrialized nations and was a founding member of the Eurasian Economic Union.
Most former Soviet member states agreed to become early members of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
Russia was suspended from this group in 2014 due to Russia's annexation of Crimea.
Member states have not mentioned the CIS agreement for several years, and the international community has not mentioned the CIS agreement for several years.
This commitment has faded significantly over time, and the agreement has not been mentioned for nearly a decade.
This lack of mention is due to political realities.
This suppression led to deteriorated relations between Russia and several neighboring countries.
The total value of these purchases was in the billions of US dollars.
This cooperation represents the first step in forming a national BRICS technology alliance.

The Russian Armed Forces are divided into the Ground Forces, the Navy, and the Aerospace Forces—and there are also two independent arms of service: the Strategic Missile Troops and the Airborne Troops.
, the military have around a million active-duty personnel, which is the world's fifth-largest, and about 2–20 million reserve personnel.
It is mandatory for all male citizens aged 18–27 to be drafted for a year of service in the Armed Forces.

Russia is among the five recognised nuclear-weapons states, with the world's largest stockpile of nuclear weapons; over half of the world's nuclear weapons are owned by Russia.
Russia possesses the second-largest fleet of ballistic missile submarines, and is one of the only three countries operating strategic bombers.
Russia maintains the world's third-highest military expenditure, spending $109 billion in 2023, corresponding to around 5.9% of its GDP.
In 2021 it was the world's second-largest arms exporter, and had a large and entirely indigenous defence industry, producing most of its own military equipment.

== Structure and Personnel ==

The Russian military consists of the air force and includes the air and space defense branch.
In 2006, the military had 1.03 million members in active service, which was also recorded as 1,037,000 active personnel.
That year, the Russian military was the fourth largest in the world by number of trained personnel.
The Soviet Armed Forces were succeeded by the Russian Armed Forces, and the number of troops was significantly reduced.
The conscription system is similar to that of the Soviet Union, and the conscription period was shortened starting in 2008 due to various problems.
Conscript soldiers were expected to make up 70% of the army by 2010.
Specnaz is a general term for a range of different units that are special purpose units of the Russian Army and part of the Russian Armed Forces and security forces.
The training of Specnaz units is among the most demanding in the world.
Russia's paramilitary organizations include the National Guard, the Border Guard, the Civil Defense Forces, and the Federal Protective Service.

The arsenal of weapons was significantly reduced.
The Russian Federation Armed Forces are organized under a unified command system.
The country adopted a conscription system on January 1, 2009.
Putin declared that conscripts would not be deployed to combat units.
The Constitution guarantees conscientious objection to military service and allows for alternative service if religious beliefs conflict with military duty.
Russia accelerated defense reforms after the war with Georgia.

== Nuclear Arsenal and Strategic Forces ==

Russia possesses the largest stockpile of weapons of mass destruction in the world and inherited most of the former Soviet Union's weapons.
These forces possess intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) that are equipped with nuclear warheads and include both fixed and mobile variants.
Russia has the strategic nuclear missile submarine Yuri Dolgorukiy and the nuclear missile submarine Dmitry Donskoy.
The Russian Navy includes nine nuclear ballistic missile submarines.

== Defense Spending and Industry ==

Defense spending has quadrupled over the last six years.
The government's official military spending in 2008 was $40 billion, while several sources, including US Intelligence and the International Institute for Strategic Studies, estimate the military spending to be much higher than the official figure.[28,29,30,31,32,33,34] This rivalry is reflected in rising defense expenditures.
Russian military spending increased by 5.4 percent in 2016, with the estimated value of this budget being $58 billion.[32,33,378] Russia is currently upgrading its military equipment, a process that took place between 2006 and 2015 with a value of approximately $200 billion.[35,36,379]

== Arms Exports ==

Since 2001, the country has been the largest supplier of weapons [23,24,25,26].
Since 2001, Russia's arms exports account for approximately 30% of the global arms trade and are exported to about 80 countries [23,375,376,377].
Russia accounts for approximately one-quarter of the global arms trade [679,680].

== Ground Forces and Equipment ==

Russia possesses the world's largest tank arsenal and the largest tank force in the world.
The T-34 is a famous Russian tank and was the best tank design in World War II.
The T-54 and T-55 are famous Russian tanks.
The AK-47 and AK-74 rifles were designed by Mikhail Kalashnikov.
AK-pattern rifles are the most widely used assault rifles in the world, and more have been manufactured than all other types of assault rifles combined.

== Air Defense Systems ==

Modern Russian air defense systems are significantly advanced compared to foreign equivalents and include the S-300 and S-400 missile groups.
The S-400 missile group has entered service with the Russian military and its tactical technical specifications surpass those of American Patriot systems.

== Aircraft and Aviation ==

Russia is a leading country in aircraft manufacturing and has one of the largest air forces in the world.[464,465,466,467] Russia is the only country besides the United States that possesses a modern strategic bomber.[22,372,373,374] Russia owns the Mil Mi-24 helicopter, the Mil Mi-26 helicopter, the Su-34 fighter-bomber, the MiG-31 interceptor fighter, the Su-24 bomber, the A-50 long-range early warning aircraft, the Tupolev Tu-160 (White Swan) strategic bomber, and the MiG-35 fighter jet.[464,465,466,467] The MiG-35 is a fourth-generation++ fighter.[464,465,466,467] Russia possesses the Su-33 fighter jet, which is a naval fighter aircraft.
The Russian Air Force uses multirole fourth-generation fighter aircraft, including the Suchoj Su-27, the Suchoj Su-30, the Suchoj Su-35S, the MiG-29, and the MiG-31.

The Russian Air Force operates Suchoj Su-25 attack aircraft, Suchoj Su-24 fighter-bombers, Suchoj Su-34 fighter-bombers, Tupolev Tu-22M bombers, Tupolev Tu-95 bombers, Tupolev Tu-160 bombers, and hundreds of transport aircraft.

== Naval Forces and Fleet Composition ==

Russia has one of the largest navies in the world.
Russia owns frigates and destroyers, including the frigate Admiral Gorshkov, which is used for military operations in near and distant sea areas and in global ocean waters.
The Pyotr Velikiy is a heavy nuclear cruiser considered one of the largest and newest warships in the Russian Navy and is the most powerful non-aircraft carrier warship in the world.
Project 21956 destroyers will be the future of the Russian Navy fleet and must replace Project Sovremenny destroyers.
Russia has the Russian nuclear silent submarine Severodvinsk, which is quieter than the American multi-purpose nuclear submarine Seawolf.
Russia possesses the heavy aircraft carrier Admiral Kuznetsov, which is designed to destroy major naval targets and to protect friendly naval formations from potential enemy attacks.
The Russian Navy includes the Northern Fleet, the Pacific Fleet, the Black Sea Fleet, and the Baltic Fleet.

The Russian Navy includes the Caspian Fleet, Naval Aviation, and Coastal Forces.
The Northern Fleet is the strongest fleet.
The Russian Navy uses one aircraft carrier named Admiral Kuznetsov and five cruisers.
The cruiser Pyotr Velikiy belongs to the Kirov class and has a nuclear power plant.
The Russian Navy includes fourteen destroyers, six frigates, sixty-four corvettes, and dozens of attack submarines.

== Inherited Soviet Assets ==

Russia inherited the former Soviet Union's spy satellites, weapon factories, and military bases.
Some of these inherited military bases are now located outside Russia's borders in former Soviet republics.
Russia's nuclear arsenal is estimated at approximately 16,000 warheads.
Russia has a strong position in the market for naval anti-aircraft systems.

== Armed Forces Structure and Personnel ==

The Russian Air Force operates attack helicopters from the Mil and Kamov manufacturers.
The Sukhoi Su-57 is a fifth-generation fighter jet that made its first flight in January 2010, with first deliveries to the army scheduled for 2019.
As of 2022, 10 Su-57 aircraft were in the testing phase and 5 Su-57 aircraft were in series production.
Russia produces tanks, aircraft, and ballistic missiles.
The main Russian naval ports include Vladivostok.
In 2023, Global Firepower ranked the country second militarily, while the United States ranked first in military power.
Practical military instruction, which existed previously in the Soviet Union, was introduced in September 2023 in all state schools.
The Youth Army Junarmija was founded in 2016, is subordinate to the Russian Ministry of Defense, and grew to have over one million members within a few years.
The President appoints and dismisses the High Command of the Armed Forces.

== Nuclear Capabilities ==

According to the SIPRI Institute, the country possesses the largest number of nuclear warheads among all states and has a total of 4,489 nuclear warheads, of which only 1,674 are operational.

== Defense Industry and Exports ==

The Russian arms industry accounts for approximately one-quarter of the global arms trade [679,680].
Russia's defense industry is coordinated by Rosoboronexport, a state-owned defense exporter that coordinates the work of various defense companies and consolidates them into a conglomerate through shareholdings.
Russia inherited weapons industry production facilities located outside the Soviet Union's borders from the Soviet Union.
Russia's arms exports increased by 37 percent compared to the period from 2005 to 2009.
Russia supplied weapons to 56 countries.
The Russian aircraft industry offers a portfolio of internationally competitive military aircraft, including the MiG-29 and Su-30 [2307,2308].
Aircraft products account for more than half of the country's weapon exports [2309,2310].
Russia has a military-industrial complex based on the Soviet era.
Su-27 and similar manufactured weapons are sold by state-owned enterprises acting as agents, and these weapons have achieved significant success in exports.
The defense industry has been important for Russia since the Soviet era.
Russia plans to continue actively expanding its exports in the future.
Export volume exceeded 10 billion dollars in 2011 and was projected to exceed 15 billion dollars in 2012.

The trend of export growth has been steady, though exports may be halted due to political reasons.
The defense industry is expected to continue expanding as Russia is included in the global increase of military spending.
Russia spent $65.1 billion in 2019, when it was the third largest arms exporter in the world.
The United States and China ranked higher than Russia in arms exports in 2019.

== Intelligence and Security Agencies ==

The FSB is the domestic intelligence service and the largest of the Russian intelligence agencies [cite: 981][cite: 1108].
The FSB does not oversee foreign espionage or the Federal Protective Service [cite: 981].
The FSB's main tasks include state protection, domestic espionage, combating organized crime, and border service [cite: 981].
The FSB is responsible for the National Counter-Terrorism Center, possesses investigative authority powers, and operates its own prisons [cite: 981].
The FSB is primarily responsible for counter-terrorism [cite: 1112].
FSB reports have influence [cite: 1108].
Foreign policy analysis is typically the domain of the SWR and GRU agencies, which struggle to get their assessments to the President [cite: 1108].
After the collapse of the USSR, the FSB remained responsible for the territories of former Soviet republics and is not solely an internal security service [cite: 1109].
The service has good connections to the Ministry of the Interior [cite: 1112].
The National Guard was established [cite: 1112].
The FSB is led by Alexander Bortnikov [cite: 20].

The FSB has the special units ALFA and Vympel.
The Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation (FSO) is an intelligence agency whose primary mission is the security of the Russian President and the Russian government.
The FSO commands the Kremlin Regiment and has 20,000 personnel [cite: 1108].
According to Mark Galeotti, the FSO has gained an opaque role as a watcher of other intelligence agencies and conducts its own public opinion polls [cite: 1108].
The FSO prepares forecasts and analyses on national security for the President, and these additional competencies place the FSO in a competitive situation against the FSB [cite: 981].
The Sluzhba vneshnei razvedki (SWR) is also known as SVR and is the foreign intelligence service of the Russian Federation.
The Foreign Intelligence Service of the Russian Federation is a civil foreign intelligence agency that has 15,000 or more employees [cite: 1113].
The organization has a special unit called Saslon, which is responsible for protecting Russian diplomatic missions [cite: 1113].
The organization places great value on HUMINT and employs extensively installed long-term agents for this purpose [cite: 1113].
The agency is traditionally led by career civil servants with external experience rather than long-serving intelligence officers, and Sergei Naryschkin currently leads the agency [cite: 1113].
The Glavnoye Razvedyvatelnoye Upravleniye is known as the GRU.

The Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) is the military intelligence service of the Russian military and is a department of the Russian General Staff.
The service has its own Spetsnaz units.
The GRU is responsible for counter-espionage, similar to the FSB, and conducts foreign espionage, similar to the SWR.
The Federal Security Service (FSB) and the Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) currently play a role in domestic counter-espionage and intelligence organizations.
The FSB and SVR also serve as law enforcement organizations.
Their roles include defending against cyberattacks.
The Federal Protective Service exists.
The Main Staff General Directorate for Intelligence (GRU) exists.
The Main Staff Military Topography Department exists.

== National Guard ==

The National Guard of Russia is a gendarmerie founded in 2016 as the successor to the Internal Troops of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
The National Guard is directly subordinate to the President of the Russian Federation.
The National Guard's duties include protecting public order, fighting crime, combating extremism, and combating terrorism.
Competencies in counter-terrorism were transferred to the National Guard.
The National Guard participates in territorial defense.
The National Guard took over the SOBR units of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
Viktor Solotow has commanded the National Guard since its founding and is considered an ally of Vladimir Putin.
The National Guard is an important domestic political power instrument.
A National Guard was created that is directly subordinate to Putin.
The creation of this National Guard reduced the weight of the regular military.
The creation of praetorian military institutions like the National Guard is a classic maneuver.

The National Guard participates in border protection and protects critical state infrastructures.
According to the CIA World Factbook, the National Guard has an estimated strength of over 350,000 personnel, while the Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA) estimated in 2022 that the National Guard has units of approximately 60,000 to 70,000 soldiers.
The National Guard possesses armored personnel carriers, transport aircraft, helicopters, and artillery guns.
Following the failed uprising of Yevgeny Prigozhin and his Wagner group, the National Guard is expected to receive additional heavy main battle tanks.
Chechen units known as the Kadyrovtsy were integrated into the National Guard and are still commanded by Ramzan Kadyrov.

== Border and Coast Guard ==

The Border Troops of Russia are the armed forces responsible for border protection, are not part of the Russian Armed Forces, are deployed to fulfill special tasks in the field of national defense, and are subordinate to the FSB.
The Russian Coast Guard is part of the Border Troops.
The estimated personnel strength of the FSB Border Troops was 170,000.

== Wagner Group ==

The Wagner Group is a paramilitary unit founded in 2014 that is connected to the structures of the Russian state and operates in close proximity to the Russian state, contrary to the legal ban on mercenary companies.
The Russian government did not have to publicly take responsibility for the Wagner Group's actions, and the group has a close relationship with the Russian military intelligence agency.
Dmitri Utkin was the military commander of the Wagner Group and was originally a lieutenant colonel in the GRU military intelligence agency.
The Wagner Group shared its training grounds with Russian military units from the beginning, and one of the Russian military units that shared the training ground belonged to the GRU.
Leaders of the underworld joined the mercenary company Wagner, and many prisoners were offered the opportunity to serve military service for a limited time.
Wagner can be characterized as a semi-state actor that operates with a deliberately unclear legal status, while Wagner personnel continue to identify themselves with the Russian state.

== Private Military Companies and Paramilitary Groups ==

Wagner represents the privatization of state functions, a combination of oligarchic and state interests of Russia, a competitor to established structures, and actions that contradict centralized control.
Jewgeni Prigoschin was the owner of the Wagner group, which the Russian state allowed to recruit volunteers in Russian prisons who were promised generous pay, benefits for their families in case of death, and pardons for fighting in or against Ukraine.
The Wagner group fought relatively independently and temporarily consisted of an estimated 50,000 fighters, 40,000 of whom were prisoners.
Russia allowed the generation of additional fighters without needing to rely on the general population.
In 2023, Defense Minister Shoigu attempted to bind the group more closely to his ministry through a contract, while Wagner's role as a combat unit in Ukraine demonstrated its closeness to the state.
The group staged a coup to prevent stronger integration into the command chain of the Ministry of Defense.
The future of the group is uncertain following a failed uprising and the death of the group's most important leaders.

These military companies operate with the tolerance or support of the Russian state.
The Ukrainian OSINT organization molfar counts 37 different PMCs, and there are other military companies of various sizes besides Wagner, some of which have already been disbanded.
Owners of these military companies can be firms like Gazprom, which is believed to control two such units, or politicians such as Sergei Aksyonow, the Governor of Crimea, who owns the group Convoy that operates in Kherson.
The group Wagner denied any connection to the state for many years, but Putin admitted that he had financed the Wagner Group since its founding and stated that the Russian state paid the group 86 billion rubles from May 2022 to May 2023.
The Russian state under Putin is trying to preserve the group's combat power and continue the group under new commanders.
Defense Minister Shoigu is associated with militias including the Patriot group.
The Redut group is associated with oligarch Gennadi Timchenko, and it was suggested that the Redut group would succeed Wagner.

The British Ministry of Defence estimates that Wagner will be integrated into the Russian National Guard, a statement also made by Anton Yelizarov, the new commander of Wagner.
On December 25, 2023, Putin granted permission to the National Guard to recruit volunteer groups that would operate with contracts limited to several months, a practice previously used by Wagner to recruit volunteer groups with similar time-limited contracts.
Wagner's African activities were placed under the control of the Russian military intelligence agency GRU.
Military companies operate for Russian institutions and companies, including a private military company called PMC Espanola that is intended to work for and is funded by the Kremlin party United Russia.
PMC Espanola was involved in the capture of Avdiivka.

== Nuclear Doctrine and Strategy ==

President Putin signed Decree 683, which introduced a new military doctrine that came into effect on December 31, 2015.
The new military doctrine identified the United States, NATO allies, and the European Union as threats to Russia and its neighbors, marking the first time these entities were named as threats in Russian military doctrine.
In March 2018, President Putin dedicated one-third of his address to the nation to the presentation of allegedly invincible nuclear weapons.
The US Department of Defense and various Western scientists and analysts speculate that Russian nuclear strategy involves limited nuclear strikes in Europe if a military conflict occurs in Eastern Europe.
This strategy is based on the assumption that the USA would not be ready for a comprehensive similar response and involves limited nuclear escalation with the goal of subsequently de-escalating.
The development and deployment of new tactical nuclear weapons, including their deployment in Kaliningrad, as well as the integration of simulated nuclear strikes into large-scale conventional military maneuvers, indicate this strategy.

Russian military forces conduct large-scale conventional maneuvers that include simulated nuclear strikes.
Nuclear weapons are no longer solely a means of deterring attackers and now serve as a shield for imperial expansion.
The planned relocation of nuclear weapons to Belarus is interpreted as a signal to the West, particularly directed at Poland.
This approach contradicts what Russia previously published about its nuclear doctrines.

== Military Districts and Command Structure ==

Russia is divided into five military districts that are subordinate to United Strategic Commands of the same name.
In addition to the ground forces, the OSKs command the naval and air forces stationed in their respective territories.
The army is the dominant element in the military districts, a fact that applies to all military districts except the Northern Military District.
The Northern Military District covers Northwest Russia, the Arctic beyond the Arctic Circle, and Chukotka, with the Northern Fleet serving as its core.
The Western Military District covers West and Central Russia, including Kaliningrad, the Baltic region, and the Baltic Fleet.
The Southern Military District covers South Russia and the North Caucasus, includes the Crimean Peninsula in its area of responsibility, and contains the Black Sea Fleet and the Caspian Flotilla.
The Central Military District covers Volga-Ural and Western Siberia, where Western Siberia extends westward to Lake Baikal.
The Eastern Military District covers the Russian Far East and the eastern part of Siberia.

The Eastern Military District includes the Pacific Fleet and has its headquarters in Khabarovsk.

== Conscription and Personnel Demographics ==

Conscription was limited to able-bodied men, and the Russian Duma passed a law in 2023 increasing the mandatory military service age to 30 years to meet the need for soldiers in the war against Ukraine.
In 2007, the mandatory service age was reduced from 24 to 18 years, and in 2008, the duration of mandatory service was shortened to 12 months.
Conscript soldiers were previously deployed in conflict zones such as Chechnya, where abuse of young recruits by superiors occurred frequently within the context of Dedovshchina.
There is recurring criticism of conscription among the population, which is particularly driven by the mothers of conscripts.
Ethnic and religious differences play a significant and increasing role within the military.
Fifteen percent of all soldiers are Muslims, who do not hold positions in higher ranks, while 90% of personnel in higher positions are ethnic Russians or Ukrainians.
Ethnic Russian units are materially favored over units from minorities, and there is a strong emphasis on the Orthodox confession, which is linked to the Russian nation within the military.

== Budget and Expenditure ==

Military spending has been increasing significantly for several years.
Russia spent $61.4 billion on its military in 2018, while the United States spent $649 billion, China spent $250 billion, Saudi Arabia spent $67.6 billion, India spent $66.5 billion, and France spent $63.8 billion.
Germany followed the United Kingdom in the ranking.
Russia's military spending increased massively starting in 2000 and doubled between 2004 and 2014.
Russia aimed to allocate one-fifth of its total state budget to the military starting in 2014.
Russia ranked third in military spending in 2022, with the United States and China having higher military spending than Russia that year.
Russia spent 4% of its GDP on the military in 2022.
Expenditures related to the war in Ukraine are continuing to rise and have reached at least 5% of GDP.
Actual expenditures may be higher than officially stated figures.
The defense budget increased by 40% compared to 2021, an increase observed by 2023.

In 2022, 24% of all state expenditures were allocated to the military and security services, a share that is increasing and projected to reach 33%.
The Russian leadership plans to spend 6% of its GDP on military purposes in 2024, whereas in 2005 the share of government spending from GDP for the military was 3.9%.[883,1229]

== Personnel Strength and Composition ==

Information regarding military personnel numbers is largely unclear.
As of February 2022, the armed forces had approximately 850,000 personnel, with 300,000 assigned to the Army, 40,000 to the Airborne Troops, 150,000 to the Navy, 160,000 to the Air Force, 70,000 to the Strategic Rocket Forces, 20,000 to Special Forces, and 100,000 additional soldiers assigned to staff duties, cyber operations, support, and logistics.
The National Guard has an estimated strength of at least 350,000 personnel, and some units of the National Guard are capable of military use.
Members of the Wagner Group can be counted as part of Russia's military personnel, and similar semi-state militias can be counted as part of Russia's military personnel.
Volunteer battalions were created to be raised by governors in the regions, where military experience was not required, the pay was significantly higher than for regular soldiers and conscripts, and the allowed recruitment age was significantly higher than for regular soldiers and conscripts.[1156,1157,1158,1159] The maximum recruitment age was 50 years, and in special cases, the maximum recruitment age could be up to 60 years.[1156,1157,1158,1159]

In August 2022, President Putin issued a decree ordering an increase in the army size by 137,000 soldiers to reach a total of 1.15 million soldiers, with the expansion scheduled to take effect starting in 2023.
In 2023, it was announced that Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu should increase the personnel strength of the Russian military to 1.5 million soldiers based on an instruction by Putin.
A new army corps is to be established at the border with Finland, and twelve additional divisions are to be established.
Dmitri Peskov justified the expansion of the armed forces based on a 'proxy war' led by the West against Russia.
In late 2023, the Estonian Ministry of Defense estimated that Russia can currently train approximately 130,000 soldiers to combat readiness every six months, contingent on the course of the war allowing it.
The number of soldiers trained to combat readiness will decrease to 40,000 every six months, a reduction that would fall below a critical threshold for war success according to the Estonian Ministry of Defence.

== Nuclear Arsenal and Doctrine ==

As of January 2022, Russia has 5,977 nuclear warheads while the United States has 5,428 nuclear warheads.
In 2021, Russia possessed 6,255 nuclear warheads.
New missiles were announced in 2015.
The number of deployed nuclear warheads increased from 1,400 in 2013 to 1,796 in 2016.
This increase occurred compared to the entry into force of the New START treaty in 2011 and was due to newly commissioned submarines.
In 2023, Russia possessed 4,489 nuclear warheads.
According to the SIPRI Institute, Russia had the largest number of nuclear warheads in 2023.
Only 1,674 of these nuclear warheads were operational while the remaining nuclear warheads were stored away.
The Russian leadership repeatedly threatened the first use of nuclear weapons.
Groups close to the Russian leadership also made these threats.
The extent of Russia's readiness to use nuclear weapons is debated.

== Military Rankings and Capabilities ==

Global Firepower ranks Russia's military strength in 2023 as second, with the United States ranked first.
Russia has the second most powerful army in the world.
Russia has the first (largest) land force in the world.
Russia has the second most powerful air force in the world.
Russia has the second most powerful navy in the world.

== Internal Security and Civil Defense ==

The disaster relief ministry is organized militarily and is responsible for assistance during natural disasters, major accidents, and civil defense.
The ministry leads the fire department nationwide, which is organized into professional and volunteer units.
In 2019, there were 271,000 professional firefighters and 956,600 volunteer firefighters in Russia.
The firefighters operated out of 18,322 fire stations and firehouses that contained 22,735 fire engines and 1,326 turntables or telescopic masts.
262,354 children and adolescents are organized in youth fire brigades.
Russian fire departments were called to 1,161,581 incidents in the same year, 471,426 of which involved putting out fires, and the departments saved 9,461 injured people.
The basis for ensuring internal security in Russia is the association of Russian security agencies, whose leading body is the Security Council of Russia.
The security agencies association includes the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia, the Ministry of Emergency Situations of Russia, and intelligence services.

The Federal Security Service (FSB) is an intelligence service in Russia responsible for internal state security and the security of Russians living abroad.
The SVR is responsible for foreign intelligence.
The GRU is responsible for military intelligence.

== Command Structure and Organization ==

These forces included the branches of the Soviet military that were part of the Russian Federation Armed Forces, which also included force types such as strategic rocket forces, space forces, and air assault forces.
The command organ of the Armed Forces is the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation.

== Military Reforms ==

A military reform was initiated and led by former Defense Minister Anatoly Serdyukov.
The goals of the reform were to improve army organization and efficiency.
The main idea of the reform was to transform the army from a mass mobilization force to a professional military service force.
The new force would not have military districts, fronts, or armies and would adopt a brigade-level system common in the West.
Serdyukov started planning to reduce the personnel of the central administration by 30%.
He requested a radical reduction of the Russian officer corps, changing the ratio from one officer for every 2.5 soldiers before the reform to one officer for every 15 soldiers after the reform.
The reform resulted in the loss of 200,000 jobs.
The 'old guard' strongly opposed the reform.
The original deadline for the reductions was 2012, and the new deadline was 2016.
Serdyukov's main goals were to solve acute and long-term problems, including the inefficiency of Russia's defense industrial policy and the inefficiency of Russia's supply policy.

Violations of human rights in Russia have been increasingly reported by leading democracy and human rights groups.

The Russian government has been widely criticised by political dissidents and human rights activists for unfair elections, crackdowns on opposition political parties and protests, persecution of non-governmental organisations and enforced suppression and killings of independent journalists, and censorship of mass media and internet.

Muslims, especially Salafis, have faced persecution in Russia.
To quash the insurgency in the North Caucasus, Russian authorities have been accused of indiscriminate killings, arrests, forced disappearances, and torture of civilians.

Chechens and Ingush in Russian prisons reportedly take more abuse than other ethnic groups.
During the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Russia has set up filtration camps where many Ukrainians are subjected to abuses and forcibly sent to Russia; the camps have been compared to those used in the Chechen Wars.

== Political repression and suppression of dissent ==

Civil society in Russia has been silenced by Russian authorities, and civil society organizations have been shut down.

Attacks on opposition figures occur repeatedly, and arson attacks against the property of opposition figures occur repeatedly.
